_meta.description: Page manifest for the focal-4 HI viewer. Each entry corresponds to one HI page-side (left or right half of a 2-page PDF spread). The 'sequence' field is the navigation order in the viewer (left-to-right within a domain, then next domain). The 'book_page' is the printed page number visible at the bottom margin of the page.
_meta.scope: Whole-book expansion in progress: 398 pages, 162 domains (target 803 pages / 300 domains).

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第二 (鹿兒島)
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Satsuma / Kagoshima (鹿兒島藩): land assessment and fiscal totals
pages.page_topic: kokudaka and major fiscal aggregates
pages.page_summary_en: This is the land-and-fiscal page (fascicle 2) for the Satsuma domain, entered under its castle-town name Kagoshima (鹿兒島藩). It records a 草高 (assessed yield) of 869,594 koku, broken into 775,364 koku of productive land and 29,487 koku of loss-adjusted land, with 261,057 koku of current rice on hand (現石) — the totals explicitly exclude Ryūkyū tribute. Alongside the grain figures it lists Satsuma's signature trade goods, above all sugar (砂糖) at 5,092,825 units, along with paper mulberry (楮), raw wax (生蠟), and tea seed, plus a miscellaneous tax in copper coin (雜稅銭) of 159,796.

pages.page_topic: demographics — population, households, shizoku / ashigaru-and-below counts
pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第二 (高知) — 鹿兒島藩データ
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Satsuma / Kagoshima (鹿兒島藩): population and status classes
pages.page_summary_en: This page gives Satsuma's demographic register: a total population (人口) of 896,808 in 174,528 households (戸數), split into 469,468 men and 427,340 women. Of these, 43,119 households and 192,949 persons are 士族 (samurai households) — an unusually high roughly 22% share, reflecting Satsuma's rural-samurai (gōshi) system — while the 足輕以下 (foot-soldier-and-below class) accounts for 107,738 households and 579,405 people. A separate Ryūkyū sub-block records its tribute rice (8,669 koku) and its own households and population. The register is large enough that it runs on from the Satsuma leaf onto the adjacent Kōchi (Tosa) page.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八 (鹿児島)
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Satsuma / Kagoshima (鹿兒島藩): officials and military (undisclosed)
pages.page_topic: officers + military, with explicit non-disclosure annotation
pages.page_summary_en: In the officials-and-military volume (fascicle 8), Satsuma's entry is a blank: under the ○鹿兒島藩 domain-boundary marker the register carries only the phrase 書ナラス ("not disclosed"). The troop counts printed to the right of that marker — 1,568 rank-and-file, 1,106 officers, 464 corps members, and the councillor tallies — belong to the neighbouring Kanazawa domain that shares this leaf, not to Satsuma. Where nearly every other domain itemised its forces, Satsuma reported nothing, making it the most opaque military presence in the 1870 survey.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Chōshū / Yamaguchi (山口藩): land assessment and taxes
pages.page_topic: kokudaka components + combined high
pages.page_summary_en: This is the land-and-tax page (fascicle 5) for the Chōshū domain, entered under its capital Yamaguchi (山口藩). It records a 草高 (assessed yield) of 369,411 koku plus an 外高 (new-field uplift) of 618,593 koku, giving a 合高 (combined assessment) of 988,004 koku. The main land tax (正租) is stated as 206,910 koku of current rice (現米) together with 116,190 in copper coin, supplemented by a miscellaneous rice tax (雜稅米) of 14,553 koku and smaller taxes in silver and on wax and coal. Chōshū's population figures appear on the facing page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Chōshū / Yamaguchi (山口藩): households and status classes
pages.page_topic: status-class households + population (with M/F)
pages.page_summary_en: This page is Chōshū's status register (not a full commoner census), laid out in two horizontal bands. The upper band gives 17,714 households (戸數) and a population (人口) of 66,463, with status sub-counts including 3,000 士族 (samurai) households and 11,589 persons, 3,991 卒族 (lower-retainer) households and 10,362 persons, and 6,157 陪臣 (rear-vassals). The lower band records religious and outcaste groups — 1,165 Buddhist temples (寺院), 92 mountain ascetics (山伏), and 2,675 穢多 (outcaste-caste) households — each population figure carrying its own male/female split.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Chōshū / Yamaguchi (山口藩): senior officials
pages.page_topic: Chōshū (Yamaguchi) senior domain officials: governor and the three councillor ranks with named appointees
pages.page_summary_en: This is the opening (right-hand) page of Chōshū's entry in the officials-and-military volume (fascicle 9), marked by the ○山口藩 domain-boundary symbol. Read right to left, it names the domain's senior officialdom: one 知事 (governor), Mōri Motonori; two 大参事 (senior councillors); five 権大参事 (provisional senior councillors); and seven 少参事 (junior councillors), each rank listing its count and its named appointees. The small rifle-corps block of 80 men (銃隊) printed to the right of the ○山口藩 marker is a military overflow belonging to the preceding domain that shares this leaf, not to Chōshū. The junior-councillor list and the full military register continue onto the facing page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Chōshū / Yamaguchi (山口藩): army and navy
pages.page_topic: army + navy (17 battalions, 4 warships)
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries Chōshū's military register (fascicle 9), a striking contrast to Satsuma's blank entry. The land force is 17 infantry battalions (拾七大隊) of 433 men each — 7,361 infantry in all — with 6½ artillery batteries and one 93-man cavalry company. The navy is four wooden steam warships, each listed with its earlier foreign name: 第一丁卯丸 (ex-Penta), 第二丁卯丸 (ex-Asonda), 鳳翔丸, and 乙丑丸 (ex-Conchin). The domain-boundary marker and the senior officials are on the facing right half; the tail of the 権少参事 (provisional junior councillor) roster also appears here.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tosa / Kōchi (高知藩): land assessment, taxes, and products
pages.page_topic: kokudaka (5-yr avg) + tax + products + households
pages.page_summary_en: This is the land-and-fiscal page (fascicle 2) for the Tosa domain, entered under its castle-town name Kōchi (高知藩). It records a 草高 (assessed yield) of 495,486 koku, given as a five-year average spanning 1864–1868 (through the Boshin War), with current rice (現米) of 189,431 koku that combines with a further 3,587 koku to a grand total (總計) of 193,018 koku. It also gives the tax in gold and silver and a household count (戸數) of 93,736. A long 諸産物 (assorted products) list catalogues Tosa's named goods without quantities; the domain's population total is on the demographics page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tosa / Kōchi (高知藩): population, status classes, and army
pages.page_topic: population + status classes (with M/F) + standing army
pages.page_summary_en: This is Tosa's demographic page (fascicle 2), giving a total population (人口) of 495,936. The status classes each carry male/female sub-totals: 7,269 士族 (samurai) households and 30,506 persons; 3,073 卒族 (lower-retainer) households and 17,681 persons; 3,396 穢多 (outcaste-caste) households and 16,894 persons; a Shinto-priest-and-ascetic class of 1,016 households and 4,214 persons; and 476 temples with 1,572 clergy. The page closes with Tosa's army: 6,600 standing troops (常備兵) and 2,400 emergency troops (非常兵), together 9,000 men.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — end of Tosa (山內藩) and opening of Kameoka (龜岡藩)
pages.page_topic: Tail of Tosa's demographic register (a small supplementary household/population block) ending at the ○山內藩 boundary marker, then the opening kokudaka/tax columns of the next domain, ○龜岡藩 (Kameoka).
pages.page_summary_en: This left half of leaf 155 (fascicle 2) spans a domain boundary. At its right edge the ○山內藩 marker closes the Tosa (Yamauchi) entry with a small supplementary block of just 602 households and about 2,810 people, broken out by samurai and lower-retainer households, shrines, and temples — this is a minor tail, not Tosa's main population, which appears on the facing page. The rest of the leaf is the opening of the next domain, ○龜岡藩 (Kameoka), a 50,000-koku domain: it records a 草高 (assessed yield) of 57,204.7 koku (including a 7,204.7-koku new-field addition), a main land tax (正租) of about 24,461 koku, and a miscellaneous rice tax of about 3,864 koku.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八 (鹿兒島・高知)
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tosa (高知藩): officials roster
pages.page_topic: officials — the named officer hierarchy
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the officials roster (役人) of Tosa domain (高知藩), the Yamauchi domain, in the eighth fascicle of the survey. Where the preceding Satsuma entry named no one, Tosa lists its whole hierarchy: a 知事 (governor), Yamauchi; the 大参事 (senior councillor) Fukao Hiroto; the 権大参事 (junior senior councillor) Gotō Jozan; the 少参事 (junior councillor) Saitō Yakuma; and a long run of 権少参事 (provisional junior councillors) beginning with Konami Gorō and including men who would become national figures, Kataoka Kenkichi and Tani Tateki. The roster and Tosa's combined land-and-sea force of 9,000 (海陸兵員) carry on across the following leaves — the same army the demographics page splits into 6,600 standing (常備) and 2,400 emergency (非常) troops.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tosa (高知藩): junior councillors
pages.page_topic: Continuation of Tosa (Kōchi) domain's Junior Councillor (少参事) roster — thirteen named officials.
pages.page_summary_en: This left leaf continues Tosa domain's (高知藩, the Yamauchi domain) officials roster from the facing right leaf, in the eighth fascicle of the survey. A single rank heading, 少参事 (junior councillor), stands atop the rightmost column, and beneath and to its left run thirteen name columns, read right to left, closing with the celebrated Tosa figures Kataoka Kenkichi (片岡健吉) and Tani Tateki (谷干城). There is no ○ domain-boundary marker on this leaf — the boundary between Kagoshima and Kōchi lies on the facing right leaf — so everything here belongs to Tosa, and the list runs on to the next page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tosa (高知藩): provisional junior councillors
pages.page_topic: Kōchi (Tosa) domain junior-councillor (権少参事) roster — left-half overflow of the fascicle-8 officials list
pages.page_summary_en: A further leaf of Tosa domain's (高知藩) officials roster in the eighth fascicle, made up entirely of names — no figures and no ○ domain-boundary marker. A single rank heading, 権少参事 (provisional junior councillor), sits mid-leaf atop its column. Reading right to left, the six columns to the right of that heading finish the preceding 少参事 (junior councillor) list, while the heading column and the five columns to its left name the six provisional junior councillors.

pages.domain_hi_name: 高知藩・山内藩・龜岡藩
pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（山内、龜岡）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tosa (高知藩), then Yamauchi and Kameoka
pages.page_topic: Officials-and-military boundary page: tail of Kōchi (Tosa), then the start of Yamauchi (Tosa-Shinden) and Kameoka
pages.page_summary_en: A boundary leaf in the eighth fascicle carrying three domains in succession. On the right it completes the officials roster of Tosa (高知藩) — seven councillors, among them Iwasaki Yatarō, the founder of Mitsubishi — and gives Tosa's combined land-and-sea force of 9,000 (海陸兵員). That troop figure prints to the right of the next ○ marker but belongs to Tosa, the domain sharing this leaf, not to what follows. The ○山内藩 marker then opens the Yamauchi (Tosa-Shinden) domain, listing its 知事 (governor) and 大参事 (senior councillor) and a standing army of 89 (常備兵). Finally the ○龜岡藩 marker begins the Kameoka domain of Tanba, whose officials continue onto the next page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 6 — Asao (淺尾藩): closing civil fields
pages.page_topic: Closing fields of Asao domain's vol-2 civil register: status-class populations, kokudaka, and the five-year-average tax breakdown.
pages.page_summary_en: This right leaf holds the closing fields of the preceding domain, Asao (淺尾藩), in the sixth fascicle of the survey; there is no ○ domain-boundary marker here, so Saga has not yet begun — its ○佐嘉藩 marker and land figures fall on the facing left page. Reading right to left, the columns record Asao's status-class populations — no 非人 (outcastes); 98 士族 (samurai) households totalling 403 persons; 72 卒族 (foot-soldier) households totalling 100 persons — followed by its land assessment (草高, assessed yield, about 10,005 koku; 現石, current rice on hand, 4,139 koku) and a five-year-average tax breakdown (正税, main tax, of 3,921 koku of rice plus 764 ryō in cash; 雑税, miscellaneous tax, of 114 koku of rice). Two bracketed notes from the 1928 reprint mark that the survey was taken in the Kōgo year (1870) and that the following lines had stood in red ink in the manuscript margin.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 6 — Saga (佐嘉藩): land assessment and tax
pages.page_topic: kokudaka via 'two-mouth combined / 5-yr average' + main tax
pages.page_summary_en: The land-assessment and tax leaf for Saga domain (佐嘉藩), recorded in the sixth fascicle. Saga states its yield with an unusual phrasing, 貮口合平均 (the two-part combined figure, five-year average): 724,739 koku, formed from a base 高 (kokudaka) of 211,519 plus a 新田高 (new-field assessment) of 513,580 — Saga led the Edo period in reclaiming new paddy, so its real yield far outran its roughly 357,000-koku formal rating. The main tax is given as 213,478 koku of land-tax rice (正租米) and 217,789 koku of tax-collected rice (取納現米), together with a silver tax of 444.1 kanme (with its rice-equivalent 但米 of about 4,441 koku) and a small miscellaneous gold tax of 10 ryō.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 6 — Saga (佐嘉藩): population and products
pages.page_topic: population totals (with M/F) + products
pages.page_summary_en: Saga domain's (佐嘉藩) population totals and trade goods, in the sixth fascicle of the survey. It records 68,710 戸數 (households) and a total population (人員) of 354,450 — 183,517 male and 170,933 female — of which 5,273 are 士族 (samurai) households. The products block lists Saga's output with quantities, including the famous Hizen coal (石炭, 36,000,000 kin), Arita and Imari ceramics (陶器, over 20,000 bales), 92,719 koku of rice, tea, wax, sōmen, sake, and dried shrimp, alongside a cash figure of 99,831 kan-mon. The samurai and foot-soldier person counts continue on the facing left leaf.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第六 (佐嘉 → 佐倉)
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 6 — Saga (佐嘉藩): status classes, then Sakura (佐倉藩)
pages.page_topic: status-class persons + Sakura-han boundary marker
pages.page_summary_en: The left leaf of Saga's (佐嘉藩) demographic spread, giving the status-class person counts that complete the totals on the facing page, in the sixth fascicle. It records 23,823 士族 (samurai) persons; 9,369 卒 (foot-soldier) households and 43,488 persons; 1,032 monk (僧) households and 4,412 persons; and 195 shrine-personnel (社人) households and 850 persons — each with its own male/female split — together with a note that the number of shrines was not specified (社數不詳). The neighbouring domain, Sakura (佐倉藩), a Hotta domain in Shimōsa, begins alongside.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Saga (佐賀藩): officials roster
pages.page_topic: Saga domain officials (fascicle 9): the ○佐賀藩 boundary marker and Saga's councillor roster (governor heading, vacant senior councillor, provisional senior councillor and three further councillors), preceded on the right by the tail of the Ashikaga (足利藩) officials block.
pages.page_summary_en: The leaf that opens Saga domain (佐賀藩) in the ninth fascicle, the officials and military register — note that this register writes the name 佐賀, where the civil fascicles used 佐嘉. The ○佐賀藩 marker is the domain boundary: everything to its left is Saga, everything to its right belongs to the preceding domain, Ashikaga (足利藩). Saga's officials, read right to left from the marker, are a 知事 (governor) heading with no appointee named here (Saga's governor was a Nabeshima), a 大参事 (senior councillor) post recorded as 欠員 (vacant), a 権大参事 (provisional senior councillor) Nakano Takumi, and three further councillors, Ikeda Yaichi, Fukae Sukeemon, and Chō Gen'ichi. To the right of the marker stands the close of the Ashikaga block, ending with a note that its troops were not ascertained (兵隊審ナラス) — a remark about Ashikaga's forces, not Saga's. Saga's own army appears on a later leaf, not on this page.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第九 (佐賀 → 佐倉)
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Saga (佐賀藩): army
pages.page_topic: military — Saga's six-battalion army (2,972 / 36 guns)
pages.page_summary_en: Saga domain's (佐賀藩) army, in the ninth fascicle's military register; its ○佐賀藩 marker and officials roster stand on the facing page, while the force itself is recorded here. Saga fields six battalions (六大隊) totalling 2,972 troops — 864 officers (士官), 180 artillery soldiers (砲士), 1,440 infantry (兵士), 108 artillery privates (砲卒), 260 infantry privates (兵卒), and 120 bandsmen (樂卒) — with 36 cannon (大砲). A note records that the roster of junior officials and below was withheld (少参事以下書ナラス).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nomura (野村藩): civil register
pages.page_topic: Civil register (land tax, households, population with commoner/temple and M/F breakdown) of the small Nomura domain.
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page is the complete fascicle-4 civil register for the very small domain of 野村 (Nomura). It records a main tax (正税) of about 6.86 koku of rice plus 3 kanmon of cash, 45 households (戸數), and a population (人員) of 207. Under 内 (of which), that total divides into 2 Buddhist temple houses with 4 monks and 43 commoner houses holding 203 people, and the 203 commoners split into 106 male (男) and 97 female (女). The whole leaf belongs to Nomura alone; there is no ○ domain-boundary marker.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Nomura (野村藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: officials_and_military
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the fascicle-9 officials-and-military entry for Nomura (野村藩), which opens at the ○ domain-boundary marker. Its ranked establishment runs from a governor (知事) and one senior councillor (大参事) down through two junior senior councillors (権大参事) and three junior councillors (少参事), each listed with the appointee's name. The forces are given as two infantry platoons of 87 men (兵隊) and an artillery unit of six guns and 40 gunners (砲隊). The columns to the right of Nomura's ○marker belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Nobeoka (延岡藩) — the tail of its junior-councillor names overflowing leftward — not to Nomura.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Kumamoto (熊本藩): land assessment and taxes
pages.page_topic: kokudaka (formal vs real) + sundry taxes + male population
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fascicle-5 land-and-tax register for Kumamoto (熊本藩), the Higo domain of the Hosokawa house. Its formal rating (高) was 540,000 koku, but the real assessed yield (草高) is recorded at 786,016 koku — a new-field uplift of 246,016 koku noted under 但内 (of which). The main tax (正税) comes to 304,838 koku, with sundry taxes (諸税) in rice (73,363 koku), salt (1,965), gold (2,615 ryō), and 503,469 jin of wax-tree berries (櫨實), the raw material for Higo's celebrated vegetable-wax industry. The male population (男人口) of 361,024 is entered here; the female count and grand total appear on the demographic pages.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Kumamoto (熊本藩): male population by status
pages.page_topic: population by status class (male)
pages.page_summary_en: This page breaks Kumamoto's male population down by status class, and — unusually — the domain registers its commoners in full. The largest groups are farmers (農, 278,846) and the sotsu class (卒族, 37,219), followed by merchants (商, 18,738), samurai households (士族, 8,050), former rear-vassals (從前陪臣, 8,259), clergy (僧侶, 3,167), and eta or outcaste persons (穢多, 3,495), together with smaller groups, all summing to the 361,024 male total. The total female population (女人口, 355,783) and the female samurai count (士族女, 8,000) also print here; the female-by-class breakdown and the grand totals appear on the facing leaves.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Kumamoto (熊本藩): female population and totals
pages.page_topic: Kumamoto female-side status-class population, with treasure-persons, grand total population, and household counts
pages.page_summary_en: This is the female (女) half of Kumamoto's status-class population register, continuing the male-side breakdown on the facing page. Reading right to left it gives female counts for each group — sotsu class (卒族, 34,514), former rear-vassals (從前陪臣, 7,608), farmer houses (農家, 278,584), merchant houses (商家, 18,153), and eta or outcaste persons (穢多, 3,578), among others — followed by a treasure-persons category (物寳人, 3,183), the grand total population (人口合) of 719,990, the total household count (戸數) of 148,852, and 4,281 domain-retainer households (藩士). The whole leaf is Kumamoto's; there is no ○ domain-boundary marker.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第五 （久留米）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Kurume (久留米藩) opens: land, taxes, and households
pages.page_topic: Opening of the Kurume (久留米藩) civil register — domain rank, land yield, taxes, and household counts — with a short Kumamoto (Higo) sailing-ship tail above the boundary marker.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries a domain boundary. At the top right, to the right of the ○久留米藩 marker, sits the tail of the previous domain, Kumamoto (Higo): its two sail-rigged ships (風帆船, 二艘), each named with its origin and build. Left of the marker, the entry for Kurume (久留米藩) opens with its civil and economic data — a formal rank (本高) of 210,000 koku, an assessed yield (草高) of 366,272 koku, a main tax (正税) of 117,280 koku, and miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 72,685 kan (of which 8,551 is product tax). The total households (戸數) come to 50,037, broken down under 内 into 45,727 directly-administered commoner houses plus samurai (士族, 948), sotsu, eta, shrine-servants, hinin, and temple houses.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Kumamoto (熊本藩): officials roster
pages.page_topic: Kumamoto-han officials roster (governor and councillor ranks) with the domain's military-section header
pages.page_summary_en: This is the officials page of Kumamoto's fascicle-9 entry, opening at the ○熊本藩 domain-boundary marker. Kumamoto's establishment is given as four ranked headings with headcounts — one governor (知事), four senior councillors (大参事), five provisional senior councillors (権大参事), and six junior councillors (少参事) — with the appointees' names listed below in columns, beginning with 松井新次郎 as governor. The far-left 兵隊 (troops) heading opens the military section, whose corps and warship figures continue onto the facing leaf. The small run of names to the right of the ○熊本藩 marker belongs to the preceding domain sharing this leaf, not to Kumamoto.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Kumamoto (熊本藩): army and navy
pages.page_topic: army + six-ship navy
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-9 leaf records Kumamoto's disclosed forces: a samurai corps (士隊) of two battalions (576 men), a rifle corps (銃隊) of four battalions (1,152), and an artillery corps (砲隊) of 288 gunners with 24 French-pattern guns — roughly 2,016 troops in all. Its navy is notably large: six vessels, mostly foreign-built steamers, including 萬里丸 (ex-Cosmos White, French), 凌雲丸 (ex-Granada, British iron), and 奮迅丸 (ex-Felicia), plus a sailing ship (風帆船) and two more steamers. The ○熊本藩 marker and the named officials sit on the facing leaf, while the ○久留米藩 marker at the left begins the next domain, Kurume.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Kumamoto (熊本藩): households, shrines, and ships
pages.page_topic: household counts by social category, plus shrine/temple, governor's-family, and steamship registers
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-5 page tallies Kumamoto's households (軒) by social category. Reading right to left it counts soldier-class houses (兵卒, 15,118), former rear-vassals (從前陪臣, 3,815), farmers (農, 114,510), merchants (商, 6,965), shrine households (社家, 277), Buddhist temples (寺院, 1,240, of which 86 draw a domain stipend), blind persons (盲人, 573), and eta or outcaste households (穢多, 1,352). The left margin adds 19 stipended Shinto shrines (神社), the governor's family (知事家族, 10 persons — 5 male, 5 female), and the domain's three steamships (蒸氣, 三艘), each given with its foreign and Japanese names and country of build. The entire leaf is Kumamoto's, with no ○ domain-boundary marker.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kanazawa (金澤藩): population, temples, and standing army
pages.page_topic: Kanazawa (Kaga) population, religious institutions, retainer-class register, and standing army
pages.page_summary_en: This facing half of Kanazawa's (金澤藩) fascicle-2 entry opens at the ○金澤藩 domain-boundary marker at the far left; the whole leaf is Kanazawa's own data. Reading right to left it records the directly-governed population (人口, 26,064), 3,247 Shinto shrines (神社) and 2,330 Buddhist temples (寺院), and the samurai-and-soldier households (士卒族戸數, 16,780) with their population of 37,793 (19,008 male, 18,785 female). The left third lays out Kanazawa's standing army: 12 infantry battalions totalling 5,076 men (戎兵), one cavalry squadron (騎兵, 165), an artillery regiment (砲兵, 270), an engineer corps (工兵隊, 572), and a baggage and transport corps (輜重隊, 89).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kanazawa (金澤藩): land assessment, demographics, and taxes
pages.page_topic: kokudaka + headline demographics + main taxes
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the fascicle 2 (civil and economic) entry for Kanazawa (金澤藩), the Maeda house and the largest non-Tokugawa domain in Japan — the famed 'million-koku Kaga.' It records a 草高 (assessed yield) of 1,353,353 koku, of which the productive base (込高) is 1,025,020 and reclaimed new field (新田改出高) accounts for 328,333, with a main rice tax (正租米) of 633,134 koku alongside substantial coin taxes. The headline population figures also print here — 戸數 (households) 198,811 and 人口 (population) 997,669 (male 498,585, female 499,084), the largest counts in the survey — of which 士族 (samurai households) number 7,797 and 28,683 persons, a modest share against nearly a million residents. The retainer sub-classes and religious establishment continue on the following leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kanazawa (金澤藩): retainer classes, clergy, and military summary
pages.page_topic: retainer/dependent sub-classes (with M/F) + religious establishment + military summary
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Kanazawa's (金澤藩) demographic entry, breaking the wider population into its sub-classes: 卒族 (lower samurai) 27,038 persons in 9,703 households, 中間小者 (attendants and menials) 5,938 in 2,699 households, and the outcaste classes (藤内等) 11,695 in 2,243 households. It then records the religious establishment — 神社 (Shinto shrines) 407 with 1,799 shrine personnel, and temples with 13,326 monks — each population column carrying its own male/female split (for example, 卒族 14,655 men and 12,383 women). A summary of the domain's reformed army appears alongside: five infantry battalions (步兵) and three artillery units (砲兵), an officer cadre of 1,106 and 1,568 rank-and-file troops (兵卒), plus two steamships and three sailing vessels.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kanazawa (金澤藩): officials and army (shared leaf)
pages.page_topic: Domain-boundary page: the preceding domain's junior-councillor tail and full standing army, then the ○金澤藩 marker and Kanazawa's senior officials (knowledge-governor and councillors)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf, from the fascicle 8 officials-and-military register, sits across a domain boundary marked by the ○ before 金澤藩. Because the columns read right to left, the material to the RIGHT of that ○marker belongs to the PRECEDING domain: the close of its officials roster (少参事 11, 権少参事 8) followed by its full standing army — twelve infantry battalions of 5,076 men, one cavalry platoon (160 troops, 165 horses), an artillery regiment of 279 men, an engineer corps (工兵隊) of 572, and a transport corps (輜重隊) of 89. To the LEFT of the ○marker Kanazawa's own entry begins: Knowledge-Governor (知事) Maeda Yoshiyasu, Senior Councillor (大参事) Shinohara Kanroku, and Provisional Senior Councillor (権大参事) Rikuhara Shintarō, with a lower register of further councillors and a vermilion addendum, dated the twelfth month of the snake year, adding two more names.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kanazawa (金澤藩): junior officials and army corps
pages.page_topic: junior-official roster + disclosed corps
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the fascicle 8 (officials and military) entry for Kanazawa (金澤藩). Its senior officials and the ○金澤藩 boundary marker appear on the facing leaf; this half holds the junior-official roster — 少参事 and 権少参事 (Honda Shigurehei and eight others) — together with the disclosed army: five infantry battalions (步兵, 320 riflemen each) and three artillery units (砲兵, 144 men each). The personnel totals recorded with the entry are 1,568 rank-and-file troops (兵卒人員), 1,106 officers and officials (士等役員), and 464 corps members (隊士), plus four councillor counts summing to 47.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Tsurumaki (鶴牧藩): land assessment and taxes (shared leaf)
pages.page_topic: Opening of Tsurumaki domain's civil register: kokudaka, land/cash taxes, received-koku, and household count, with the preceding domain's military roster overflowing to the right of the boundary marker.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the fascicle 4 (civil and economic) entry for Tsurumaki (鶴牧藩), a small fudai domain of the Mizuno house in Kazusa, its ○鶴牧藩 boundary marker sitting mid-page with its 15,000-koku official omotedaka gloss. Everything to the LEFT of that ○marker is Tsurumaki's: a 草高 (assessed yield) of 19,910 koku given as a five-year average (1864–1868), a main rice tax (正租米) of 8,896 koku with a cash component, a miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of about 111 kan, a small received-koku figure (受領高) of 25.2 koku tied to two temples, and 戸數 (households) of 4,757. To the RIGHT of the ○marker the preceding domain's military roster overflows onto this leaf: the 振武隊 (169 men), 先進隊 (212), 壯進隊 (224), and an artillery corps (砲隊) of 30, totalling 737 men — these belong to the previous domain, not to Tsurumaki.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Tsurumaki (鶴牧藩): population and household counts
pages.page_topic: Tsurumaki domain population, household counts by status, and clergy/shrine/village/troop tallies
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the fascicle 4 (civil and economic) entry for Tsurumaki (鶴牧藩), the Mizuno house's small fudai domain in Kazusa. Reading right to left, it gives household counts (114 士族 samurai households, 101 卒族 lower-samurai households, 75 temples) and a total 人口 (population) of 20,586 (male 10,563, female 10,064), broken down by status: 561 samurai-class persons, 341 lower samurai, 61 shrine attendants, 65 temple residents, and small numbers of mountain ascetics, shrine officials, diviners, and blind-guild members. It closes with 19 神社 (Shinto shrines), 64 villages (村數), and three platoons of troops (兵隊) of forty men each, noting explicitly that the governor's family and any warships are not recorded. This is a single-domain leaf, with no ○ boundary marker.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第九 （鶴舞、鶴牧）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Tsurumai (鶴舞藩) and Tsurumaki (鶴牧藩): officials (shared leaf)
pages.page_topic: Fascicle-9 domain officials for Tsurumaki, sharing the page with the full Tsurumai officials block and a preceding-domain tail name.
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle 9 (officials and military) leaf holds parts of three adjacent crane-named domains, its columns reading right to left. First comes a single tail name belonging to the domain preceding Tsurumai; then the ○鶴舞藩 (Tsurumai) boundary marker introduces Tsurumai's complete officials roster — 大参事 2, 権大参事 4, 少参事 2, 権少参事 4 — and its army of 739 troops (兵隊). Mid-leaf the ○鶴牧藩 (Tsurumaki) marker opens Tsurumaki's own entry, but only its senior councillors appear here: 大参事 (2) and 権大参事 (5). Tsurumaki's remaining ranks and its 120 troops continue on the facing leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Tsurumaki (鶴牧藩) tail and Tsuruga (敦賀藩) opening (shared leaf)
pages.page_topic: The tail of Tsurumaki's officials/military register (junior councillors + 120 troops) followed by the ○敦賀藩 boundary marker opening Tsuruga's councillor roster.
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle 9 (officials and military) leaf sits across a domain boundary marked by the ○ before 敦賀藩 (Tsuruga). Because the columns read right to left, the material to the RIGHT of that ○marker belongs to the PRECEDING domain, Tsurumaki (鶴牧藩): its junior-councillor counts (少参事 1, 権少参事 5), six named officers, and its military figure of 120 infantry (兵隊). The ○敦賀藩 marker then opens Tsuruga, whose councillor columns follow to the LEFT — Senior Councillor (大参事) Teramachi Shirōzaemon, two Provisional Senior Councillors (権大参事), and several junior councillors — along with a two-man liaison office (公用役掛) and a short editorial note at lower left.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第四 (名古屋)
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nagoya (名古屋藩): land assessment and sub-fiefs
pages.page_topic: kokudaka — reformed survey, sub-fief highs, and the 8-bu tax note
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the fascicle 4 (civil and economic) entry for Nagoya (名古屋藩), the senior Tokugawa shinpan of the Owari-Tokugawa house, with lands scattered across Owari, Mino, Ōmi and Settsu. Reflecting its reformed survey of June 1870, it records a current 高 (kokudaka) of 853,125 koku — among the largest in the country — from which sundry deductions (諸引高) of 40,736 leave a residual (殘高) of 778,897, with 261,250 koku delivered as tax (租納高) and a further surveyed 'external figure' (外數) of 282,150 koku. The page also itemises Owari's semi-autonomous sub-fiefs as separate managed-yield (所務高) entries, including Ishikawa Tahachirō's 19,171 koku and 10,000 koku returned by the Imao domain, and carries the 此八分出 ('eight-tenths output') note explaining how the tax-rice was recalculated.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第四 （名古屋）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nagoya (名古屋藩): tax and cultivated area
pages.page_topic: Nagoya (Owari) tax and cultivated-area register: koku deductions, net assessed/levied yield, and total/exempt/waste arable area continuing the kokudaka entry.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the fascicle 4 (civil and economic) entry for Nagoya (名古屋藩), the Owari-Tokugawa domain, carrying its assessment forward from the preceding leaf. Reading right to left it gives a koku block — sundry deductions (諸引高) of 766, a remaining yield (残高) of 9,234, tax paid (租納) of 2,599, and a measured 'eight-tenths output' quantity of 2,807 — followed by an area section (內) recording total arable land (反別) of 11,164 chō drawn from holdings in Owari, Mino, Mikawa, Ōmi and Shinano, of which 1,288 chō is exempt or transferred land (引地) and 8,565 chō remains taxable (残反別), with a final area tax (税納) of 8,969 koku. This is a single-domain leaf, with no ○ boundary marker.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第四（名古屋）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nagoya (名古屋藩): kokudaka and population
pages.page_topic: Nagoya (Owari) civil register: tail of the kokudaka/rice-revenue block (including the 山村・千村・毛利 and 石河 sub-fief administered-kokudaka figures) plus the household and population (士族/卒, with 男/女 splits) block.
pages.page_summary_en: This is Nagoya domain's (the Owari-Tokugawa house) civil and economic register in the fourth fascicle of the survey. It completes the land and rice-revenue figures — a combined current rice yield (合現米) of 320,938 koku, plus additional administered kokudaka held by the Kiso sub-fief stewards (13,485 koku) and by Ishikawa Tahachirō (石河太八郎, 10,097 koku) whose internal breakdown the source states was not reported. It then gives the household and population block: 8,650 samurai-class households (戸數), of which 2,530 are 士族 (samurai households) and 6,120 are 卒 (lower-samurai), for a population (人員) of 49,340 — 15,644 shizoku (7,629 male / 8,015 female) and 33,696 sotsu (17,844 male / 15,852 female). The whole leaf is Nagoya's continuing register; no neighboring domain begins here.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第四 (名古屋)
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nagoya (名古屋藩): commoner and religious population
pages.page_topic: population by class — household counts paired with class populations (with M/F)
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues Nagoya domain's (Owari) demographic register in the fourth fascicle, pairing household and institution counts with the matching class populations. It records 192,177 commoner households (平民戸數), of which most are farming households, alongside 2,438 Buddhist temples (寺院), 811 shrine-priest households (社家), 518 outcaste (穢多) households, and 1,531 hinin and beggar households (非人乞丐). Each population is given with a male/female split — for example an internal population (内人員) of 840,896 (420,055 male / 420,841 female), 5,663 Buddhist clergy (内僧, including 86 nuns), and 6,001 hinin and beggars (2,873 male / 3,128 female). Unusually for these registers, Owari recorded its commoners in full detail; the domain's second population total and its military figures print on the facing half-page.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第九（鶴田、名古屋）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Tsuruta (鶴田藩) and Nagoya (名古屋藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials and military (Nagoya; Tsuruta tail)
pages.page_summary_en: This is an officials-and-military leaf from the ninth fascicle, and it carries two domains across a boundary. To the right of the ○名古屋藩 domain-boundary marker is the tail of the previous domain, Tsuruta (鶴田藩, Hizen), with its own ○marker, four councillor rank headings, and its named appointees stacked in columns. To the left of the marker is Nagoya's own record: its officials are given only as headcounts — 2 senior councillors (大参事), 6 junior-senior councillors (権大参事), 5 junior councillors (少参事), and 11 provisional junior councillors (権少参事) — followed by the military block (兵隊, troops): 2,480 samurai-class soldiers (士族兵) and 4,720 lower-samurai soldiers (卒族兵), for a total of 7,200. The leftmost Tsuruta name-column overflows to the right of the Nagoya marker but still belongs to Tsuruta.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nagoya (名古屋藩) tail and Nakatsu (中津藩) opening
pages.page_topic: Domain-boundary page: the tail of Nagoya's commoner-population block (right of the ○中津藩 marker) meets the head of Nakatsu's kokudaka / tax-yield block (left of the marker).
pages.page_summary_en: This is a boundary page in the fourth fascicle (the civil and economic register), read right to left. The right-hand columns finish the previous domain, Nagoya (名古屋藩): a population (人員) of 724,569 (360,899 male / 363,670 female), 28,634 merchant households, 488 temple halls with 731 clergy, 88 yin-yang diviner (陰陽師) households, and a standing force of 7,200 men. The ○中津藩 domain-boundary marker, with its territory note spanning districts of Buzen, Bungo, and Chikuzen, then opens Nakatsu domain (the Okudaira house). Nakatsu's figures begin on the left: an assessed yield (草高) of 100,000 koku, a tax yield (物成高) of 54,354 koku of rice plus 238 ryō of gold, and a main land tax (正租) of 46,310 koku of rice.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nakatsu (中津藩): taxes and population
pages.page_topic: Nakatsu domain's civil register: miscellaneous tax (money + rice) figures, household and population totals, and the religious-house / clergy breakdown.
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues Nakatsu domain's (中津藩, the Okudaira house of Buzen) civil register in the fourth fascicle. The right side carries the miscellaneous-tax group (雜税) — a large cash sum of some 20,279 ryō, a rice figure of 294 koku, and further cash sums. The center gives 20,767 households (戸數) and a population (人員) of 98,542, with an itemized breakdown: 1,523 samurai, lower-samurai, and sundry households (士卒雜人共) totaling 7,133 people (4,055 male / 3,078 female); 170 shrine-priest households (社家); 227 Buddhist temples (寺院); and 287 shrines (神社). The entire leaf is Nakatsu; the next domain's boundary marker would begin on the following page.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第九 （中津、中村）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Nakatsu (中津藩) and Nakamura (中村藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Nakatsu officials & military, into Nakamura
pages.page_summary_en: This is an officials-and-military leaf from the ninth fascicle, read right to left, spanning two domains. The ○中津藩 boundary marker opens Nakatsu (the Okudaira house of Buzen): its official establishment count is recorded as 不詳 (not detailed), and its army (兵隊, troops) is given as 1,059 samurai (士) and 878 lower-samurai (卒), for 1,937 in all. Its senior officials then follow by rank — senior councillors (大参事), junior-senior councillors (権大参事), and junior councillors (少参事) — with the last two Nakatsu names overflowing to the right of the next marker but still belonging to Nakatsu. The ○中村藩 marker then opens Nakamura (the Sōma-Nakamura house of Mutsu), whose named councillors hang in columns below their rank headings; Nakamura's record continues onto the following page.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第二（和歌山）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Wakayama (和歌山藩): land, taxes, and population
pages.page_topic: Wakayama (Kii) domain land assessment, tax, product-tax revenue, households, and population
pages.page_summary_en: This is Wakayama domain's (Kii, a major Tokugawa-collateral house) fiscal and demographic entry in the second fascicle, opened by the ○和歌山藩 boundary marker at the right. It records an assessed yield (草高) of 539,469 koku plus a small newly reclaimed-field yield (新田高), the regular land tax (正租) in rice, gold, and cash, miscellaneous taxes (雜税) including salt (鹽), and a product tax (産物税) of about 28,743 ryō of gold. It closes with 108,245 households (戸數), a population (人口) of 458,826 (232,646 male / 226,180 female), and an additional 5,326 outcaste (穢多) households.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（小見川、和歌山）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Omigawa (小見川藩) and Wakayama (和歌山藩): officials
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (governor and councillor ranks) for Omigawa and the opening of Wakayama, from the fascicle-8 administrative-personnel survey.
pages.page_summary_en: This is an officials leaf from the eighth fascicle, and it holds the boundary between two domains. The upper block belongs to Omigawa (小見川藩), a small Shimōsa domain: its governor (知事) and five councillor-rank posts are listed with headcounts, its named appointees run in a column headed by governor Nukada Daigorō (額田大五郎), and a troop figure (兵隊) of 93 is given with a note that troops were recorded but no personnel detail. Below the ○和歌山藩 boundary marker begins Wakayama (Kii); only the start of its officials appears here — a governor (知事), one senior councillor (大参事), and three junior-senior councillors (権大参事). Everything to the right of the ○和歌山藩 marker belongs to the preceding Omigawa entry, so only the three left-hand columns and the marker itself are Wakayama's.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第二（小見川）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Omigawa (小見川藩): taxes, population, and villages
pages.page_topic: Omigawa domain (小見川藩) civil/fiscal survey: land tax, misc tax, households, population by status, temples/shrines, eta, villages.
pages.page_summary_en: This is Omigawa domain's (小見川藩, an Uchida-family domain of about 10,000 koku in Shimōsa Province) civil and fiscal entry in the second fascicle; the running header and the closing village note naming 小見川村 identify it. There is no ○domain-boundary marker on this leaf — the data flow as a single continuous domain. It records a main land tax (正租) of 589,812 mon in cash, miscellaneous taxes (雜税) of rice and cash, 1,621 households (戸數), and a commoner population (人口) of 8,264 (4,071 male / 4,193 female). It also gives 80 samurai and lower-samurai households (士卒族, of which 74 are 士族 and 6 are 卒) totaling 288 people, 43 Buddhist temples (寺), 27 shrines (社), 6 outcaste (穢多) households, and 24 villages (村).

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（小見川、和歌山）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Omigawa (小見川藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Omigawa (小見川) officials + troops — shares the Wakayama-opening leaf
pages.page_summary_en: This is Omigawa domain's (小見川藩, Shimōsa) officials-and-military block from the eighth fascicle, on a leaf it shares with Ōtawara to the right and the opening of Wakayama to the left. It lists the domain's councillor ranks by headcount — one senior councillor (大参事), two junior-senior councillors (権大参事), one junior councillor (少参事), and one provisional junior councillor (権少参事) — together with a troop figure (兵隊) of 93. Omigawa printed no governor's name on this page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hiroshima (廣島藩): land assessment
pages.page_topic: Hiroshima domain fascicle-7 landholding: total/remaining kokudaka, district and village counts, plus household, shrine, eta, and warship notations.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the landholding register for Hiroshima domain (廣島藩) from Fascicle 7 of the survey; its figures read to the left of the ○廣島藩 domain-boundary marker. It records a gross assessed yield (惣高) of 488,024.24735 koku — including 12,433.15575 koku of newly reclaimed fields (新田) and an iron-mine levy (鐵山役高) of 582.972 koku — and, after 456.9244 koku of tax-exempt land (除地) is set aside, a residual yield (殘高) of 487,567.32295 koku. The holding spans Aki and Bingo provinces across 868 villages (村數), with 22 Shinto shrines (神社), a governor's household (知事家) of 3, and an outcaste (穢多) population of 13; warships are noted as not recorded. A marginal variant copy gives an alternate gross total of 485,714.12515 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hiroshima (廣島藩): fiscal totals
pages.page_topic: Hiroshima domain fiscal totals (fascicle 7): land after deductions, land tax, miscellaneous tax, cash revenue, remaining koku, and grand total, followed by a variant-edition (別本) recomputation of the same figures printed in the original book's margin.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Hiroshima domain's (廣島藩) fiscal accounts in Fascicle 7; it carries no ○ boundary marker, so all figures belong to Hiroshima. The main block records internal assessed land (内高) of 2,133.3459 koku, a residual yield (殘高) of 483,580.77925 koku, the regular land tax in rice (正租) of 242,999.4185 koku, miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 12,390.225 koku, cash revenue (錢) of 86,018.928 kan, and a grand total (合〆) of 254,422.4051 koku. A note explains that the following six lines were written in the margin of the original book, introducing a variant edition that re-reports the land tax (242,032.18 koku), miscellaneous tax (14,509.009 koku), cash (66,097.765 kan), its rice equivalent (此米, 861.939 koku), and a variant grand total of 258,370.366 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hiroshima (廣島藩): population and households
pages.page_topic: Hiroshima domain demographics (population by status class, household counts, temples/shrines, outcaste dwellings) and product-tax revenue.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Hiroshima domain (廣島藩) in Fascicle 7 with its demographic register; it carries no ○ boundary marker, so all figures belong to Hiroshima. It gives a total population (人口) of 914,157 (468,180 male / 445,977 female) and 185,104 households (戸數), with samurai households (士族, 1,780) and foot-soldier households (卒族, 4,730) broken out separately, alongside the samurai population (9,536) and foot-soldier population (23,046). The page also counts 999 Buddhist temples (寺院), 507 shrine-priest families (社家), 2,737 shrine officiants (社務人), and 5,028 outcaste dwellings (非人穢多小屋). The printed page number in the bottom margin is 169.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Hiroshima (廣島藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Fascicle-9 officials-and-military register: the tail of Shizuku domain (senior councillors + a 3-platoon force) to the right of the ○廣島藩 marker, then Hiroshima's councillor establishment (大参事 2, 権大参事 1, 少参事 4, 権少参事 4) with appointee names and its 6,000-man / 10-battalion army.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf holds the officials-and-military register (職員・兵隊) for Hiroshima domain (廣島藩) from Fascicle 9. To the left of the ○廣島藩 boundary marker is Hiroshima's own entry: a councillor establishment of two senior councillors (大参事), one associate senior councillor (権大参事) with three more under selection, four junior councillors (少参事), and four associate junior councillors (権少参事), together with named appointees, and a military strength of 6,000 troops (兵員) organized into ten battalions (大隊). The columns to the right of the marker belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Shizuku (志筑藩): its senior councillors and its small force of one platoon of standing troops (常備兵) and two platoons of reserve troops (非常兵), not Hiroshima's.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Okayama (岡山藩): land, tax, and population (opening)
pages.page_topic: Boundary page: tail of Numata domain's civil register (right of the marker) and the opening land/tax block of Okayama domain (left of the ○岡山藩 marker), Fascicle 2.
pages.page_summary_en: This is a boundary leaf in Fascicle 2 of the survey where the ○岡山藩 marker opens the Okayama domain (岡山藩) entry. To the left of the marker are Okayama's opening figures: a nominal assessed yield (草高) of 454,117.20 koku (of which 15,000 koku were split off to Ikusaka domain), a base assessment (高) of 315,200.03 koku, reclaimed new-field yield (新田改出高) of 138,917.17 koku, regular land-tax rice (正租米) of 186,911.31 koku, and miscellaneous-tax rice (雜税米) of 1,387.49 koku. Because the text reads right-to-left, the columns to the right of the ○岡山藩 marker — 41 temples (寺), 123 villages (村數), and the outcaste household and population counts (穢多戸數 215 / 穢多人口 1,012; 非人戸數 13 / 非人人口 58) — belong to the previous domain, Numata (沼田藩), not Okayama. The printed page number is 102.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Okayama (岡山藩): tax reconciliation and population
pages.page_topic: Okayama domain fascicle-2 continuation: land-tax/kokudaka reconciliation (with koku apportioned to the Ikusaka sub-domain) and the samurai/commoner household-and-population breakdown.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Okayama domain (岡山藩) in Fascicle 2; it carries no ○ boundary marker, so all figures belong to Okayama. The right half completes a land-tax and yield reconciliation, with a grand total (合) of 188,298.79 koku, 723.55 koku lost to flood and drought (水旱減石), and portions of the actual koku (現石) and land tax apportioned off to the Ikusaka sub-domain (生坂藩), leaving a remainder of about 183,246 koku (殘高). The left half records households and population by status: samurai (士族) 2,711 households and 9,738 persons (5,304 male / 4,434 female), foot-soldiers (卒族) 3,026 households and 7,799 persons (5,820 male / 1,979 female), and commoners (庶人) 77,489 households. The printed page number is 103.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Okayama (岡山藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Okayama-han officials roster (fascicle 8): governor and senior councillor appointees, with the preceding domain's junior-councillors and military tally overflowing to the right of the marker.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the officials-and-military entry for Okayama domain (岡山藩) in Fascicle 8, headed by the ○岡山藩 boundary marker. Reading right-to-left, Okayama's own roster lists the governor (知事), the senior councillors (大参事) Tokura and Ikeda, and the associate senior councillors (権大参事), continued on the facing leaf. The military figures to the right of the ○岡山藩 marker — 121 samurai riflemen (銃士), 110 lower-rank riflemen (銃卒), 20 artillery soldiers (砲士), and 2 cannon (大砲) — belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Toyotsu (豐津藩), not Okayama. The printed page number in the bottom margin is 273.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tottori (鳥取藩): land, population, and status
pages.page_topic: Tottori domain civil/economic profile (fascicle 2): rice yield, households, population with male/female and status breakdowns, shrines/temples, and one warship.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf holds the civil and economic profile of Tottori domain (鳥取藩) from Fascicle 2, opened by its ○ boundary marker with a former assessment (元高) of 320,000 koku. It records an assessed rice yield (合米) of about 206,359.7 koku, 147,510 households, and a total population of 714,022 (363,776 male / 350,246 female). An internal breakdown gives the samurai-and-foot-soldier class (6,432 households; 30,645 persons), shrine-priest families (社家), and temples (寺). Village and shrine counts are marked as not recorded, the governor's family is noted as unrecorded (知事家族不記), and the domain reports one warship (艦壹艘), the Boshin-maru (戊辰丸).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tottori (鳥取藩): yield and tax revenue
pages.page_topic: Tottori domain fiscal survey (Fascicle 2): assessed yield, branch-fief sub-allotments, tax revenue in rice and silver
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Tottori domain (鳥取藩), the Ikeda house's holding in Inaba and Hōki, in Fascicle 2; it carries no ○ boundary marker, so all figures belong to Tottori. The right block records a nominal assessed yield (草高) of 428,169.70 koku, three branch-fief allotments held by Ikeda kinsmen (30,000 / 4,500 / 20,000 koku), and 14,710.255 koku of permanently uncultivable land (永荒). The left block gives the five-year-average tax revenue — regular land-tax rice (正租米) of 156,284.052 koku, fixed-rate rice (定免米) of 164,720.944 koku, miscellaneous-tax rice (雜税米) of 523.706 koku, and silver (銀) of 516.658 kanme — together with a 3,000-koku received fief (受領高) in the Ōyama area of Hōki.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tottori (鳥取藩): new-field tax and demographics
pages.page_topic: Tottori domain land-tax revenue (new fields, regular/fixed-rate/miscellaneous rice, copper cash) and household/population figures with samurai (shizoku) and foot-soldier (sotsu) status breakdowns.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Tottori domain (鳥取藩), which administered Inaba and Hōki provinces, in Fascicle 2. It records the new-field tax base — reclaimed fields (新田) of 516.893 koku, regular land-tax rice (正租米) of 1,220.545 koku, fixed-rate rice (定免米) of 1,312.025 koku, miscellaneous-tax rice (雜税米) of 3.5 koku, and copper cash (錢) of 81 kan — alongside demographic totals of 79,881 households (戸數) and a population (人口) of 371,640 (191,093 male / 180,547 female). A breakdown (内譯) then splits out the samurai (士族: 1,710 households / 8,605 persons) and foot-soldier (卒族: 7,456 households / 24,205 persons) populations by sex. The printed foot-soldier male and female sub-totals do not sum to the printed total, an inconsistency left as it appears in the source.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tottori (鳥取藩): religious and outcaste households
pages.page_topic: Tottori religious/outcaste household counts and populations with male/female splits (Fascicle 2 continuation)
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page continues Tottori domain's (鳥取藩) demographic register in Fascicle 2 (藩制一覧表第二) of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran. The domain identity carries over from the preceding leaf and no ○ domain-boundary marker appears, so every column here belongs to Tottori. It tabulates households and populations, each split into male (男) and female (女), for a series of religious and outcaste categories: Shinto-priest households (社家戸數) at 750 houses and 1,752 people, Buddhist temples (寺院) at 536 with a population of 2,013, eta (穢多, outcaste) at 1,261 households and 3,783 people, hinin (非人) at 272 households and 816 people, Shugendō ascetics (修驗), onmyōji diviners (陰陽師), and komusō mendicant monks (虚無僧). It closes with a shrine total (神社) of 1,518; the village-count field (村數) is left blank, the source printing the note シレス ("not known").

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tottori (鳥取藩): officials
pages.page_topic: Tottori domain officials (governor and councillors) opening its fascicle-8 entry, preceded by the tail of Tokushima domain's military overflow.
pages.page_summary_en: This is a Fascicle 8 page, the fascicle that records domain officials and military strength. The ○鳥取藩 marker opens Tottori domain's entry, and its roster of officials (職員) fills the lower part of the leaf: the governorship (知事, no name printed here), a grand-councillor rank (大参事) with three appointees, an acting grand-councillor rank (権大参事) with two, and a junior-councillor rank (少参事) with two. The material to the right of the ○鳥取藩 marker is the tail end of the previous domain sharing this leaf, Tokushima (徳島藩): its last official plus its troop counts of 1,619 soldiers (兵士) and 2,579 rank-and-file (兵卒). Those troop figures belong to Tokushima, not Tottori.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Horie (堀江藩): civil register
pages.page_topic: Horie domain civil register: shrine/temple land, households, population by status, villages, shrines, Shugendo, governor's family
pages.page_summary_en: This right half-page is the complete civil register (Fascicle 1) entry for Horie domain (堀江藩), a tiny (~10,000-koku) Tōtōmi domain; the running header reads 藩制一覧表第一（堀江） and the block closes with the governor's-family field. It records 15 koku of shrine and temple land (社寺領) — a 10-koku Kashima Myōjin shrine and a 5-koku Shukurō-ji temple, each with its rice tax — and a total of 1,605 households (戸數) and 7,678 people (人口). Status sub-counts follow for the combined shi–sotsu class (士卒族) at 77 households and 298 people, shizoku (士族, samurai households) at 70 households and 203 people, sotsu (卒, lower retainers), and temples (寺) at 30 with a clergy population of 57. It also gives 18 villages, 4 shrines, 3 Shugendō houses, and a five-person governor's family, with an editorial note that the number of shrines is uncertain and that no warships are recorded.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 8 (Horie)
pages.page_topic: Horie-domain officials roster (fascicle 8), with Honjō military/officer overflow
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page of fascicle 8 (officials and military) opens the Horie-domain (堀江藩) entry at the ○堀江藩 marker and lists its administrators: governor (知事) Ōsawa Motohisa; grand councillors (大參事) Uchida Masao and Kanazawa Iwao; acting grand councillor (權大參事) Hamano Hanzō; junior councillors (少參事) Matsumoto Seiji and Niimura Osada; and acting junior councillor (權少參事) Mase Genroku — Ōsawa being the daimyō later punished for the 1868–71 kokudaka-inflation fraud. Everything to the right of the marker belongs to the preceding domain, Honjō (本荘藩, p.258/141R): three trailing officer-name columns and Honjō's troop counts of 197 gunners (銃士) and 235 rank-and-file (兵卒). The running header names Horie as the fascicle's domain (provenance) and the printed page number is 259. NB: the project MASTER mis-assigned Honjō's two troop counts to Horie and shuffled Horie's council seats; the scan is followed here.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tokushima (徳島藩): assessment and tax revenue
pages.page_topic: Tokushima domain: assessed kokudaka, land-tax (genmai), and cash/product tax revenue (Fascicle 2 civil/fiscal register).
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page opens Tokushima domain's (徳島藩) entry in Fascicle 2 (第二) of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran, headed by the ○徳島藩 domain-boundary marker. It is the fiscal core of the register: an assessed yield (草高) of 442,735 koku, a land tax stated in current-rice terms (現米) of 218,481 koku, an of-which (内) five-year-average figure of 41,675 koku covering the 1864–1868 remissions, and a balance (差引) of 202,840 koku after deductions. Cash and product taxes (諸税諸産物金) come to 28,158 ryō, with a rice-equivalent (此米) of 3,519.725 koku. A marginal note explains that a great flood cut the actual revenue collected to the 26,034-koku figure shown alongside.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Tokushima (徳島藩): demographic totals (shared leaf)
pages.page_topic: Tokushima demographics (shares the Tottori-opening leaf; Tokushima's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens Tottori's entry with the ○ domain-boundary marker and its assessed-yield figure, but the bulk of the page — read right-to-left, to the right of that marker — is the demographic tail of the previous domain sharing the leaf, Tokushima (徳島藩). The Tokushima figures recorded here are a combined rice total (合米) of 206,359.725 koku, 147,510 households (戸數), and a population (人口) of 714,022, split into 363,776 male (男) and 350,246 female (女). Status counts follow — shi–sotsu households (士卒族戸數) at 6,432 with a population of 30,645, shizoku households (士戸數) at 2,100, and sotsu households (卒戸數) at 4,332 — along with Shinto-priest households (社家戸數), temples (寺), temple monks (寺僧) and nuns (寺尼), and one warship (艦). These belong to Tokushima, not Tottori.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tokushima (徳島藩): officials and troops
pages.page_topic: Tokushima domain officials (chiji through gon-shōsanji) and garrison troop count
pages.page_summary_en: This is a single-domain page for Tokushima (○徳島藩) in Fascicle 8, which records domain officials and military strength. The upper band carries the rank headings — governor (知事), acting grand councillor (権大参事) with five men, junior councillor (少参事) with two, and acting junior councillor (権少参事) with two — with the appointee names hung in columns below, beginning with the daimyō-governor Hachisuka Mochiaki. A note records that the names of the councillors below grand-councillor rank were not filed, which is why that rank shows no count. The one military figure given is a garrison of 75 troops (兵隊), a partial return consistent with the incomplete roster.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第三（加知山）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Kajiyama (加知山藩): assessment and demographics
pages.page_topic: Kajiyama domain civil register: land assessment (kokudaka/rice), taxes, households, and population.
pages.page_summary_en: This right half-page opens the entry for Kajiyama domain (加知山藩) in Fascicle 3 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran, marked by the ○加知山藩 domain-boundary marker; the running header reads 藩制一覧表第三（加知山）. The columns record the principal assessment (本高) of 13,969.897 koku, the five-year-average current tax-rice (現米) of 4,560.116 koku, a small reclamation-license rice line, two cash lines in the 永 (ei) unit, and a combined current-rice subtotal (合現米) of 4,620.587 koku. Demographic figures follow: total households (總戸數) of 3,181, a population (人口) of 16,102 split into 8,031 male (男) and 8,071 female (女), and a shrine-priest count (社家) of 16 households and 83 people. The modest totals are consistent with Kajiyama's status as a small (~14,000-koku) domain.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Kajiyama (加知山藩): demographic tail (shared leaf)
pages.page_topic: Kajiyama demographics (shares the Yonezawa-opening leaf; Kajiyama's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens Yonezawa's entry with the ○ domain-boundary marker and its assessed-yield figure, but the bulk of the page — read right-to-left, to the right of that marker — is the demographic tail of the previous domain sharing the leaf, Kajiyama (加知山藩). The Kajiyama figures recorded here cover temple clergy (寺人口, 138 people), Buddhist halls (堂), yamabushi mountain ascetics (山伏, 2 households and 9 people), eta and hinin outcaste households (穢多非人戸數, 13 households and 49 people), shizoku households (士族戸數, 122 households and 417 people), and sotsu (卒族), together with 117 shrines (神社), 30 villages (村數), one rifleman unit (銃兵), and 2 cannon (大砲). These belong to Kajiyama, not Yonezawa.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（加知山）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kajiyama (加知山藩): officials and troops (shared leaf)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and troop strength (fascicle 8: 職員・兵隊) — tail of Kanbe-han followed by the opening of Kaijiyama-han
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 8 page, which records officials and military strength, carries two domains. The upper register completes the entry for the previous domain sharing the leaf, Kanbe (神戸藩, Ise): its councillor ranks (権大参事, 少参事, 権少参事), a garrison of 75 troops (兵隊), and seven appointee names hung below, one seat marked vacant (一員欠). The ○加知山藩 domain-boundary marker then opens the primary domain of this page, Kajiyama, whose own officials follow in the lower register: the governor (知事, no name printed here), a grand councillor (大参事), and two acting grand councillors (権大参事). The running header names 加知山.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Yonezawa (米澤藩): assessment and demographics
pages.page_topic: Yonezawa domain civil register: temple/shrine and status-group population and household counts, villages, riflemen and cannon, and the grass-yield (kusadaka) grand total.
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page belongs to Yonezawa domain (米澤藩), marked by the ○米澤藩 domain-boundary marker and the running header 藩制一覧表第三（米澤）, in Fascicle 3 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran. Read right-to-left, it records temple, shrine, and status-group counts — temple clergy of 138, yamabushi ascetics (山伏), eta and hinin households, shizoku (士族, samurai households) of 122 households and 417 people, sotsu (卒), 117 shrines and 78 temples, and 30 villages — most with an inner male/female (内男/女) breakdown. It also gives the domain's military strength (a rifle platoon of about 70 men and 2 cannon with their artillerymen) and the grand total assessed yield (草高) of 147,248.723 koku, alongside a reclaimed and added-land figure (外込高新田高改出高) of 28,818.872 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Yonezawa (米澤藩): land total and tax yield
pages.page_topic: Yonezawa domain (Fascicle 3), continued: land-total (合高), five-year-average yield (物成) and its rice/purchased-rice/gold components, and the regular- and miscellaneous-tax figures in rice, silver, and coin.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the Fascicle 3 fiscal register for Yonezawa domain (米澤藩); the two ○ markers here open internal sub-sections of Yonezawa's own entry, not a boundary to a neighboring domain. It records the samurai-reclaimed and newly-opened land (諸士開高并新開高, 108,681 koku), the combined land total (合高, 284,748 koku), and the five-year-average tax yield (物成, 85,452 koku), the last broken into a rice component (米, 54,398 koku) and a gold component (金, 70,968 ryō). The tax section gives the regular land tax (正租) as 41,735 koku of rice (正租稅米) plus 556 kan of silver (正租銀), and the miscellaneous tax (雜稅) in rice (2,217 koku), coin (16,408 kan), and silver (191 kan), with purchased rice (買米, 10,445 koku) between the two blocks.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Yonezawa (米澤藩): product taxes and tax totals
pages.page_topic: Yonezawa domain — fascicle-3 product-tax commodities (wax, safflower, cotton, ramie, charcoal), their ryō tax-equivalents, and the summary land-tax totals (regular + miscellaneous tax).
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Yonezawa domain's (米澤藩) Fascicle 3 entry, listing the domain's taxable products alongside their value in tax. Reading right to left, it records the miscellaneous corvée tax (諸役稅, 33,459) and quantities of charcoal (炭, 21,365), safflower (紅花, 264), cotton (綿, 69), blue ramie (靑苧, 14,698), and wax-tree berries (山蠟實, 700, with a village figure of 8,900), each followed by a small-print note converting the commodity into its ryō tax-equivalent. A standalone ○ labeled 取合如上 ("the reckoning is as above") opens the summary block, which gives the five-year-average regular tax (正租) of 41,735 koku of rice and the miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 2,217 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Yonezawa (米澤藩): money taxes and product quantities
pages.page_topic: Yonezawa domain miscellaneous taxes (silver/copper-cash duties) and product-tax quantities (charcoal, ramie, silk floss, safflower, purchased rice, wax berries)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the Fascicle 3 economic register for Yonezawa domain (米澤藩). The right-hand columns give money taxes in silver (銀, 191) and copper-cash (錢, 16,408 kan), followed by a large charcoal (炭) figure of 21,365 kan. An 外 ("besides") divider then introduces a block of product-tax quantities, each with its commodity name at the column foot: purchased rice (買米, 10,445 koku), safflower (紅花, 264), silk floss (眞綿, 69), ramie (青苧, 14,698), and two grades of wax berry (山蠟實 700, 里蠟實 8,900). The block closes with a miscellaneous-duty gold tax (諸役稅金, 33,459).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Yonezawa (米澤藩): population and households
pages.page_topic: Yonezawa domain demographic register: total population with sex split, plus household counts by status group (samurai/sotsu, clergy, outcastes), religious buildings, and a miscellaneous copper-coin tax figure.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf holds the demographic portion of Yonezawa domain's (米澤藩) Fascicle 3 entry. It records a total registered population of 127,277 (人員), split 64,977 male (男) and 62,272 female (女), with sub-populations for samurai households (士族, 15,801 persons / 3,425 households) and lower retainers (卒族, 22,438 persons / 3,308 households). Household and religious-establishment counts follow: 23,440 households (戸數), 361 Shinto shrines (神社), 179 Buddhist halls (佛閣), plus tallies for shrine families (社家, 50), temples (寺院, 434), mountain ascetics (修驗, 219), guild houses (座等, 15), and the outcaste groups eta and hinin (穢多非人, 117). A miscellaneous coin tax (錢) of 25,978 kan 873 mon appears in the far-right column.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Yonezawa (米澤藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials and military establishment of Yonezawa domain (fascicle 8: 職員兵隊)
pages.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page for Yonezawa domain (○米澤藩) from Fascicle 8 of the survey. The top band gives the military strength as 52 troops (兵隊, 五拾貳員) and the administrative ranks: a governor (知事, no count printed), 3 senior councillors (大参事), 3 junior senior councillors (権大参事), and 6 junior councillors (少参事). Below, in the standard two-register layout, ten named appointees hang beneath their rank headings, read right to left: 都筑利義, 大坪誠之, 毛利安積, 千坂嘉遜齋, 新保新, 大瀧新藏, 庄田惣五郎, 三潴清藏, 黒井繁邦, and 小川源太郎. The entire page belongs to Yonezawa; no other domain appears.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Yoshii (吉井藩): tax, households, and population
pages.page_topic: Civil register (kokudaka, tax, households, status-group population, shrines/temples) for Yoshii domain — tail of the record
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf holds the Fascicle 3 civil register for Yoshii domain (吉井藩), a small holding of roughly 10,000 koku in Kōzuke province; the outer-margin running header reads 藩制一覧表第三（吉井）. The record continues from the preceding leaf and shows no ○ boundary marker, so all content here belongs to Yoshii. It records present rice (現米, about 1,982 koku), a combined land-and-miscellaneous tax in gold (金, about 1,390 ryō), 111 households (戸數) split into 81 samurai (士族) and 30 lower-retainer (卒族) households, and a total population (人員) of 111 with the same 81/30 status split. The shrine, temple, village, and troop fields are left blank or marked 不分明 (unclear).

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八 （吉井、高鍋）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Yoshii (吉井藩) and Takanabe (高鍋藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military establishment (fascicle 8): Yoshimi overflow, Yoshii (no data), and Takanabe
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 8 officials-and-military leaf, read right to left, spans three domains. The four rank columns at the far right — 2 junior senior councillors (権大参事), 1 junior councillor (少参事), 1 junior junior councillor (権少参事), and 30 riflemen (銃兵) — sit to the right of the ○吉井藩 marker and belong to the previous domain, Yoshimi (吉見藩), whose entry opened on the facing leaf, not to Yoshii. The ○吉井藩 (Yoshii) heading carries the note 審ナラス ("not investigated"), so Yoshii itself records no counts. The rest of the page is Takanabe (高鍋藩): 2 senior councillors (大参事, appointees 城勇雄 and 黒水鷲郎), 1 junior senior councillor (権大参事, appointee 坂田蒡), and a military of rifle infantry (銃兵) in 5 platoons of 64 plus 1 artillery unit of 54 gunners with 6 cannon (大砲).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Takamatsu (高松藩): land assessment and tax
pages.page_topic: Takamatsu domain land-assessment and tax totals (kokudaka, reclaimed land, regular and miscellaneous tax)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the Fascicle 3 entry for Takamatsu domain (高松藩), marked by the ○ boundary marker before the header ○高松藩. It records the domain's fiscal base: an assessed yield (草高) of 120,000 koku, additional and newly-reclaimed land (込高・新田高改出高) of 85,387 koku, and a grand total (〆) of 205,387 koku. The regular tax (正税) is given as 98,262 koku of rice (正税米) and 9,662 koku of barley (正税麥), with a miscellaneous tax (雜税) of 21,351 ryō and a small vermilion-seal exempt-land (朱印地) figure of 975 koku; a marginal note flags that the following lines were written in vermilion in the original manuscript.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Takamatsu (高松藩): population and households
pages.page_topic: Takamatsu domain population, household, and status-group counts (士族/卒族/平民/寺社/穢多非人) with a residual land figure
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf holds the demographic portion of the Fascicle 3 register for Takamatsu domain (高松藩). It records a total population (人員) of 305,191 and 72,582 households (戸數), broken down by status group: samurai (士族, 701 households / 10,122 persons), lower retainers (卒族, 4,486 households / 17,851 persons), commoners (平民, 63,870), and religious and outcaste groups — 289 Shinto shrines (神社), 347 Buddhist temples (寺院), shrine families (社家, 204), mountain ascetics (修驗, 121), and the outcaste groups eta (穢多, 930 households) and hinin (非人, 346 households). The rightmost column carries a tax-exempt-land (除地) figure of 2,696 koku, and the five-year-average yield is noted as undetermined (五ヶ年平均高不詳).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Takamatsu (高松藩): population by status and military
pages.page_topic: Takamatsu domain population-by-status counts (commoners, Shinto/Buddhist clergy, outcaste groups, with male/female splits) and the domain's 1870 military establishment.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the Fascicle 3 civil register for Takamatsu domain (高松藩), giving by-status population counts with male/female splits: commoners (平民) 268,238 (男 138,798 / 女 129,440), shrine households (社家) 1,016, Buddhist clergy (僧) 1,711, nuns (尼) 4, eta (穢多) 4,293, and hinin (非人) 1,479. It then records the domain's military establishment as surveyed in the 11th month of 1870: a total of 2,153 troops, itemized by rank and type, together with 40 platoons of infantry and 4 artillery companies of 8 boat-guns each. All data on this leaf belong to Takamatsu; no domain boundary appears.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Takamatsu (高松藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Takamatsu domain officials (governor and councillors) and military strength (infantry and artillery)
pages.page_summary_en: This page opens the Takamatsu domain (○高松藩, Sanuki province) entry in Fascicle 8, the survey's roster of officials (職員) and troops (兵隊). It heads the domain with the governor (知事, whose name is not printed here) and the councillor ranks: five senior and acting-senior grand councillors (正權大參事) and eight senior and acting-junior lesser councillors (正權少參事), of which five posts are filled and three vacant. The military lines record an infantry (步兵) of 40 platoons at 40 men each — about 1,600 men — and an artillery (砲兵) of 4 companies. Seven named appointees, from Ōkubo Kanō through Sakuma Kumazō, hang in columns below; only Takamatsu appears on this leaf.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第三 （曾我野）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Sogano (曾我野藩): population, households, and status groups
pages.page_topic: Sogano domain population, household, and status-group totals with a two-province combined tax figure (Fascicle 3 civil register).
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page is a totals page from the civil register (Fascicle 3) of the small Sogano domain (曾我野藩); it continues the entry and carries no ○ domain-boundary marker of its own. It records an aggregate population (人員) of 10,612 in 1,794 households (戸數) and a two-province combined assessed yield (草高) of 3,000.412 koku. The population is broken out by status group: 170 samurai (士, 69 households), 99 lower retainers (卒, 28 households), 10,235 commoners (平民), 6 nobles (華族), 61 outcasts (非人), and no eta (穢多), alongside 72 Shinto shrines (神社), 29 Buddhist clergy (僧), and 12 shrine officiants (社務人). A troop figure (兵隊) of 166 is also given.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Tsu (津藩): land assessment and tax
pages.page_topic: Tsu domain (津藩) landholding, tax, and revenue register from the 1870 Hansei Ichiran civil fascicle 4.
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page carries the complete land-and-tax entry for Tsu domain (○津藩), the seat of the Tōdō house in Ise, in Fascicle 4 of the survey. It records a nominal assessed yield (草高) of 299,334.818 koku and a higher total yield inclusive of newly opened fields (高) of 323,950.002 koku, from which a portion is split off to the Hisai (久居) sub-domain, leaving a residual (殘而) of 270,950.002 koku. The tax figures follow: a regular land tax (正税) of 124,906.121 koku given as a five-year rice average (Rat through Dragon years), a miscellaneous tax (雑税) of 1,544.981 koku, and a small monetary levy in gold (金).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Tsu (津藩): revenue, households, and population
pages.page_topic: Tsu domain civil data (fascicle 4): revenue totals, kokudaka accounting, population, households, and status-class counts with male/female splits
