pages.page_summary_en: This is the right half of the Fascicle 4 civil spread for Tsu domain (津藩, Ise province); no new ○ marker opens here, so every column continues Tsu's own record. The fiscal cluster gives a combined rice total (合米) of 126,451.102 koku, a gold-to-rice conversion (此米) of 87.512 koku, and their grand total (合) of 126,538.614 koku. The demographic cluster records 52,513 households (戸數) and a total population (人口) of 247,682, broken out by status class: 7,917 samurai (士族), 6,889 rural samurai (郷士族), 1,956 lower retainers (卒族), 28 imperial-tomb keepers (御陵守), 698 shrine officiants (社務人), and 1,336 Buddhist clergy (僧).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Tsu (津藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials and military (fascicle 9): Tsu domain personnel counts and appointee roster, with Sonobe overflow
pages.page_summary_en: This page opens the Tsu domain (○津藩) entry in Fascicle 9, the survey's roster of officials and military. It records Tsu's personnel and troop counts: 197 military-administration officials (兵制諸官員), a samurai corps (士隊) of 563, locally-settled soldiers (土著之兵士) numbering 971, 1,334 infantry privates (兵卒), and 48 reserve troops (豫備兵). Below, the appointee roster names councillors of the ruling Tōdō house and their deputies. The troop figure of 166 and the three names printed to the right of the ○津藩 marker belong to the preceding domain, Sonobe (園部藩), which shares this leaf — not to Tsu.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第五 （谷地・松江）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Yachi (谷地藩) and the opening of Matsue (松江藩)
pages.page_topic: Civil-register (F5) tail of Yachi domain and the opening kokudaka block of the neighbouring Matsue domain — a two-domain boundary half-page.
pages.page_summary_en: This is a boundary half-page in the civil register (Fascicle 5) that carries two domains. Most of the columns close out Yachi domain (○谷地藩): 85 temple and hermitage residents (寺庵寮), 132 shrines (神社), 4 districts (郡), 53 villages (村), 52 households (戸數), and a samurai-and-retainer population (士卒) of 150 (83 men, 67 women); its assessed yield is noted as undetermined because Yachi is an internal sub-portion of the parent house. At the left the next domain begins with the ○松江藩 marker, opening Matsue with a nominal assessed yield (草高) of 245,341.159 koku, from which 65,331.391 koku is deducted as a loss allowance.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Matsue (松江藩): tax and revenue
pages.page_topic: Matsue domain's tax and revenue totals (land tax, miscellaneous tax, shrine/temple lands, transit dues) plus the household count
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left half of Matsue domain's fiscal entry in the civil register (Fascicle 5), continuing from the facing page. It records the domain's tax accounts in koku: a gross land-tax figure (正) of 180,009.768 koku, of which 5,155.555 koku is newly reclaimed land (新田); a regular land tax (正税) of 104,657.636 koku; a miscellaneous tax (雑税) of 19,581.039 koku; and their combined total (合) of 124,238.675 koku. Shrine and temple lands (社寺領) come to 6,940.816 koku (1,134.289 shrine, 5,806.527 temple). The page also gives 67,944 households (家數) and separately levied transit and commercial dues (諸運上) of 59,768.5 ryō.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Matsue (松江藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (san'ji ranks) and military establishment
pages.page_summary_en: This page from Fascicle 9 gives the officials and military establishment of Matsue domain (松江藩, the Matsudaira house of Izumo). Below the governor it lists the councillor ranks with the number filled: senior councillors (大参事) 2 posts, 1 filled; deputy senior councillors (権大参事) 5 posts, 4 filled; and junior councillors (少参事) 4 posts, 3 filled — with eight appointees named in columns beneath. The military side records an infantry (歩兵) of 40 platoons at 25 men each, an artillery (砲兵) of 4 batteries plus 34 men, a cavalry (騎兵) of 1 platoon of 24 horsemen, and a grand total of 1,850 troops (兵員), with no warships but two transport vessels of 1,460- and 1,400-koku capacity. This is a continuation leaf, so no ○ marker appears; the domain is named in the running header.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Fukuoka (福岡藩): population, status groups, and kokudaka
pages.page_topic: Fukuoka domain (福岡藩) civil register: population by status, villages, kokudaka
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page opens the Fukuoka domain (○福岡藩) entry in the civil register (Fascicle 5). It records a population of 12,805 broken down by sex, together with the status-group populations: 507 samurai (士族), 365 lower retainers (卒族), 139 shrine households (社家), 39 temple residents (寺), and 65 outcasts (穢多), each with a male/female sub-count. The page also gives 29 villages, notes that the governor's family and warships are not recorded (不記), and states the assessed yield (草高) of 473,100 koku plus a newly reclaimed-field yield (新田高) of 98,041 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Fukuoka (福岡藩): taxes, households, and population
pages.page_topic: Fukuoka domain: aggregate kokudaka, land/miscellaneous taxes (rice, soybeans, silver, copper cash), household counts by status class, and total population with male/female split.
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left half of Fukuoka domain's entry in the civil register (Fascicle 5). The fiscal columns give a combined assessed yield (合高) of 571,141 koku and the principal land tax (正租) — 206,066 koku of rice, 26,940 koku of soybeans (大豆), and 133,750 monme of silver — plus a miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 128 koku of rice, 271,140 monme of silver, and 41,800 mon of copper cash. The demographic columns record 67,557 households (戸數) by status class — 1,749 samurai (士族), 5,171 lower retainers (卒族), 416 Shinto priests (神職), 772 Buddhist clergy (僧徒), and 3,700 leather-worker outcasts (皮多) — and a total population (人員) of 366,330, split into 185,320 men and 181,010 women.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Fukuoka (福岡藩): population and status groups
pages.page_topic: Fukuoka demographics (shares the Fukui-opening leaf; Fukuoka's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens Fukui's entry in the fifth fascicle (第五), a civil and demographic register, but the bulk of the page — read right-to-left, to the right of the ○福井藩 boundary marker — is the population tail of the preceding domain, Fukuoka (福岡藩). It counts Fukuoka's status groups: 6,769 士族 (samurai households, 3,480 male and 3,289 female), 26,005 卒族 (lower retainers, 14,564 male and 11,441 female), 4,052 神職 (Shinto priests), 1,999 僧徒 (Buddhist clergy), and 21,485 皮多 (kawata leather-worker outcastes). It also notes one Western-rigged working vessel (運用舶). The figures beginning at the ○marker and continuing onto the facing leaf belong to Fukui.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Fukuoka (福岡藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials (權大參事 / 少參事 / 權少參事) and military establishment (three shizoku battalions, seven sotsu battalions, 16-gun artillery corps, grand total 4,272 men, plus one Western-style vessel) — the closing portion of Fukuoka domain's fascicle-9 entry, followed by the ○福井藩 boundary marker opening Fukui.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the closing portion of Fukuoka domain's (福岡藩) entry in the ninth fascicle (第九), which lists domain officials and military strength. The officials block records six 権大参事 (provisional senior councillors), two 少参事 (junior councillors), and two 権少参事 (provisional junior councillors), with the appointees' names hung in two registers beneath each rank. The 兵隊 (troops) section gives three battalions raised from 士族 (samurai households), an artillery corps of sixteen guns, and seven battalions raised from 卒族 (lower retainers), for a grand total (総計) of 4,272 men, together with one Western-style vessel (軍艦). At the bottom left the ○福井藩 boundary marker begins the next domain, Fukui — its own figures start at the marker and run onto the facing leaf, so everything to the right of the marker is Fukuoka's.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Fukui (福井藩): kokudaka and status groups
pages.page_topic: Fukui domain civil register: status-group populations (with male/female splits), shrine/temple land, one Western-style ship, and total kokudaka.
pages.page_summary_en: This right half-page is the opening of Fukui domain's (○福井藩) entry in the fifth fascicle (第五), a civil register. Read right-to-left it gives the status-group head-counts, each split into 男 (male) and 女 (female): 6,769 士族 (samurai households), 26,005 卒族 (lower retainers), 4,052 神職 (Shinto clergy), 1,949 僧徒 (Buddhist clergy), and 21,485 皮多 (kawata outcastes). It further records a total assessed yield (草高) of 336,194.0396 koku, 100 koku of vermilion-seal shrine land (朱印地神社), and 694.919 koku of tax-exempt temple land (除地寺領), notes that the governor's family was not registered (知事家族不記), and lists one Western-style operational vessel (運用舶), its name not given.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Fukui (福井藩): taxes, produce, and households
pages.page_topic: Fukui domain civil register: land-tax totals (main/misc/grand-total current rice), product-tax items, and household counts by status group.
pages.page_summary_en: This left half-page continues Fukui domain's (福井藩) entry in the fifth fascicle (第五). The tax columns are given in 現米 (current rice): a principal land tax (正租) of 109,414.8966 koku, a miscellaneous tax (雑税) of 3,221.9277 koku, and their combined total (都合) of 112,636.8245 koku, followed by product levies on 奉書紙 (fine official mulberry paper, 230,000 sheets), 切石砥石 (cut stone and whetstones), 午房種 (burdock seed), and 鎌幷菜切 (sickles and vegetable knives). The household section gives 66,384 total 戸數 (households), broken down by status: 887 士族 (samurai), 1,439 卒 (lower retainers), and small counts of shrine and temple households — 28 社家 (shrine-priest families), 638 寺 (temples), 22 山伏 (mountain ascetics), 81 道場 (training halls), 66 庵 (hermitages) — plus 46 穢多 and 130 非人 (outcaste groups). This is a single-domain leaf, with no boundary marker.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Fukui (福井藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (governor and councilors) and military strength for Fukui han
pages.page_summary_en: This is an officials-and-military page from the ninth fascicle (第九) for Fukui domain (福井藩), whose head is a member of the Matsudaira (松平) family. The appointment roster records one 知事 (governor) and the councillor grades below him — 4 大参事 (senior councillors), 3 権大参事 (provisional senior councillors), and 5 少参事 (junior councillors) — with the appointees' names set in two horizontal registers under each heading. At the left the 兵隊 (military) block gives Fukui's forces as 11 infantry companies totalling 737 men (歩兵) and one artillery unit of 53 men (砲兵).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Mito (水戸藩): boundary leaf with Yunagaya census
pages.page_topic: Boundary page: end of Yunagaya-domain civil census (temples, outcastes, total population with sex split, priests, ascetics, monks, nobility, shrines, soldiers) followed by the ○Mito domain marker and Mito's 350,000-koku headline kokudaka.
pages.page_summary_en: This right half-page in the seventh fascicle (第七) is the boundary leaf where Mito domain's (水戸藩) entry begins: the ○水戸藩 marker sits near the left edge, and Mito's headline assessment of 高三拾五萬石 — a kokudaka (assessed yield) of 350,000 koku — begins there and continues onto the facing leaf. Read right-to-left, all the census columns to the right of the ○marker belong to the preceding domain, Yunagaya (湯長谷藩), a small Iwaki domain whose entry began on the prior leaf. Those figures record 46 寺 (temples), 5 行屋 (ascetic lodges), 115 穢多 (outcaste houses), a total registered population of 7,766 (3,931 male and 3,835 female), 38 社家 (shrine-priest families), 6 修験 (Shugendō ascetics), 29 僧 (monks), 5 華族 (nobility, 2 male and 3 female), 6 社 (shrines), and 72 兵員 (soldiers).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Mito (水戸藩): land assessment and taxes
pages.page_topic: Mito domain assessed koku (kokudaka), land totals, and tax receipts split between Hitachi and Shimotsuke provinces
pages.page_summary_en: This left half-page covers Mito domain (水戸藩) in the seventh fascicle (第七), recording its land assessment and tax receipts across two provinces. The current assessed yield (當高) of the main Hitachi (常陸) holding is 325,606.037 koku including new fields, of which 20,000 koku was administered by the sub-fief steward Nakayama Bitchū-no-kami; the Shimotsuke (下野) portion adds 18,652.845 koku. Related figures give a base assessment (高) of 297,875.297 koku, new-field additions (新田高) of 9,077.895 koku, and an aggregate holding (合高) of 306,953.192 koku. The tax columns record principal land tax as 42,805.909 koku of rice (正租米) and 28,297 ryō of cash (正租金), while the miscellaneous-tax block (雑税納高) breaks out 3,148.06 koku of 稗 (barnyard millet) alongside separate cash and rice sums for Hitachi and Shimotsuke.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran (Survey of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 7 (Mito)
pages.page_topic: Mito demographics, religious institutions, status groups, retainers and troops
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf (printed page 116) carries the tail of Mito domain's fascicle-7 civil register, opening with the remaining miscellaneous taxes — 144.493 koku in barnyard millet and 332 ryō 2 bu plus 204 mon in cash — before turning to the demographic block. Mito reports 43,475 households and a population of 254,877 (129,374 male, 125,503 female) across 478 villages, alongside 465 shrines staffed by 2,047 shrine personnel and 208 temples housing 773 monastic residents. The two outcaste status groups are enumerated separately, 655 eta (359 male, 296 female) and 710 hinin (387 male, 330 female); the hinin total carries a printed 「マヽ」 sic-note because the source's own male/female split sums to 717, not 710. The leaf closes with 6,559 domain retainers and 3,815 troops, followed by a two-line addendum written in vermilion in the original manuscript recording 1,362.98 koku of shrine land held outside the village assessment.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hikone (彦根藩): kokudaka and tax revenue
pages.page_topic: Hikone domain land assessment, tax revenue (rice, gold, copper-cash), and totals
pages.page_summary_en: This right half-page opens Hikone domain's (彦根藩) entry in the seventh fascicle (第七), a fiscal register, marked by the ○彦根藩 boundary marker with a base assessment (本高) of 200,000 koku noted beside it. It records a gross assessed total (惣高) of 203,887.99 koku including new-field re-surveys, then the tax revenues: principal land tax (正租) of 83,026.042642 koku of rice and 2,248 ryō of gold, and miscellaneous taxes (雑税) of 10,562.823156 koku of rice, 348 ryō of gold, and 9,319.0975 kan of copper cash. Combined totals (合計) and a current-rice figure (現米) of 94,030.0263938 koku close the block. A marginal note dates ten of the lines to the first month of 1871 and records that the governor's family was not registered (知事家族不記).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hikone (彦根藩): itemized taxes and temple land
pages.page_topic: Hikone domain fiscal register (fascicle 7): continuation of the tax-revenue itemization (內譯), giving the principal land-tax rice and cash, miscellaneous-tax rice and cash, cash coin (錢), and a supplementary block for shrine/temple vermillion-seal land (社寺領朱印地) in Ōmi, Musashi and Shimotsuke provinces.
pages.page_summary_en: This left half-page continues Hikone domain's (彦根藩) fiscal register in the seventh fascicle (第七) under the heading 内訳 (itemized breakdown). The main columns give the principal land tax in rice (正租米) of 83,026.042642 koku and gold (金) of 2,248 ryō, the miscellaneous tax in rice (雑税米) of 20,562.823156 koku and gold of 348 ryō, and 9,319.0975 kan of copper coin (銭). A separate block for shrine- and temple-held vermilion-seal land (社寺領朱印地), spread across Ōmi, Musashi, and Shimotsuke provinces, records an assessed yield (高) of 1,660.10575 koku, its rice equivalent (此米) of about 441 koku, its cash equivalent (此金) of 931 ryō, and an actual yield (物成米) of 729.21652 koku, with a marginal note of forest in three places and 2 tan of dry field.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hikone (彦根藩): produce taxes and temple land
pages.page_topic: Tail of Hikone's fiscal register: miscellaneous produce/grain taxes (barley, soybean, hulled rice, millet), the copper-cash and eiraku-money miscellaneous levy, plus a marginal shrine/temple-land (社寺領) supplementary listing with its combined-provinces kusadaka and a note that the yield equals the main-text total.
pages.page_summary_en: This right half-page closes Hikone domain's (彦根藩) fiscal register in the seventh fascicle (第七). Read right-to-left, the main columns record the domain's miscellaneous produce and grain taxes: a copper-cash levy (銭) of about 33,979 mon and an eiraku-money charge, together with small grain dues of 籾 (hulled rice, 40.13004 koku), 稗 (barnyard millet, 13.7158 koku), 大豆 (soybean, 6.54341 koku), and 麦 (barley, 15.8678 koku). A parenthetical note flags the following seven lines as a separate shrine-and-temple-land survey (社寺領) entered in the original margin: these give a combined assessed yield (草高) of about 1,660 koku across the three provinces of Ōmi, Musashi, and Shimotsuke, along with small entries for forest (山林) in three places and a yield reconciliation.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hikone (彦根藩): households and population
pages.page_topic: Hikone domain household and population register: total households, samurai/soldier/temple/shrine/outcaste household counts, and total population with status and male/female breakdowns.
pages.page_summary_en: This is the demographic register (Fascicle 7) for Hikone (彦根藩), the Ii family's domain in Ōmi province. The right-hand block records 42,145 households (戸數), broken down by status: 817 upper-rank samurai (上等士族), 434 lower-rank samurai (下等士族), 2,707 sotsu or lower-retainer households (卒族), 115 shrine-priest families (社家), 498 Buddhist temples (寺), and small outcaste counts (48 hinin 非人 and 897 eta 穢多). The left-hand block gives a total population (人口) of 177,518 persons — 88,216 male (男) and 89,302 female (女) — itemized by status, including 5,066 upper samurai, 1,542 lower samurai, 6,494 sotsu, 222 shrine attendants (社人), and 2,129 Buddhist clergy (寺侶).

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Hikone)
pages.page_topic: Hikone domain — civil and fiscal returns (households, land tax, kokudaka, population)
pages.page_summary_en: A continuation page for Hikone domain (彦根藩) in fascicle 7, covering the domain's directly-held territory (御領リ地). It records 5,078 households (of which 36 are dōjō / training halls), an assessed gross yield (草高) of 34,278.92 koku, regular land tax of 10,232.56445 koku and miscellaneous tax of 1,496.4262 koku in rice (combined rice total 11,728.9907 koku), and cash taxes of 32.1875 + 64.125 ryō combining to 96.375 ryō. It also lists the governor's household (10 persons: 3 male, 7 female) and an eta population of 5,407 (2,708 male, 2,699 female). Shrines are entered only as a territorial notation, with 3 shrine-buildings (identity uncertain) and 88 temples noted separately.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Hikone (彦根藩): officials and military, opening of Hirado (平戸藩)
pages.page_topic: officials and military (fascicle 9): tail of Hikone's officials roster and military figures, plus the opening of Hirado
pages.page_summary_en: This officials-and-military page (Fascicle 9) reads right to left and carries two domains. Most of the leaf belongs to Hikone (彦根藩): a short military tail continuing from the facing page (infantry and artillery units, 砲兵) followed by Hikone's roster of councillors, arranged under four rank headings — 大参事 (senior councillor), 権大参事 (junior senior councillor), 少参事, and 権少参事 — each topping a column of named appointees. The ○平戸藩 boundary marker (○ marks the start of a new domain) then opens Hirado (平戸藩), given here only as counts — 2 大参事, 5 権大参事, and 1 公議人 (assembly delegate) — before its entry continues on the next page. Everything to the right of the ○平戸藩 marker is Hikone, not Hirado.

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions (Hansei ichiran), Table 7 (Hitotsubashi)
pages.page_topic: Hitotsubashi domain: assessed yield, land and miscellaneous taxes, cash levies, population and households
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf is the fascicle-7 (藩制一覧表第七) data block for Hitotsubashi domain (一橋藩). It records a total assessed yield (合高) of 119,428.62958 koku plus 613.241 koku of newly-opened paddy (新田高), followed by five-year-average tax figures: a main land tax of 40,082.4818 koku of rice together with its 2,444.96396-kan cash (永) portion, and miscellaneous levies of 1,310.8015 koku (諸税米), 33.693 koku soybeans, 14.3466 koku perilla, 363 ryō in gold, a second eisen entry of 619.34835 kan, and 111.6 kan of copper cash. The domain's population is 115,228 (58,381 male, 56,847 female) living in 25,705 households. The page carries the printed page number 197.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Administration Overview (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 (Hitotsubashi)
pages.page_topic: Revised household & population census, Hitotsubashi domain
pages.page_summary_en: A demographic addendum leaf for 一橋藩 (Hitotsubashi) from fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran. Per a marginal vermilion note copied from an attached slip (掛ヶ紙), it records the revised commoner counts (23,570 households; 106,251 persons) alongside the samurai (士族: 1,217 households / 5,154 persons), foot-soldier (卒族: 447 / 1,154) and Shinto-priest (神職: 74 / 316) populations. These combine into grand totals (總合) of 25,234 households and 112,559 persons (男 57,075 / 女 55,488), excluding the priests. The page carries no maru-marker and belongs entirely to Hitotsubashi.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Survey, Fascicle 7 (Hitotsubashi)
pages.page_topic: Religious institutions and outcaste/marginal-status population counts
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the Hitotsubashi (一橋藩) demographic tables of the Hansei Ichiran (Fascicle 7), enumerating religious institutions and hereditary marginal-status ("senmin") groups. It records 470 Buddhist temples (3 on tax-exempt land) housing 668 people (22 on exempt land), and 139 halls/hermitages housing 12 people. It then breaks out outcaste-group households and populations: eta 1,119 households / 6,105 people (3,101 male, 3,004 female); chasen 46 households / 205 people; onbō (crematory workers) 17 households / 67 people; and ban-hinin (guard-hinin) 30 households / 130 people. A vermilion editorial note flags the following lines as marginal annotations transcribed from an affixed paper slip. Printed page 199.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hitotsubashi (一橋藩) tail, opening of Morioka (盛岡藩)
pages.page_topic: Civil register (fascicle 7): tail of Hitotsubashi domain's temple/shrine/village counts, then the ○Morioka boundary marker and Morioka's kokudaka.
pages.page_summary_en: This civil-register half-page (Fascicle 7) sits on a domain boundary and reads right to left. Most of the leaf completes the demographic and religious tally of Hitotsubashi (一橋藩), whose entry runs off the preceding pages: 311 Shinto priests (神職), 452 Buddhist temples (寺院) plus a few on tax-exempt land (除地), 703 shrines (神社), 320 villages (村數), 123 halls and hermitages (堂庵), and notes that the governor's family is not recorded and that there are no warships. The ○盛岡藩 boundary marker (○ marks the start of a new domain) then opens Morioka, the Nanbu family's domain, whose only figure here is its assessed yield (草高) of 130,000 koku; Morioka's remaining data continue on the following pages.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Morioka (盛岡藩): assessed yield, land tax, and product taxes
pages.page_topic: Morioka domain kokudaka, land-tax and miscellaneous-tax revenue (rice, soybeans, gold, cash), and product taxes (hinoki boards, charcoal).
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fiscal opening (Fascicle 7) for Morioka (盛岡藩), the Nanbu family's domain in the northeast; there is no ○ boundary marker here, so the whole leaf is Morioka. It records a combined assessed yield (合高) of 160,923.932 koku — including a 516.286-koku internal write-off for flood and waste land and a 30,923.932-koku newly reclaimed increment (新田改出) — and then the regular land tax (正租) in rice (69,927.04 koku), soybeans (大豆, 1,623.93 koku), gold, and cash. It also lists a miscellaneous tax (雜稅) in gold and cash and product taxes in cypress boards (檜柾, 180,000 sheets) and charcoal (炭, 420 bales). A marginal note explains that in the Tora and Tatsu years a five-year fixed-exemption average was applied because of crop failure.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Morioka (盛岡藩) population, opening of Mori (森藩)
pages.page_topic: 人口 (population / demographics), plus opening kokudaka and land-tax columns of the next domain
pages.page_summary_en: This civil half-page (Fascicle 7, demographic register) carries two domains, split by the ○森藩 boundary marker (○ marks the start of a new domain) at center. The columns to the right of the marker complete Morioka's (盛岡藩) demographics: a total population (人口) of 117,527 — 61,314 male and 56,213 female — plus its eta (穢多) counts (31 households, 189 persons) and a directly administered-land tally of 24,515 households, all under a 'not surveyed in detail' notation. To the left of the marker begin the fiscal figures of neighbouring Mori (森藩): an assessed yield (草高) of 12,500 koku, an additional 1,774.64306 koku, a combined total (合高) of 14,274.64306 koku, and land-tax rice (正租米) of 5,165.59044 koku averaged over 1864–1868.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Morioka (盛岡藩): officials and troops, Hitotsubashi (一橋藩) overflow
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (councillor ranks) and troop strength, fascicle 9
pages.page_summary_en: This officials-and-military page (Fascicle 9) carries two domains. The ○盛岡藩 boundary marker (○ marks the start of a new domain) opens Morioka near the center: everything to its left is Morioka's data. Morioka records its councillor establishment — 1 大参事 (senior councillor), 2 権大参事, 7 少参事, and 11 権少参事 — but declines to state its troop strength, printing instead a note that the 兵隊 (troops) are to be investigated and reported at a later date. The columns to the right of the marker belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Hitotsubashi (一橋藩), whose officials overflow from the facing page: its 703 soldiers (兵士), an assembly delegate (公議人), and a full roster of ten senior administrators (参政).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Izuhara / Tsushima (嚴原藩): land-tax revenue
pages.page_topic: Annual land-tax revenue of Izuhara (Tsushima) domain: rice, converted-rice, and cash valuations
pages.page_summary_en: This is an opening page of Fascicle 1 for Izuhara, the Sō family's domain on Tsushima (嚴原藩), its header stamped with an Imperial Library seal (帝國圖書館藏書). The page reports the domain's annual land tax: a rice (米) figure of 337.848 koku and a converted-rice subtotal of 26,799.187 koku, given as a five-year average of the tax across the domain's holdings on the Kyushu mainland, together with three cash valuations in gold (金) — 43,311, 11,172, and roughly 13,337 ryō. Interlinear notes value the domain's barley (麥, 7,218.597 koku) and mainland soybeans (大豆, 1,862.1198 koku) at a reckoning of about 6.5 ryō per koku. No assessed yield (草高) figure is printed in this Fascicle-1 register.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Izuhara / Tsushima (嚴原藩): fiscal totals and Korea-trade goods
pages.page_topic: Tsushima (Izuhara) domain fiscal totals and the opening of its Korea public-trade goods list
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the Izuhara / Tsushima (嚴原藩) entry in Fascicle 1, giving the domain's fiscal totals. It records grand totals (都合) of 27,137 koku of rice and 64,822 ryō of cash, followed by an itemized breakdown (内) of the components — rice, cash, barley (麥), and soybeans (大豆), each with a cash-equivalent conversion — drawn from a five-year average of miscellaneous taxes collected in the domain's Kyushu jurisdiction. Below are a net shortfall in actual rice (差引不足 現米, 6,727 koku) and a cash surplus (金, 3,437 ryō). The lower-left opens the ○公貿易 heading, beginning the register of goods received each year from Korea through the official trade, starting with white rice (白米, 16,620 bales).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Izuhara / Tsushima (嚴原藩): Korea-trade commodities
pages.page_topic: Tsushima (Izuhara) domain — Korea-trade commodities and their rice/silver conversion values (continuation)
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page continues Izuhara / Tsushima's (嚴原藩) account of goods received each year through the official Korea trade (公貿易 with Chosŏn), begun on the facing page. Rather than a household or land register, it is a commodity ledger: each line is a traded good with a quantity and, for the major items, a silver or copper-cash conversion value and a small inline exchange-rate note. The goods listed include kōboku tribute cotton (公木, 33,245 bolts), soybeans (大豆) and azuki beans (小豆), kudzu and hagi-bark ropes, bent nails, folded floss, large straw mats, and raw ramie, along with rice subtotals for goods exchanged for rice. There is no ○ boundary marker on this leaf — all of it is Tsushima.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Izuhara / Tsushima (嚴原藩): Korea-trade imports
pages.page_topic: Tsushima Korea-trade imports: itemized list of goods received from Korea with silver-equivalent valuations
pages.page_summary_en: This is a further page of the Izuhara / Tsushima (嚴原藩) entry in Fascicle 1, listing goods received each year from Korea through the domain's official trade (公貿易). Each line names a commodity, its quantity, and an equivalent value (代) in silver monme (匁) with a per-unit conversion rate. The items shown here include ginseng (人參), tiger and leopard pelts (虎皮・豹皮), white cloth, pongee, and cotton, oiled cloth, writing brushes and ink sticks, split stakes and boards, sail matting, large bamboo, and straw; a summary line values eleven of the miscellaneous articles (十一品) at about 3,652.5 monme of silver. There is no ○ boundary marker on this leaf — all of it is Tsushima.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Tsushima/Izuhara (嚴原藩): Korea-trade goods and their silver values
pages.page_topic: Tsushima (Izuhara) domain — continuation of the Korea-trade (公貿易) commodity list: itemized goods received annually from Chosŏn with their silver-equivalent (代銀) valuations, plus grand-total and two internal subtotals.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Tsushima (Izuhara) domain's trade register in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran, listing the goods received each year through the domain's 公貿易 (official trade with Korea). Read right to left, each column names a commodity — wax-coated wrappers, cloth packs, oiled and hat paper, oil, walnuts, pine nuts, dried chestnuts, jujubes, and figured mats — paired with its 代銀 (silver-equivalent value) and per-unit conversion notes. The final columns give a grand total silver equivalent of about 14,692,657 monme together with two 内 (of-which) subtotals. Because the page tallies only goods and their monetary value, it carries no population figures or land assessment.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Tsushima/Izuhara (嚴原藩): traded commodities and appraised values
pages.page_topic: Products / trade goods (産物) register for Izuhara (Tsushima) domain — continuation listing commodities with quantities and appraised values (代)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf belongs to Tsushima (Izuhara) domain's trade register in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran, listing commodities each with a quantity and an appraised silver value (代). Entries include white rice (about 6,393 bales), pepper (3,100 kin), sappanwood dyewood (7,005 kin), alum, Japanese vermilion, and patterned paper (1,800 sheets), followed by finished luxury goods — maki-e lacquered mirrors, trays, and inkstone boxes, a portable field bath, and a small gold folding screen. A short inset note explains that the accompanying silver and rice cover the costs of escorting shipwrecked drifters, staffing the Korean checkpoint, and other official-trade sundries.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Tsushima/Izuhara (嚴原藩): copper imports from the Korea trade
pages.page_topic: Tsushima official Korea-trade (kōbōeki) copper imports: silver-value prices and quantities, with an explanatory note on the abolished copper guild
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Tsushima (Izuhara) domain's trade register in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran, itemizing the copper obtained through the domain's 公貿易 (official trade with Korea). Each entry pairs a silver value in kan-monme with a copper product and quantity: a nested copper wash-basin set, 荒銅 (crude copper) of 26,900 kin, and three grades of 吹銅 (refined copper) — 11,000 kin, 6,500 kin, and 3,629 kin. Interlinear notes explain the freight and expense reckoning and record gifts allotted to the Korean interpreter-officials; a further memorandum notes that the former mountain-works and copper-guild purchasing arrangements had been abolished, upsetting the domain's copper-trade projections. Two grand totals in cash close the page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Tsushima/Izuhara (嚴原藩): Wakan and checkpoint expenses
pages.page_topic: Tsushima (Izuhara) domain sundry expenditures: Wakan-and-two-checkpoints expense block, itemized rice/cash breakdown, and the opening of the drifted-persons relief expense item
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Tsushima (Izuhara) domain's expense accounts in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran. It records the ○和館兩關所入費 block — the running costs of the Wakan (the domain's Japanese trading factory at Pusan in Korea) together with its two barrier checkpoints — totaling 56,618 ryō in gold plus a small silver remainder, resolved into a rice component of about 819 koku and a cash component of 815 kan. A 此小譯 (breakdown of the above) then itemizes the sub-amounts, with notes explaining that the money covers stipend-rice, brushes, ink, paper, oil, and wax, and the year-round upkeep of officials posted at the checkpoints and the Wakan. At the far left the next item, expenses for shipwrecked drifters and their rice rations, is opened and continues on the facing leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Tsushima/Izuhara (嚴原藩): castaway-relief and repatriation expenses
pages.page_topic: Tsushima domain (嚴原藩): itemized breakdown and explanatory notes for special expenditures on castaway relief and Korea repatriation / Nagasaki ship costs
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Tsushima (Izuhara) domain's expense accounts in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran. Under the heading 此小譯 (the itemized breakdown of this), it records special outlays in rice (米, in koku) and copper cash (錢) tied to the domain's diplomatic role: provisions and shipboard costs for hosting drifting castaways (漂民), collecting them from Nagasaki, and repatriating them by ship to Korea. The total castaway-relief expense comes to about 94 koku of rice and 13,809,074 in cash, with further lines for the Nagasaki pickup, the Korea repatriation, and relief for castaways from other domains. Explanatory notes qualify each pair of figures and cross-reference earlier lines.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八　職員　兵隊
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tsushima/Izuhara (嚴原藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials and military establishment of Izuhara (Tsushima) domain
pages.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page for Tsushima (Izuhara) domain in Fascicle 8 of the Hansei Ichiran, whose ○ domain-boundary marker and columns fill the whole leaf. The upper register prints the standard rank headings in descending order — 知事 (governor), 大参事, 権大参事, 少参事, and 権少参事 — with a note that the appointees' personal names are not recorded here, and the faint name columns hang beneath. The military block gives 兵員 (total troops) of 478 men, 歩兵 (infantry) of 6 platoons, and 砲兵 (artillery) of 2 sub-platoons.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Nishio (西尾藩): land assessment, population, and status groups
pages.page_topic: Civil register: land yield, tax revenue, households, population, and non-commoner status populations (temple/shrine, outcast) for Nishio domain
pages.page_summary_en: This is the civil register for Nishio domain (西尾藩), a Matsudaira domain in Mikawa province, in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran. It records the domain's actual combined tax rice (現合米) of 23,668.8474 koku, its copper-cash and gold tax figures, a 戸數 (household count) of 12,083 houses, and a total 人口 (population) of 52,078, split into 25,327 men and 25,792 women. The lower portion breaks out the non-commoner status groups: temple and hermitage clergy (寺庵, 232 houses, with a nested tally of priests, nuns, mountain ascetics, and lay devotees), the 穢多 outcast group (28 houses, 103 people), the 非人 outcast group (24 houses, 83 people), and 社家 (Shinto shrine households, 24 houses with 147 shrine people).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Nishio (西尾藩): junior councillor ranks
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (shokuin) — assistant-councillor ranks for Nishio han
pages.page_summary_en: This is an officials page for Nishio domain (西尾藩) in Fascicle 8 of the Hansei Ichiran, continuing the roster from the preceding leaf. It carries only the later councillor ranks — 権大参事 (senior provisional councillor), 少参事 (junior councillor), and 権少参事 (junior provisional councillor) — the governor and senior councillor having appeared earlier, so this leaf shows no ○ domain marker and no governor's surname. The 権大参事 rank lists 12 named appointees; 少参事 gives 7, with a note that one man was dismissed and another appointed in the fifth month; and 権少参事 gives 10. No military figures appear on this page.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第一（二本松）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 1 — Nihonmatsu (二本松藩): land assessment and tax revenue
pages.page_topic: Nihonmatsu domain kokudaka, actual-rice tax, cash revenue, and miscellaneous taxes; plus the tail-end demographic/status block of the preceding domain
pages.page_summary_en: This civil register opens the Nihonmatsu domain (二本松藩) entry in Fascicle 1 of the Hansei Ichiran, marked by the ○ domain-boundary marker at ○二本松藩. Nihonmatsu's own figures, to the left of the marker, give a 草高 (assessed yield) of 50,000 koku, an actual-rice figure of 11,839.2381 koku, collected cash revenue (収納金) of 3,949 ryō 1 bu in gold plus about 28 kan in copper, and miscellaneous taxes (諸税金) of 150 ryō 3 bu in gold plus 1,186 kan in copper. Everything to the right of the ○ marker — the village count, samurai and foot-soldier households, and the population with its 士族 (samurai households) and 卒 (foot-soldier) breakdowns — is the closing block of the previous domain sharing this leaf, not Nihonmatsu.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（二本松）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Nihonmatsu (二本松藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials and military (職員兵隊) — Nihonmatsu domain
pages.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page for Nihonmatsu domain (二本松藩) in Fascicle 8 of the Hansei Ichiran, the only domain on the leaf, opened by the ○二本松藩 boundary marker. Reading right to left, the rank headings run from 知事 (governor) down through 大参事 (senior councillor, one person), with the governor Niwa Yoshinari (丹羽至善) named in the lower band and eight further appointees listed for the junior ranks. The military entry records 兵員 不記 (troop count not recorded), with a note explaining that only the cadre from the battalion commander down to the first-rank flank guards — 51 persons — is enumerated, so the domain's full army strength is not disclosed.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Obama (小濱藩): products and miscellaneous tax
pages.page_topic: Obama domain — products/specialty-goods output and miscellaneous tax revenue
pages.page_summary_en: This right half-page belongs to Obama domain (小濱藩) and comes from Fascicle 2 of the survey, which records each domain's economy. Reading right to left, it lists the domain's specialty outputs: 油 (oil) at 1,239.98 koku, 魚漁 (fisheries) valued at 25,469 ryō, 銅 (copper) at 173 units, 石灰 (lime) at 334,737 bales, and 生糸 (raw silk) at about 1,305 kanme, the silk noted as tax-exempt on a five-year average. It then records miscellaneous cash receipts, including a 雜税金 (miscellaneous tax) of 20,696 ryō and a 5,210-ryō toll on freight passing the Tsuruga-road gate (敦賀道之口通荷運上). A far-left column gives the domain's 戸數 (household count) of 23,886.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Obama (小濱藩): population and status groups
pages.page_topic: Obama demographics (shares the Ogaki-opening leaf; Obama's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the entry for the next domain, Ogaki, with its ○ domain-boundary marker and land figures, but the bulk of the page — everything to the right of that marker, read right to left — is the demographic close of the previous domain, Obama (小濱藩). It records a 人口 (population) of 105,957 (52,713 male and 53,244 female), the 士族 (samurai households) at 475 households and 4,237 persons, and the 卒族 (lower-retainer households) at 249 households and 1,975 persons, each with male and female splits. It also counts 484 神社 (Shinto shrines) and 634 寺 (Buddhist temples), with a temple clergy population of 681 men and 272 women plus 12 尼 (nuns).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Ogaki (大垣藩): kokudaka and establishment
pages.page_topic: Ogaki domain (大垣藩): population, status-group households, temples/shrines/ascetics, military establishment, and kokudaka
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 2 civil register opens the entry for Ogaki domain (大垣藩), marked by the ○ domain-boundary marker and annotated with a true assessed yield of 100,000 koku. It records the domain's 草高 (assessed yield) as 131,106.43158 koku, given with notes that it includes newly reclaimed and resurveyed land and is stated as a five-year average. The register also notes Ogaki's military establishment: a two-battalion, English-style army and an eight-gun artillery unit.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Ogaki (大垣藩): tax accounts and population
pages.page_topic: Ogaki domain fiscal register: land-tax rice, miscellaneous-tax rice, cash and silver tax, an editorial ◎ block giving the flood-adjusted average figures, additional received stipend, tax-rice subtotal, household count, and population with a male/female split.
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 2 fiscal page covers Ogaki domain (大垣藩) in Mino province. The right-hand block gives the registered figures: 正租米 (land-tax rice) of 51,069.41 koku, 雜稅米 (miscellaneous-tax rice) of 34.31 koku, and a 金 (cash tax) of 7,161 ryō plus a small amount of 銀 (silver). A double-circle ◎ block to the left restates these as a flood-adjusted average — land-tax rice of 49,392.78 koku — with a note that severe flooding in the Tiger and Dragon years left the earlier figure short. The page also records an 外受領高 (additional received stipend) of 405 koku, identified as land of the Nangū shrine at Miyashiro in Fuwa district, along with 242 家 (households), of which 38 are shrine households, and a 人口 (population) of 979 (466 male, 513 female).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Ogaki (大垣藩): temple-land register
pages.page_topic: Ogaki domain temple-lands register: grants, tax rice, and temple demographics
pages.page_summary_en: This left half-page continues the Fascicle 2 entry for Ogaki domain (大垣藩) with a register of 寺領 (temple landholdings). Reading right to left, it lists four temples — 金蓮寺 (Konren-ji), 妙應寺 (Myōō-ji), 乙津寺 (Ottsu-ji) in Kagashima, and 阿願寺 (Agan-ji) in Higashijima — each with its 受領高 (received grant), the 租税米 (tax rice) levied on it, a household count, and a resident population broken into men, women, and 僧 (monks). Konren-ji, for example, is recorded with a 35-koku grant, 17.37 koku of tax rice, 43 households, and 194 residents; the grants for the other three run from 10 to about 55 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Ogaki (大垣藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Ogaki domain officials (governor and councillors) and military establishment
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 8 page covers the officials and military of Ogaki domain (大垣藩), opened by the ○ domain-boundary marker (○大垣藩). The officials section lists the domain governor (知事, with no appointee named here), one 大参事 (senior councillor, Ōhara Zesui), two 権大参事 (acting senior councillors, Takaoka and Ōhara Susumu), and one 少参事 (junior councillor, Onozaki Kurao), with the appointees' names set in a lower register. The military figures give a 銃隊 (rifle corps) of six platoons totalling 360 men, a 砲隊 (artillery corps) of 8 cannon, and 77 砲臺守衞士 (battery-guard soldiers).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Oshi (忍藩): households and population
pages.page_topic: Oshi domain (Musashi) civil register: currency reserves, household counts by status, temples/shrines, and population by status with male/female splits
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 2 civil register covers Oshi domain (忍藩) in Musashi province. It records the domain's cash reserve of 202 kan and its 銀 (silver) holdings, then breaks the 戸数 (households) — 24,654 in all — into 士族 (samurai) at 458, 卒族 (lower retainers) at 1,180, shrine families at 64, 寺 (temples) at 430, 修験 (Shugendō practitioners) at 10, and the 穢多 and 非人 (outcaste) groups. It then gives a 人口 (total population) of 113,070 (56,907 male, 56,163 female), with separate populations for the samurai, lower-retainer, and shrine-family classes, each split by sex. A few of the printed status figures do not add exactly to their stated totals; these are minor arithmetic inconsistencies carried over from the original.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Oshi (忍藩): status-group populations
pages.page_topic: Oshi demographics (shares the Ozu-opening leaf; Oshi's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the entry for the next domain, Ozu, with its ○ domain-boundary marker and land figures, but most of the page — everything to the right of that marker, read right to left — is the demographic close of the previous domain, Oshi (忍藩). It records the 穢多 (outcaste) population at 2,723 (1,386 male, 1,337 female), the 非人 (outcast) population at 42 (23 male, 19 female), the population on shrine and temple lands at 473 (233 male, 240 female), and the 寺 (temple) population, along with a small governor's household and a shrine tally.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Ozu (大洲藩): land assessment and population
pages.page_topic: Ozu domain civil/economic register: land assessment, troops, governor's household, villages, shrines, and outcaste/religious populations
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 2 civil and economic register opens the entry for Ozu domain (○大洲藩) in Iyo province, with the ○ domain-boundary marker set to the left of all the data columns, so every field to its right belongs to Ozu. It records the domain's 草高 (assessed yield) as roughly 60,906 koku, of which the 内田高 (paddy-field yield) is 36,473.4 koku. The page also gives the domain's 兵隊 (troops) as 14 platoons of about 40 men each, a small governor's household of 3 persons, a shrine count of 2,083, and outcaste populations of 2,723 穢多 (eta) and 42 非人 (hinin), among other village and religious figures.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Ozu (大洲藩): land-tax accounts and households
pages.page_topic: Ozu domain land-tax accounts: dry-field koku, crop yields (rice/soybean/sesame), cash miscellaneous tax, paddy/dry-field breakdown, and samurai-class households and population
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 2 land-and-tax page continues the entry for Ozu domain (大洲藩) in Iyo province. Reading right to left, it records the 畑高 (dry-field assessment) of 24,432.6 koku with its tax-rate note, then a crop-and-cash block of 實米 (actual rice) 25,087.1 koku, 豆 (beans) 11,923 koku, 胡麻 (sesame) 222.1 koku, and a 雜稅金 (miscellaneous cash tax) of 195 ryō. It goes on to a 用高 (allotted yield) of 9,268.9 koku with a Niiya-branch note, a 殘リ用高 (remaining allotted yield) of 51,637.1 koku, and a paddy-versus-dry-field breakdown. The page closes with the 士卒族戸數 (samurai and lower-retainer households) at 1,245 and a 人口 (population) of 5,018 (2,541 male, 2,471 female).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Ozu (大洲藩): population and status classes
pages.page_topic: Ozu domain civil register: households by status class, population totals with male/female splits, plus shrines, temples, and troops
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page continues the civil and demographic register (fascicle 2) for Ozu domain (大洲藩) in Iyo province; the running header 藩制一覧表第二（大洲）confirms the domain, and with no ○ domain-boundary marker on the leaf it carries on from the preceding page. It gives household and population counts by status class — 士族 (samurai) 263 households / 1,130 people, 卒族 (lower retainers) 352 / 1,368, 輕卒 (light foot soldiers) 630 / 2,520 — each with a male/female split, and a whole-domain total of 22,771 households and 93,603 people (男 47,791 / 女 45,812). The sheet also records 921 outcaste (穢多) households, 1,342 shrines (神社), 1,045 temples (寺), and 730 troops (兵隊), with priest and clergy sub-counts noted in the margins.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Ozu (大洲藩) officials and troops; Oshi (忍藩) opening
pages.page_topic: officials_and_military
pages.page_summary_en: This is an officials-and-military page (fascicle 8, 職員兵隊) that carries two domains on one leaf. Reading right to left, the material to the right of the single ○忍藩 (Oshi domain) marker completes Ozu domain (大洲藩): its military establishment — an infantry force of two battalions, one artillery company (大砲一隊), and six cannon (大砲) — together with its named councillors. The columns to the left of the ○忍藩 marker open Oshi's own entry, listing one governor (知事), two senior councillors (大参事), two acting senior councillors (権大参事), and four junior councillors (少参事). The running header reads 忍 and the printed page number in the bottom margin is 二百八十 (280).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Ozu (大洲藩): officials, with previous domain's troops
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (職員) and military establishment (兵隊) — Fascicle 8
pages.page_summary_en: This officials-and-military page (fascicle 8) opens the entry for Ozu domain (大洲藩) at the ○大洲藩 boundary marker. Below the marker are the administrative ranks — 知事 (governor, no name printed here), 大参事 (senior councillor, 2 members: Ōhashi Shigeyuki and Nakamura Toshio) and 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 4 members: Yamamoto Mayumi, Kodama Kiyoshi, Hori Hiroma, and Kumoide Azusa). The military figures printed to the right of the ○大洲藩 marker (roughly fourteen companies of about forty men, one of them artillery) belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, whose own marker fell on the preceding page, not to Ozu. The running header reads 藩制一覧表第八（大洲）and the bottom-margin page number is 二百八十一 (281).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kameyama (龜山藩): population, households, and minor rice levies
pages.page_topic: Kameyama domain civil register: population by status (total / shi-sotsu / shizoku / sotsu with male-female splits), household counts, temples and shrines, and three minor rice transport/land taxes.
pages.page_summary_en: This half-page is the civil register (fascicle 2) for Kameyama domain (龜山藩); the running header at the right margin reads 藩制一覧表第二（龜山）. It records a total population of 41,924 (男 21,093 / 女 20,831) in 8,790 households, of which the samurai-and-foot-soldier segment (士卒) numbers 3,667 people in 726 houses, broken down into 士族 (samurai households) 270 / 1,373 and 卒 (lower retainers) 456 / 2,294. Religious counts are 212 temples (寺, including hermitages) and 33 shrines (神社). Three short columns on the right list minor rice levies (米): a 2-bale dyers' license tax, a 4-bale tax on Wakamatsu incoming-ship wholesalers, and a 4-bale tribute on retainers' fallow upland fields. The bottom-margin page number is 160.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kameyama (龜山藩) tail, on the Kawagoe-opening leaf
pages.page_topic: Kameyama demographics (shares the Kawagoe-opening leaf; Kameyama's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the entry for Kawagoe domain (its ○ marker and land assessment), but the bulk of the page — read right to left, to the right of that marker — is the demographic tail of the previous domain, Kameyama (龜山藩). The Kameyama figures shown here cover its religious and status populations: shrine-priest families (社家) 202 people (男 104 / 女 98), monks and nuns (僧尼) 671 (男 427 / 女 244), 743 shrines (神社), and mountain ascetics (修驗) in 11 households / 40 people, followed by a small military note of 8 troops (兵隊) and 3 cannon-corps officers (大砲隊役員).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kameyama (龜山藩) officials; Kawagoe (川越藩) military
pages.page_topic: Officials (職員) and military strength (兵隊) — fascicle 8; Kawagoe tail + Kameyama officials
pages.page_summary_en: This officials-and-military page (fascicle 8) carries two domains. The ○龜山藩 marker and the officials roster in the main body belong to Kameyama domain (龜山藩): its ranks are 知事 (governor, no name printed here), 大参事 (senior councillor, Kondō Takuzan), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, Katō Tomohiko and Kondō Yukitome), and 少参事 (junior councillor, Hosoki Masayuki). Everything to the right of the ○龜山藩 marker belongs to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Kawagoe (川越藩): five overflow official-name columns and Kawagoe's full military block — an infantry battalion of 360 men (six 60-man platoons), 80 infantry reserves, 30 artillerymen, and a 32-man artillery company. The running header reads 藩制一覧表第八（龜山）and the bottom-margin page number is 308.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kawagoe (川越藩): clergy populations and land assessment
pages.page_topic: Kawagoe domain civil register: clergy/shrine-family populations, military units, and land-tax/kokudaka figures
pages.page_summary_en: This left half-page continues the entry for Kawagoe domain (川越藩) in fascicle 2 (bottom-margin page 161). The right-hand columns record religious and status populations with male/female splits — shrine-priest families (社家) 202 people, monks and nuns (僧尼) 671, shrines (神社) 743, and mountain ascetics (修驗) in 11 households — followed by the domain's military establishment of eight infantry platoons (287 men) and a three-section artillery corps. The ○川越藩 marker heads the fiscal block, which reports 草高 (assessed yield) of 81,562.30 koku, a supplementary 高 of 60,442.51 koku, reclaimed and newly surveyed yield (込高新田改出高) of 21,119.79 koku, the principal land-tax rice (正租米) of 18,213.62 koku, and miscellaneous-tax rice (雜稅米) of 2,733.74 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kawagoe (川越藩): population, temples, villages, and taxes
pages.page_topic: Kawagoe domain civil register: population, households, temples/shrines, villages, outcaste populations, and tax revenue in silver/copper/kan
pages.page_summary_en: This is a continuation page of the civil register (fascicle 2) for Kawagoe domain (川越藩), book page 162; the running header reads 藩制一覧表第二（川越）and there is no ○ domain-boundary marker on the leaf, so all of it belongs to Kawagoe. It records land-tax residuals in cash (永 446 kan), silver (銀 3,105.33 monme), and copper coin (錢 1,952 mon); a total of 11,650 households (戸數) and 57,623 people (人口, 男 28,887 / 女 28,736); shrine-priest households (社家, 44 with a resident population of 173); 142 temples (寺) with 333 resident clergy and 75 unoccupied temples (無住寺); 190 villages (村數); and outcaste populations of 713 (穢多) and 46 (非人), households not separately recorded.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kawagoe (川越藩) tail, on the Kasama-opening leaf
pages.page_topic: Kawagoe demographics (shares the Kasama-opening leaf; Kawagoe's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the entry for Kasama domain (its ○ marker and land assessment), but the bulk of the page — read right to left, to the right of that marker — is the demographic tail of the previous domain, Kawagoe (川越藩). The Kawagoe figures shown here give its samurai and lower-retainer classes: 士族 (samurai households) 571 / 2,447 people (男 1,179 / 女 1,268) and 卒族 (lower retainers) 447 / 1,416 (男 736 / 女 680), followed by a military note of 597 elite troops (精兵) and 212 auxiliary troops (聚合兵).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kawagoe (川越藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (chiji through gon-shōsanji) and military establishment of Kawagoe domain
pages.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page (fascicle 8) for Kawagoe domain (川越藩), opened by its ○川越藩 marker. It lists the administrative ranks — 知事 (governor, heading only, no name printed here), 大参事 (senior councillor, 3), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 3), 少参事 (junior councillor, 2), and 権少参事 (acting junior councillor, the named appointees Norimatsu Shidō and Horie Shinzō) — followed by the military establishment: eight infantry platoons (歩兵, about 320 men), a three-section artillery company (大砲隊), a cannon unit of 98 (砲隊), a rifle corps of 499 (銃隊), and a combined reserve of 210 (聚合隊). A small note in the right margin records a variant reading in which there is no acting junior councillor and the junior councillors instead number three. The running header and page number (三百九 = 309) sit in the outer margin.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kasama (笠間藩): kokudaka and taxes
pages.page_topic: Kasama domain (笠間藩) — fascicle-2 civil register: samurai/soldier households and population (士族・卒族・兵隊), assessed kokudaka (草高), and land + miscellaneous taxes in rice and cash (正租・雜稅).
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf is the Fascicle 2 (第二) civil and fiscal entry for Kasama (笠間藩), a roughly 85,000-koku domain in what is now Ibaraki, opening with its ○ domain-boundary marker. Reading right to left, it records the 士族 (samurai households, 571) and 卒族 (foot-soldier households, 447) with their populations, along with a two-part 兵隊 (troop) count of 597 regular and 212 reserve men. The fiscal columns give an assessed yield 草高 (kokudaka) of 85,310.6648 koku, and, as five-year averages, the 正租 (regular land tax) of 16,273.6368 koku of rice plus 6,596.28 kan in cash, and the 雜稅 (miscellaneous tax) of 553.4329 koku of rice plus 923.73 kan in cash.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kasama (笠間藩): population and households
pages.page_topic: Kasama domain civil register: population, households, temples/shrines, villages, samurai/sotsu and outcaste populations, and rice/currency tax subtotals
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Kasama's (笠間藩) Fascicle 2 civil register, with no ○ domain-boundary marker of its own, so the whole half-page belongs to Kasama. It records a total population of 44,046 (22,800 male, 21,246 female) across 7,425 households in 197 villages, together with 238 Buddhist temples (147 of them uninhabited). It also breaks out the 士族 (samurai households, 310) and 卒族 (foot-soldier households, 443) with a samurai population of 3,255, along with 穢多非人 (outcaste) and 社家 (Shinto-priest) households. A right-hand rice subtotal 右合 of 25,187.8892 koku closes the fiscal columns; the 神社 (shrine) heading is printed but left blank here.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Kasama (笠間藩): military units
pages.page_topic: Kasama domain military establishment (troops by unit) and Shugen (mountain-ascetic) clergy households
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 2 half-page for Kasama (笠間藩) is a military register. Its main block is the 兵隊 (troop) roster, enumerating units by strength: scouts (斥候隊, 120 men), artillery (大砲隊, 50 men plus 16 reserves), sharpshooters (狙擊隊, 120 men plus 18 reserves), volley-fire troops (整發隊, 160 men), and first-, second-, and third-class guard companies (61, 51, and 52 men), for a stated total of 679, with 30 役員 (officials) noted separately. A closing entry records the domain's 修驗 (mountain-ascetic clergy): 35 households and 28 persons (17 male, 11 female).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kasama (笠間藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (councillors) and troop strength of Kasama domain
pages.page_summary_en: This is the Fascicle 8 officials-and-military entry for Kasama (笠間藩), marked by its ○ domain-boundary marker. The top band lists the councillor establishment: 大参事 (senior councillor) 2, 権大参事 (acting senior councillor) 1, 少参事 (junior councillor) 3, and 権少参事 (acting junior councillor) 3, under a 知事 (governor) heading left unfilled here. A note at the right gives the troop strength as 597 line troops (横兵) and 212 reserve troops (聚合兵). Beneath the rank headings hangs a roster of ten named appointees.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Takasaki (高崎藩): kokudaka and taxes
pages.page_topic: Takasaki domain fiscal and military register (kokudaka, land tax, miscellaneous tax, troop strength)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf is the Fascicle 3 civil and economic register for Takasaki (高崎藩). Reading right to left, it opens with a 兵員 (military head-count) block of 240 corps officials, 384 soldiers, and 768 troopers. The ○ domain-boundary marker introduces the land figures: an assessed yield 草高 (kokudaka) of 82,000 koku, a supplementary yield 外高 of 8,573.5401 koku, and a combined total 合高 of 90,573.5401 koku. The lower registers give the 正租 (regular land tax) of 32,653.59 koku of rice plus cash and gold, and the 雜稅 (miscellaneous tax) of 45.93 koku of rice plus smaller cash and gold amounts.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Takasaki (高崎藩): revenue totals and households
pages.page_topic: Takasaki domain — combined revenue totals (合) and household/clergy demographic register (continuation page)
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left continuation of Takasaki's (高崎藩) Fascicle 3 civil register; it carries no ○ domain-boundary marker of its own, since the marker and 知事 (governor) heading sit on the facing leaf. The right-hand columns give the combined revenue total 合 broken into rice (32,699.52 koku), 永 cash, gold, and copper coin, followed by a 産物税 (products tax). The left-hand columns record the demographic register: 20,972 total households, 58 shrines, 330 temples, 1,444 士族 (samurai households), 201 卒族 (foot-soldier households), and smaller counts of shrine families, Buddhist halls, and mountain-ascetic temples. Several entries carry interlinear notes citing the 1870 ninth- and tenth-month surveys.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Takasaki (高崎藩): population by status group
pages.page_topic: Population and household register by status group (Takasaki domain)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Takasaki's (高崎藩) Fascicle 3 status register; it has no ○ domain-boundary marker or 知事 (governor) name, marking it as an interior page. It carries two parallel breakdowns. The persons-by-status register gives a total 人員 (population) of 97,550, with 2,815 士族 (samurai), 1,251 卒族 (foot-soldiers), 91,066 平民 (commoners), and smaller counts of shrine priests, temple clergy, mountain ascetics, and others, most split into male and female subtotals. The households-by-status register records 18,530 commoner households (including 16 that migrate seasonally to Kishū), 11 ferryman households, and 264 穢多 (outcaste) households.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Takasaki (高崎藩) tail, shared with Tatebayashi (館林藩)
pages.page_topic: Takasaki demographics (shares the Tatebayashi-opening leaf; Takasaki's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the entry for Tatebayashi (館林藩) with its ○ domain-boundary marker and kokudaka, but the bulk of the page, read right to left to the right of that marker, is the demographic tail of the previous domain, Takasaki (高崎藩). Those Takasaki figures include 93 villages, 1,287 穢多 (outcaste persons, 693 male and 594 female), and small counts of ferrymen, physicians, mountain ascetics, and others. A 兵員 (military strength) figure of 735 also appears in the header column.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Takasaki (高崎藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: officials_and_military
pages.page_summary_en: This is the Fascicle 8 officials-and-military entry for Takasaki (高崎藩), the single domain on the leaf, marked by its ○ domain-boundary marker. The 兵員 (military strength) is given in two figures, 384 and 768 persons. The officials roster lists one 知事 (governor, Yamakawa Jingorō), one 大参事 (senior councillor), one 権大参事 (acting senior councillor), and six 少参事 (junior councillors), each named. The roster continues onto the facing leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Takasaki (高崎藩): officials roster (continuation)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (councillors) and military personnel
pages.page_summary_en: This Fascicle 8 leaf belongs entirely to Takasaki (高崎藩), continuing the officials roster begun on the facing page; it carries no new ○ domain-boundary marker. The header column records the domain's 兵員 (military strength) as 735 persons. The tail of the councillor list appears here: a block of six holdover names, followed by the 権少参事 (acting junior councillor) heading with its count of five and its five named appointees. A small interlinear note flags that two of the men have no recorded given names and that one is entered at the 権少参事 rank.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Tatebayashi (館林藩): population, troops, and land assessment
pages.page_topic: Tatebayashi domain civil register: population sub-classes (eta, blind, miko, nuns, yamabushi, ferrymen, physicians, kengyo), troops, village count, and land assessment / land-tax figures
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the civil register (人別) for Tatebayashi domain (館林藩), opened by the ○ domain-boundary marker at the ○館林藩 heading. Reading right to left, it lists small population sub-classes with male and female detail — physicians (医師) 28 and one kengyō, mountain ascetics (山伏) 28, ferrymen (渡守) 66, blind persons 4, one shrine maiden (巫女) and four nuns, and an eta (穢多) population of 1,287 (693 male, 594 female). It then records 735 troops (兵), 93 villages (村), and the land figures: an assessed yield (草高) of 60,000 koku, a new-field uplift (外高) of 53,851.7 koku, a combined assessment (合高) of 113,851.7 koku, and a regular land tax in rice (正租米) of 12,337.4 koku given as a five-year average.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Tatebayashi (館林藩): households, temples, and population by status
pages.page_topic: Tatebayashi domain: population by status, households, temples/shrines, and miscellaneous-tax receipts
pages.page_summary_en: This civil-register leaf for Tatebayashi domain (館林藩) records the miscellaneous tax (雑税) — 1,826.6 koku in rice plus cash — followed by the domain's household and population accounts. It gives 15,868 households (戸数), 105 shrines (神社) and 290 temples (寺院), and a breakdown by status: samurai households (士族) 293, lower retainers (卒族) 618, shrine-priest families (社家) 43, commoners (平民) 14,551, mountain ascetics (修験) 18, crematory attendants (煙亡) 19, eta (穢多) outcastes 406, and hinin (非人) 21. The final column gives a total population (人員) of 75,057, split into 37,859 male and 37,198 female. Several entries are dated to the first month of 1871 (辛未正月).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 3 — Tatebayashi (館林藩): population by status, villages, and troops
pages.page_topic: Tatebayashi domain population by status class, clergy, outcaste groups, villages/towns, and troop strength
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the civil register for Tatebayashi domain (館林藩), breaking the population into status categories with male and female sub-totals: samurai (士族) 1,525, lower retainers (卒族) 2,980, shrine-priest families (社家) 143, mountain ascetics (修験) 94, commoners (平民) 67,589, temple clergy (寺院) 654, four nuns (尼), crematory workers (煙亡) 89, eta (穢多) outcastes 1,845, and hinin (非人) 134. It also records 125 villages (村数) and 18 towns (町数), and a military establishment of soldiers plus 637 foot-soldiers (兵卒) organized as sixteen platoons of forty. Because the domain's heading appears on its opening leaf, no ○ marker or governor's name is printed here.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（館林、大聖寺）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tatebayashi (館林藩) and Daishōji (大聖寺藩): officials
pages.page_topic: Officials establishment (職員) for Tatebayashi and Daishōji domains — administrative-officer ranks with counts; military not disclosed for Tatebayashi
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-8 officials leaf (職員) carries two domains. The first is Tatebayashi (○館林藩), whose officer establishment is given as rank headings with counts: a governor (知事, heading only, no name printed), one senior councillor (大参事), four acting senior councillors (権大参事), seven junior councillors (少参事), and six acting junior councillors (権少参事); its troop strength (兵員) is marked as not recorded (記セス). The lower left opens the next domain, Daishōji (○大聖寺藩), listing its senior councillor Maeda Kan (前田幹) and four acting senior councillors — Aoike Yaemon (青池彌右衞門), Tamaru Morie (田丸守衞), Isshiki Kiyoshi (一色清), and Kōsaka Kuemon (上坂九右衞門). Daishōji's remaining figures continue on the facing leaf.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（館、高槻）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Tatebayashi (館林藩) and Takatsuki (高槻藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (職員) and military establishment (兵隊) — Fascicle 8
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-8 officials-and-military leaf is dominated by Tatebayashi domain (館林藩), whose ○ marker opens a full administrative roster read right to left: a governor (知事), two senior councillors (大参事), six acting senior councillors (権大参事), five junior councillors (少参事), six acting junior councillors (権少参事), and a standing force (常備兵) of 1,249 men. The military and officials figures printed to the right of Tatebayashi's ○ marker — a force (兵隊) of two battalions of six companies each and an artillery corps (砲隊) of 98 men and 8 guns, together with the junior-councillor appointees Inagaki Awa (稲垣淡) and Ikoma Kazuhiko (生駒一彦) — belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, not to Tatebayashi. At bottom left the next domain, Takatsuki (○高槻藩), opens, with its senior-councillor post (大参事) noted as vacant for the time being (當分欠官).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nakamura / Sōma (中村藩): land, revenue, and population
pages.page_topic: Civil/economic register (kokudaka, gendaka, tax breakdown, population, households, status counts) for Nakamura (Soma) domain
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf is the civil and economic register for Nakamura (Sōma) domain (中村藩), opened by the ○ domain-boundary marker in the fourth fascicle of the survey. It records an assessed yield (高) of 83,809.0 koku and a current-rice figure (現米) of 36,423.7 koku, with a two-part revenue breakdown: a regular land tax (正租) of 29,397.1 koku (a five-year average from Bunkyū 3 to Keiō 3) and miscellaneous tax (雑税納) of 6,935.2 koku. Demographic and status data follow — a total population (人員) of 63,893, total households (戸数) of 9,638, samurai households (士族) of 1,937, and eight kazoku (華族, nobility) persons. A note in the header records the troop strength as 1,059 samurai and 878 lower retainers (卒) plus an artillery corps.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nagao (長尾藩): households and population by status
pages.page_topic: Nagao domain (長尾藩) civil register — households, population, and status-group / clergy / outcaste-adjacent breakdowns with male-female splits
pages.page_summary_en: This is the right-hand half of a fascicle-4 civil-register leaf for Nagao domain (長尾藩), a small Kazusa domain identified here by its running header; because this is a continuation leaf, no ○ marker or governor's name is printed. The columns record total households (戸数) of 12,275 and a total population (人員) of 70,850 (35,056 male, 35,794 female), followed by per-group counts with male and female splits: monkey-showmen (猿牽), constables (長吏), shrine-priest families (社家), temples (寺, 333 sites and 320 persons), temple-land peasants (寺領百姓, 282 houses and 1,482 persons), samurai (士族) 310, lower retainers (卒族) 268, and foot-soldiers (兵卒) 153, each with a dependent-family (家族) breakdown. The facing left half of this leaf carries the neighbouring domain of Nagaoka (長岡藩).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Nagao (長尾藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: officials_and_military
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-9 leaf (職員兵隊, officials and military) covers Nagao domain (長尾藩), opened by the sole ○ marker on the page at ○長尾藩. Nagao's military is recorded as 161 standing troops (常備兵) and 155 reserve troops (准備兵). Its officials roster runs across two registers — a compact surname-and-rank block on the right (Honda and Masuda as senior councillors 大参事; Shigetomi, Kameda, Ishii, and Okumura as junior councillors 少参事) and a fuller full-name block on the left, headed by a senior-councillor column carrying the editorial note that the following seven lines were originally written in vermillion (以下七行原朱書). The 兵隊 figure of 627 troops printed to the right of the ○長尾藩 marker belongs to the previous domain sharing this leaf, not to Nagao, whose troops total 316.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Nagaoka (長岡藩): land, revenue, and households by status
pages.page_topic: Nagaoka domain civil register: kokudaka, five-year-average current rice, miscellaneous tax, and household/population breakdown by status group
pages.page_summary_en: This left half-leaf records the fascicle-4 civil register for Nagaoka domain (長岡藩), opened by the ○ marker at ○長岡藩. It gives an assessed yield (草高) of 24,000 koku, a five-year-average current-rice figure (現米) of 22,993.4, and a miscellaneous-tax rice figure (雑税現石) of 614.3 koku. The bulk of the leaf is a household count (戸数) broken down by status group: samurai (士族) 607 houses (including one kazoku 華族 house), foot-soldiers (卒) 1,122, rural commoners (在方) 3,901, townsmen (町方) 1,813, temples (寺) 80, shrine-priest families (社家) 10, and eta (穢多) 2. The total population (人員) and the eta-hinin count are left blank or marked indeterminate (不分明).

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第九（長岡、長島）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Nagaoka (長岡藩) and Nagashima (長島藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: officials_military
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-9 officials-and-military leaf names both Nagaoka and Nagashima in its running header. The primary domain is Nagaoka (長岡藩), whose ○ marker opens the block: its army (兵隊) is recorded as 828 troops, its officials headcount (官員) is undisclosed (不詳), and its named appointees run through the senior councillors (大参事: Makino Tanomo 牧野頼母, Mishima Okuchōrō, Kobayashi Torasaburō), the acting senior councillors (権大参事: Nagino Kahei, Akita Motome, Hara Ichihei, Takebe Seizō), and longer junior-councillor rosters. The note printed to the right of the Nagaoka marker (以上大参事以下姓名届留守官) belongs to the previous domain, Nakamura (中村藩), on the facing leaf. At the far left, the ○長島藩 marker opens the next domain, Nagashima, whose own officials continue on the following leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Oka (岡藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: officials_and_military
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 8 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) records the officials and military establishment of Oka (岡藩), the Nakagawa family's domain in Bungo province. The ○ domain-boundary marker opens Oka's entry mid-leaf, and its roster of 官員 (administrative officials) runs leftward from there: a 大参事 (senior councillor, 1), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 4), 少参事 (junior councillor, 2), and 権少参事 (acting junior councillor, 1); the 知事 (governor) heading is printed but names no appointee. Read right-to-left, the officials and troop figures to the RIGHT of the ○岡藩 marker — a lone 権少参事 appointee together with 歩兵 (infantry, one 600-man battalion) and 砲兵 (artillery, one 144-man battery) — belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, not to Oka.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kanō (加納藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: officials_and_military
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 8 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) opens the entry for Kanō (加納藩) with its ○ domain-boundary marker, then gives its officials roster: a 知事 (governor), 大参事 (senior councillor, 1), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 2), and 少参事 (junior councillor, 3). Read right-to-left, the material to the RIGHT of the ○加納藩 marker belongs to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Kasama (笠間藩): its named 知事 (governor) and its full military establishment of seven unit types — scout, artillery, sharpshooter, and volley-fire companies, plus first-, second-, and third-class guard companies of 61, 51, and 52 men. That Kasama military does not belong to Kanō.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Takada (高田藩): officials
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (職員) — Takada domain administrative appointees
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 8 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) is the officials (職員) page for Takada (高田藩), the single domain shown, marked by its ○ domain-boundary marker. The 知事 (governor) line carries no name or count and is noted as 審ナラス (not disclosed); the domain reports 大参事 (senior councillor, 5) and 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 6), with a 権少参事 (acting junior councillor) heading standing atop a roster of eleven named appointees. No military figures appear on this leaf — it is purely a roster of names, with troop data falling on the adjacent pages.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 4 — Tsuyama (津山藩): land assessment and civil register
pages.page_topic: Civil register (kokudaka, land tax, vessels, temples/shrines, outcaste and clerical populations) — Tsuyama domain opening on this leaf, with the tail of the previous domain Tsu on the right.
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 4 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) is a civil register that opens the entry for Tsuyama (津山藩) at its ○ domain-boundary marker. Tsuyama's land figures give a 高 (base assessment) of 100,000 koku, a 込高新田改出高 (reclaimed and re-surveyed add-on) of 4,576.913 koku, a 草高 (total assessed yield) of 104,576.913 koku, and a 正租 (main land tax) of 41,967.4508 koku of rice, averaged over five years.
