Read right-to-left, the fields to the RIGHT of the ○津山藩 marker are the tail of the previous domain, Tsu (津藩): its 兵卒 (troops, 1,647), one steamship and one sailing vessel, 579 villages, 1,247 temples, 1,122 shrines, 1,564 hinin and 9,098 eta (each with a male/female split), and 52 nuns — closed by a submission note dated the 11th month of 1870. Those Tsu counts belong to Tsu, not Tsuyama.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Tsuyama (津山藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (councillors) and military establishment of Tsuyama-han
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) records the officials and troops of Tsuyama (津山藩), the single domain shown, marked by its ○ domain-boundary marker. Officials are listed by rank — 大参事 (senior councillor, 2), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 2), and 権少参事 (acting junior councillor, 11) — with appointee names hung in columns below the headings; an inline note reads 少参事以下不詳 (junior councillor and below: not detailed). The 兵隊 (troops) line reads 一大隊但一小隊六十人 — one battalion, with each company comprising sixty men. No gun, cannon, warship, or total-strength figures are printed here.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第九（津和野、土浦）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Tsuwano (津和野藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (職員) and military (兵隊) — Fascicle 9: Tsuwano domain full officials roster + its 6-platoon force, plus the opening of Tsuchiura domain
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) is headed for Tsuwano and Tsuchiura and carries two domains. Tsuwano (津和野藩), opened by its ○ domain-boundary marker, fills most of the page: a 知事 (governor, unnamed here), a 大参事 (senior councillor) marked 欠員 (vacant), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 3), 少参事 (junior councillor, 7), and 権少参事 (acting junior councillor, 3); its force is 六小隊 (six platoons of sixty men, 360 total), with a note of 40 additional sub-officials. At the far left the ○土浦藩 marker opens Tsuchiura (土浦藩) with its 大参事 heading and first four appointees; that roster continues on the following leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Tsuchiura (土浦藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (councillors) and military establishment of Tsuchiura domain
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) continues the entry for Tsuchiura (土浦藩), the 90,000-koku Tsuchiya-family domain in Hitachi province, the single domain shown here. The 知事 (governor) heading carries no surname (the governor's name appeared on the preceding leaf); the councillor ranks run right-to-left as 大参事 (senior councillor, 2), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 1), 少参事 (junior councillor, 2), and 権少参事 (acting junior councillor), with appointee names hung below each heading. The military entry records 大隊貳隊 (two battalions), qualified by a note that 47 men make one platoon and six platoons make a battalion. A marginal caretaker-official report dated the 6th month of 1870 attaches to a separately listed 大参事 at the far left.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Matsuyama (松山藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (chiji / sanji ranks) and military establishment for Matsuyama domain, with a naval-vessel note overflowing from the preceding domain (Matsue).
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) is opened by the ○松山藩 marker, so the domain shown is Iyo-Matsuyama (松山藩), the Hisamatsu-Matsudaira house. The 知事 (governor) heading carries no printed name; the councillor ranks are 大参事 (senior councillor, 3), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 3), and 少参事 (junior councillor, 3), with nine appointee names hung in columns. The military entry gives 歩兵 (infantry) as 30 platoons of 75 men each (2,250), 砲兵 (artillery) as 3 units of 43 gunners plus 10 officers each (129), and 船ナシ (no ships). Read right-to-left, the naval note 千石積 一艘 (one 1,000-koku-capacity vessel) printed to the RIGHT of the ○松山藩 marker belongs to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Matsue (松江藩), not to Matsuyama.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Himeji) — running header
pages.page_topic: Himeji kokudaka (opening entry) + Hikone temple/shrine-land households & population (continuation)
pages.page_summary_en: This is a boundary page in fascicle 7 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran: it closes Hikone domain's entry and opens Himeji's. The right two-thirds continue Hikone's temple- and shrine-land tabulation (管轄内社寺領地戸口): 5,169 total households and 21,421 people (男10,551/女10,870, including 154 monks and 310 temple clergy), sub-divided into shrine-land (211 households / 759 people, with 20 Shinto priests, 4 shrine-maidens, 5 monks, 4 nuns) and temple-land (334 households / 1,776 people, with 176 monks and 4 nuns). To the left of the ○姫路藩 marker begins Himeji domain: nominal assessed yield (草高) of 150,000 koku plus an additional 61,224.081 koku from new-field re-survey, for a combined total of 211,224.081 koku, followed by the five-year-average heading. Printed book page is 百七十七 (177).

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 — Himeji
pages.page_topic: Himeji domain — land tax, miscellaneous levies, and product taxes
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the Fascicle 7 fiscal entry for Himeji domain (姫路藩). It records the domain's regular land-tax rice (正租米) of 87,437.108 koku, followed by miscellaneous tax rice (雜稅米) broken into three named levies — petty imposts/komononari (小物成) 702.009 koku, commercial dues/unjō (運上) 338.663 koku, and mountain-district dues (山方運上) 6.93 koku. Under a 諸產物稅 (product-tax) header, four domain products are each paired with their tax: bleached cotton (晒木綿, ~540,000 tan → 2,055 ryō), salt (鹽, >280,000 koku → 69.003 koku of rice), tanned leather hides (~28,000 pieces → 179 ryō), and stone (~5,700 pieces → 149 pieces in kind, equal to 0.61 koku of hulled rice). The printed book-page number is 178.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 7 (Himeji) — outer-margin running header (provenance)
pages.page_topic: Himeji domain household & population statistics by status group
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the Himeji domain (姫路藩) entry in fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran, tabulating households and population by status group. It records 51,489 total households and a population of 222,661. The itemized status households are: 706 samurai (shizoku) households with 4,030 persons (1,925 M / 2,105 F); 1,402 foot-soldier (sotsu) households with 4,582 persons (2,433 M / 2,149 F); 273 boatmen-and-fixed-guard households with 1,095 persons (592 M / 503 F); 118 bureau-servant/substitute-hire households with 789 persons (468 M / 321 F); and 135 shrine-family (shake) households with 488 persons (262 M / 226 F); plus 647 temples. No domain marker appears on the page, so every figure belongs to Himeji (the block opens on the facing page with the ○姫路藩 marker).

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Register, Fascicle 7 (Himeji)
pages.page_topic: Himeji special-status population, shrines, and governor's household
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the Fascicle-7 demographic register for Himeji Domain (姫路藩). It records special-status populations — temple residents 1,650 (clergy 893, male 213, female 544), shugendō practitioners 65 (ascetics 17, male 20, female 28), eta 11,389 (male 5,757, female 5,632), and hinin 109 (male 54, female 55) — together with structural counts: 2,307 eta households, 1,059 shrines, 19 shugendō sites, and the governor's household of 3 (male 1, female 2). Village count and hinin household count are both marked "not recorded" (記セス). A three-line red-ink marginal note reconciles the household total: the original combined figure of 51,948 households becomes 52,548 when summed by category, so the 1,059 shrines are subtracted to follow the breakdown.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Hirado) — running header
pages.page_topic: Himeji five-year-average land-tax account and shrine/temple-land yield; opening of Hirado (kokudaka)
pages.page_summary_en: The right two-thirds of the page completes Himeji Domain's fascicle-7 fiscal entry as a five-year-average (五ヶ年平均) tax account: regular land-tax rice (正租米) of 1,234.488 koku, miscellaneous-tax rice (雜稅米) of 13.497 koku, and a cash tax (錢) of 10.756 kan whose rice equivalent (此米) is 0.134 koku, summing to a combined tax rice (合米) of 1,248.119 koku. It also records shrine- and temple-land yield (社寺領高) of 2,665.856 koku, with an additional 16.66 koku reckoned in, and notes that Himeji holds no ships (船ナシ). Below the ○平戸藩 maru-marker the page begins Hirado Domain, giving its nominal assessed yield (草高) of 61,700 koku and a heading for newly-reclaimed-field re-survey yield. The printed book-page number is 181 and the running header reads "Fascicle 7 (Hirado)."

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Himeji (姫路藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials and military (職員兵隊) — Hikone tail + Himeji
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表) is headed for Himeji (姫路藩), opened by its ○ domain-boundary marker. To the LEFT of the marker is Himeji's own entry: its officials are noted as 官員不詳 (not disclosed), and its military totals 288 兵士 (soldiers) and 576 兵卒 (rank-and-file troops) in 6 and 12 platoons respectively, plus 168 砲手 (gunners) and 54 樂手 (bandsmen). Read right-to-left, the columns to the RIGHT of the ○姫路藩 marker belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Hikone (彦根藩): its 少参事 (junior councillor, 2), 権少参事 (acting junior councillor, 3), a foot-soldier force of 36 platoons, and 2 artillery batteries of six guns each. That Hikone material does not belong to Himeji.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Hiji)
pages.page_topic: Hiji domain regular land tax, miscellaneous tax, and household/status counts
pages.page_summary_en: This is a continuation page for Hiji domain (日出藩, Bungo province, Kyushu; Kinoshita house) within fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran. The regular land tax (正租) is rice 8,906.0237 koku plus soybeans 1,584.274 koku, which sum exactly to the total regular tax (正租合高) of 10,490.2977 koku recorded here as a red-ink marginal note; the soybean levy is separately valued at 8,064 ryō 1 bu (at ~5 ryō 1 shu per koku) and re-expressed as 1,008.055 koku of rice at 8 ryō per koku. Miscellaneous taxes (雜稅) comprise rice 473.9329 koku and cash 112 ryō 1 bu plus 13 mon (ei). The domain has 4,712 households, of which 195 shizoku, 261 sotsu, 39 shrine families, 10 Shugendō yamabushi, and 9 blind monks, along with 47 temples.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Hitotsubashi section)
pages.page_topic: Hiji domain population by status and religious estate; Hitotsubashi kokudaka
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page completes the Fascicle 7 demographic block for Hiji domain (日出藩, Bungo province): a total population of 20,925 (10,649 male, 10,276 female), broken out into 946 shizoku, 1,044 sotsu, 201 shrine attendants (社人), 127 Buddhist clergy (寺侶), 46 mountain ascetics (修驗山伏), 37 blind monks (盲僧), and an eta (outcaste) population of 177 persons living in 44 households, together with 125 Shinto shrines; the domain governor's own household is expressly not recorded. At the far left a maru-marker opens the Hitotsubashi domain (一橋藩) section, whose scattered holdings across eight provinces are noted in a warichu and whose nominal assessed yield (kusadaka) is given as 118,815.38858 koku. The male/female splits and the eta population column read directly from the scan were absent or transcribed incorrectly in the prior dataset. The running header names Hitotsubashi (provenance) even though the bulk of the data belongs to Hiji.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第九（日出、一橋）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Hiji (日出藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Officials (shokuin) and troop strength (heitai) for three domains: the tail of an unnamed preceding domain, then Hiji (日出藩), then the start of Hitotsubashi (一橋藩)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表), read right-to-left, is headed for Hiji and Hitotsubashi and carries three domains. The central and dominant block is Hiji (日出藩), opened by its ○ domain-boundary marker: 大参事 (senior councillor, 1), 権大参事 (acting senior councillor, 2), 少参事 (junior councillor, 2), and 兵隊 (troops) of 5 platoons — 2 士族 (samurai) platoons and 3 卒 (foot-soldier) platoons. The rightmost columns are the tail of the domain immediately preceding Hiji: its 権大参事 (3), 少参事 (3), 権少参事 (3), named appointees, and 兵隊 (troops, 160 persons); because this troop figure sits to the RIGHT of the ○日出藩 marker, it belongs to that preceding domain, not to Hiji. At the far left the ○一橋藩 marker opens Hitotsubashi (一橋藩), whose 執政 (regents) begin here and continue onto the facing leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 5 — Matsuoka (松岡藩): demographics
pages.page_topic: Matsuoka demographics (shares the Fukuoka-opening leaf; Matsuoka's tail continues here)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf sits on the boundary between two domains in Fascicle 5 of the survey, which records population and household figures. At the lower left it opens the entry for Fukuoka (福岡藩) with that domain's ○ (domain-boundary marker) and land figure. But read right-to-left, everything to the right of that marker is the closing demographic block of the preceding domain, Matsuoka (松岡藩): a total population of 12,805, with 士族 (samurai households) numbering 507 persons and 卒族 (lower-samurai households) 365, alongside 139 Shinto-priest and 39 temple residents, 65 in the outcast (穢多) group, and 29 villages. The Fukuoka data proper continues on the following leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 2 — Okayama (岡山藩): demographics
pages.page_topic: Okayama domain population and household breakdown by status group, grand totals, shrines/temples, and one warship (Fascicle 2 demographics).
pages.page_summary_en: This page comes from Fascicle 2 of the survey, the demographic register, and carries the closing portion of the Okayama domain (岡山藩) entry. The ○ (domain-boundary marker) for the next domain, Ōizumi (大泉藩), appears at the lower left, so every column to the right of it belongs to Okayama. It records a commoner population of 328,341 (172,475 male, 155,874 female), broken down by status group: Shinto-priest households and population (642 households, 2,772 persons), 709 temple clergy, mountain-ascetic (山伏) households and population (105 / 323), and outcast (穢多) households and population (993 / 9,128). The grand totals are 85,431 households and 358,827 persons, and the domain reports 701 shrines, 464 temples, and one warship.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Okayama (岡山藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Okayama domain officials (councillors and administrative ranks) and standing military force, at the boundary with the Ōizumi domain entry.
pages.page_summary_en: This page belongs to Fascicle 8 of the survey, which lists domain officials and military strength. Although the running header names the Ōizumi (大泉藩) section, the ○ (domain-boundary marker) for Ōizumi sits in mid-page, so everything to its right is the entry for the preceding domain, Okayama (岡山藩). It names eight councillors (議員) under the administrative ranks 少参事 (junior counsellor) and 権少参事 (acting junior counsellor), and gives Okayama's standing army as seventeen rifle battalions (銃隊) and four artillery emplacements (砲隊), totaling 7,862 men. To the left of the marker, the 知事 (governor) heading opens the next domain, Ōizumi.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran (Domain Survey), Fascicle 8 (officials & military register), Ōizumi (Shōnai) section — running header / provenance
pages.page_topic: Domain officials — councillor ranks and roster
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left (continuation) page of the Ōizumi (大泉 = the 1869 rename of Shōnai/庄内) Domain's officials entry in Fascicle 8 of the Hansei Ichiran. It records four councillor ranks with headcounts — Grand Councillor (大参事) 2, Acting Grand Councillor (権大参事) printed as 5 but corrected by an interlinear note to 4, Junior Councillor (少参事) 5, and Acting Junior Councillor (権少参事) 2 — followed in the lower band by the thirteen named officeholders. The roster of thirteen names matches the corrected sum 2+4+5+2 exactly, confirming that the 権大参事 count is four rather than five. The ○大泉藩 marker and the governor (知事) that open the entry are on the facing right page (p.149 recto), not on this leaf; the inner-margin figures give the provenance header 藩制一覧表第八（大泉）and reprint page number 275.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Hirosaki (弘前藩): land assessment and taxes
pages.page_topic: Fascicle-7 boundary page: tail of the previous domain's population/religious/warship fields, then the head of Hirosaki-han's (弘前藩) fiscal block (kokudaka, land tax, totals, households).
pages.page_summary_en: This is a boundary leaf from Fascicle 7 of the survey, which records each domain's land assessment, taxes, and household totals. The ○ (domain-boundary marker) here reads ○弘前藩, opening the entry for Hirosaki (弘前藩) at an original assessment of 100,000 koku. Everything at and to the left of that marker is Hirosaki's own fiscal block: 草高 (assessed yield) of 274,482 koku including reclaimed land, 正租 (regular land tax) of 130,854.5 koku as a five-year average, miscellaneous taxes in rice and cash, combined grand totals, and 50,162 households (戸數). The five columns to the right of the marker — clergy, outcast population, shrines, the governor's family, and warships — are the closing fields of the previous domain, whose own entry falls on the preceding leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Hirosaki)
pages.page_topic: Population, status counts, temples/shrines, and Boshin reward-rice (弘前藩)
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page continues the fascicle-7 population/household block for Hirosaki domain (弘前藩) in Mutsu. It records a total population of 278,842 — a printed figure the 1928 reprint flags with a マ ("sic") mark, since the male 142,085 + female 136,657 split actually sums to 278,742 (100 fewer). Of the population it breaks out shizoku 12,469 persons, sotsu 10,215, shrine-people (社人) 799, and temple-clergy (寺侶) 726, each with its own male/female split, and notes that eta/hinin were not recorded. Household counts give 2,066 shizoku, 2,261 sotsu, 269 temples and 117 shrine-households; the domain has 873 shrines, holds no warships, and receives an imperial reward-rice (御賞典米) of 2,500 koku tied to a perpetual 10,000-koku grant plus a 10,000-koku-per-year three-year grant.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Mori (森藩): population and taxes
pages.page_topic: Mori Domain (森藩) civil statistics — continuation: retainer-class households/populations, domain kokudaka taxes (soybean, misc-tax rice, gold, ei), total households, and population with male/female splits
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left, continuation half of the two-page Fascicle 7 entry for Mori (森藩), a small domain of about 12,500 koku in Bungo Province held by the Kurushima (久留島) family. Its ○ (domain-boundary marker) and header open on the facing right half, so this half carries no marker and is read right-to-left as a continuation. It records Mori's population of 14,244 (6,839 male, 7,405 female) and, by status, 128 士族 (samurai households) with 720 persons and 130 卒族 (lower-retainer households) with 726 persons, for 2,645 households (總戸數) in all. The tax yields follow: soybeans of 1,205.278 koku, miscellaneous-tax rice (雜稅米) of 262.216 koku, gold of 245 ryō, and a small cash (永) figure of 17.122.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Overview, Fascicle 7 (Mori)
pages.page_topic: Mori han religious populations, temple/shrine counts, outcaste households, governor's family, villages, and warships
pages.page_summary_en: This is a continuation leaf of the 森藩 (Mori Domain, Bungo province) entry in Fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran, with no domain marker; the running header (Fascicle 7, Mori) identifies the block and all columns belong to Mori. It records small religious and marginal populations: the shrine-office (社務) community numbers 11 households and 71 persons (39 male, 32 female), and the Buddhist-temple clergy 20 temples with 70 persons (33 male, 37 female). Outcaste groups are minimal — 穢多 3 households / 20 persons (7 male, 13 female) and 非人 2 households / 12 persons (printed as 5 male, 7 female, which MASTER has recorded with the sexes reversed). The page also lists 10 Shinto shrines (plus 14 auxiliary, 10 subordinate, and 13 minor shrines), the governor's household of 5 (3 male, 2 female), notes that the village count was not recorded (記セス), and reports no warships (艦ナシ); the leaf is printed page 204.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Kōharu / Kokura (香春藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Fascicle-8 officials-and-military boundary page: Tottori's overflow (權少参事 officials + army) at right, and the start of Kōharu's block at left.
pages.page_summary_en: This is a Fascicle 8 leaf recording domain officials and military strength, sitting on the boundary between two domains. The ○ (domain-boundary marker) reads ○香春藩, so the block to the left of it opens the entry for Kōharu (香春藩): a governor (知事), one senior councillor (大参事), four acting senior councillors (権大参事), and a force of forty-six companies totaling roughly 2,700 men. Everything to the right of the marker is the overflow of the preceding domain, Tottori (鳥取藩): its 権少参事 (acting junior counsellor) rank with six named appointees, and its army of ten battalions (3,734 men) plus an artillery corps (砲隊) of 240 men.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Numata (沼田藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (chiji and sanji ranks) and military strength
pages.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page (Fascicle 8) for Numata (沼田藩) in Kōzuke Province. In its two-register layout, the upper band gives the administrative ranks — a governor (知事), two senior councillors (大参事), two acting senior councillors (権大参事), and five junior councillors (少参事) — with the appointees' names in the lower band; the governor's slot carries no printed name, and the nine listed names fill the councillor rolls exactly. At the left the military entry records a garrison of 251 troops (兵隊) organized as three and a half platoons, noted at 66 men per platoon including officers. This is a clean single-domain leaf, with no ○ (domain-boundary marker) and no overflow from a neighbor.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（大田原）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Ōtawara (大田原藩): officials roster
pages.page_topic: Fascicle-8 domain-officials roster (governor and councillors) — the data belongs to Ōtawara domain (大田原藩), NOT Wakayama despite the batch label
pages.page_summary_en: This is a Fascicle 8 page of the survey, listing the appointed administrative officers of a single domain. The running header names Ōtawara (大田原藩), a small fudai domain of about 11,400 koku in Shimotsuke Province, and the governor (知事) is its hereditary lord Ōtawara Ichigaku (大田原一學). The roster records one governor, one senior councillor (大参事), one acting senior councillor (権大参事), five junior councillors (少参事), and three acting junior councillors (権少参事), each named individually. A small interlinear note beside the fifth junior councillor records a variant reading of his name.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 8 — Yoshimi (吉見藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military (職員兵隊) — Yoshii officials/troops overflowing right of the Yoshimi marker, plus the opening of the Yoshimi entry
pages.page_summary_en: This is a Fascicle 8 leaf recording domain officials and military strength, sitting on the boundary between two domains. The ○ (domain-boundary marker) printed here reads ○吉見藩, so Yoshimi (吉見藩) is the page's own domain: its entry opens with the governor (知事, unnamed on this half) and one senior councillor (大参事), continuing onto the facing half. Everything to the right of the marker is the overflow of the preceding domain, Yoshii (吉井藩): its lower-rank tallies — three junior councillors (少参事), two acting senior councillors (権大参事), and three acting junior councillors (権少参事) — a military strength of 178 men (兵員), and a roster of nine named officials. Two small collation notes record variant readings from another copy of the source.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Nobeoka (延岡藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: officials_and_military
pages.page_summary_en: This is the officials-and-military page for Nobeoka (延岡藩) in Hyūga Province, governed by Naitō Masanori (内藤政學), from Fascicle 9 of the survey. Read right-to-left, the ○ (domain-boundary marker) ○延岡藩 opens Nobeoka's entry: a governor (知事), two senior councillors (大参事), one acting senior councillor (権大参事), and five junior councillors (少参事), together with a separately reported list of officials. Nobeoka's military (兵隊) totals 878 men — 345 samurai troops and 503 foot-soldier troops (upper and lower), plus six cannon (大砲) with thirty gunners. The three fields to the right of the marker — undetailed officials, 159 foot soldiers, and 175 rural levies — are overflow belonging to the previous domain in this fascicle, not to Nobeoka.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第九（山上、山家）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Yamagami (山上藩) and Yamaga (山家藩): officials and military
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (chiji through gon-shōsanji, with appointee names and a kōginin) and military strength for Yamagami-han and Yamaga-han
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf comes from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表), the fascicle that records each domain's officials roster and military strength, and its running head names the two domains it covers: Yamagami (山上藩) and Yamaga (山家藩). The ○ domain-boundary marker on this leaf opens Yamaga (○山家藩), which lists one 知事 (governor), two 大参事 (senior councillors), two 権大参事 (junior senior councillors), and four 少参事 (junior councillors), with named appointees. The officials and 兵隊 (troops) block printed to the right of the ○山家藩 marker belong to the previous domain sharing this leaf, Yamagami — whose roster runs from governor down through junior councillors and whose military is given as 36 士族 (samurai-class troops) and 61 卒 (foot-soldier-class troops), for 97 in all.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 9 — Yatabe (谷田部藩), with Yachi (谷地藩) and Matsue (松江藩)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials (governor and councillors) with appointee names, plus military notation, for Yatabe, Yachi, and Matsue
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf comes from Fascicle 9 of the Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表), the fascicle recording each domain's officials roster and military strength, and is read right to left. Its principal domain is Yatabe (○谷田部藩), whose full slate of officials is printed: one 知事 (governor), one 大参事 (senior councillor), three 権大参事 (junior senior councillors), and four 少参事 (junior councillors), together with eight named appointees; Yatabe's troop strength is left unspecified (兵隊未詳, troops not detailed). This leaf also carries the opening of two neighbouring domains — Yachi (○谷地藩), whose officials and troops are both marked undetailed (職員兵數不詳), and Matsue (○松江藩), which shows one 知事 (governor) with its remaining figures continuing onto the following page.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran-hyō (Survey of Domain Administration), Fascicle 6
pages.page_topic: Kōriyama domain — land assessment and tax (kokudaka, land tax, miscellaneous tax, cash)
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the fascicle-6 (藩制一覧表第六) economic entry for Kōriyama Domain (郡山藩, Yamato province; Yanagisawa clan). It records a gross assessed yield (草高) of 152,912.29987 koku and states the land tax as three rice figures — regular land-tax rice (正租米) 34,931.513 koku, a rice item of 902.9454 koku, and an unlabeled component of 18,417.38 koku — which sum exactly to the 合 total of 54,251.8384 koku (arithmetic verified). Miscellaneous-tax rice (雜稅米) is 101.3114 koku, and the entry lists two cash figures (39 ryō + 永36.7 mon; 2 ryō 1 bu 2 shu + 永16.8 mon) plus a further rice figure of 3,824.4078 koku. The block is a single domain: the ○郡山藩 marker sits at upper right, all data columns lie to its left, and a rectangular library-collection seal overlaps the running header at the top right.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Kōriyama)
pages.page_topic: Kōriyama domain: households, population, and rice/cash figures
pages.page_summary_en: This second folio of the 郡山藩 (Yamato-Kōriyama, Yanagisawa) entry in fascicle 6 records the domain's household and population statistics alongside rice and cash figures. Households total 22,557 (戸數), of which the itemized special statuses are 士族 1,114, 卒族 754, 社人 49, 陰陽師 7, 座頭 2, 非人番 70, 煙亡 116, and 穢多 575. The population is 102,426 (男 50,917; 女 51,509), of which the 士族 population is 4,468 (男 2,018; 女 2,450). The sheet also gives rice sums of 1,303.1926 koku (米) and a combined 5,228.9118 koku (合米), and two cash amounts headed 金 (≈15 ryō and ≈56 ryō).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Kōriyama)
pages.page_topic: Special-status population counts and religious institutions (Kōriyama)
pages.page_summary_en: This interior leaf of the Kōriyama (Yamato) domain block in fascicle 6 tabulates special-status population counts and religious institutions. It records the sub-samurai (卒族) class at 1,781 (872 male / 909 female) and religious and outcaste groups including 897 Buddhist monks, 25 nuns, 169 shrine attendants, 26 onmyōji diviners, 2 zatō, 228 hinin watchmen, 225 onbō, and 2,003 eta (990 male / 1,013 female), with male/female breakdowns that all sum correctly. It counts 406 Shinto shrines and 683 Buddhist temples, and identifies the principal shrine, Sasaki-jinja at Jōrakuji village in Gamō district, Ōmi province, with an assessed endowment (受領高) of 100 koku and regular land-tax rice (正租米) of 63.9375 koku. A bracketed "of which" male/female note beside the monk and nun entries reads 308 male / 745 female — a total (1,053) that exceeds the 922 monks-plus-nuns, an apparent source inconsistency noted but transcribed as printed.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō (Table of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 6 (Koga)
pages.page_topic: Koga domain: land assessment, land/misc tax with cash-commutation, and households
pages.page_summary_en: This is the opening page of the 古河藩 (Koga Domain) entry in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran. It records Koga's base assessment 本高 80,000 koku and gross assessment 草高 101,257.932593 koku (of which 1,096.764 koku is 従前無地高, formerly no-land / newly-assessed yield); a regular land tax 正租米 24,108.736514 koku with a commuted-cash component 永 12,431.170142 kan-mon equal to 1,553.89628 koku of rice (at the noted rate of 8 ryō per koku); a small miscellaneous tax 雜税米 3.8323 koku with its own cash component 永 318.285347 kan-mon = 39.785669 koku; a grand total 合米 25,706.250763 koku; and 16,747 households. The two columns to the right of the ○古河藩 marker (正税 2.28 koku and the note 右制物有之分) are overflow belonging to the PRECEDING entry — the 佐々木神社 shrine estate in Ōmi (江州蒲生郡常樂寺村, 受領高 100 koku) — not to Koga.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Koga)
pages.page_topic: Koga domain population and status register (fascicle 6, demographic)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf is a continuation of the fascicle-6 (demographic) return for Koga Domain (古河藩), a Shimōsa domain held by the Doi house. It records a total population of 74,777 (37,707 male / 37,070 female), broken out by status: 1,349 shizoku persons in 287 households, and 2,682 sotsu (lower-retainer/foot-soldier class) in 665 households. Clerical and outcaste groups follow: 448 Buddhist clergy (monks+nuns), 412 shrine attendants and 122 shrine households, plus 3,679 eta in 735 households, 77 hinin in 20 households, and 16 onbō (crematory/grave attendants) in 4 households. The page closes with 313 temples and 337 koku of shrine-and-temple land. Nearly every population total is followed by a male/female split that sums exactly to the total; the one exception is the Buddhist-clergy line, whose printed total (448) exceeds its own 345+95 breakdown by eight.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration Survey, Fascicle 6 (Komoro)
pages.page_topic: Komoro domain kokudaka, land tax & tax-in-kind; Koga military tail
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand leaf of Fascicle 6 opens (top right) with the military tail of the PREVIOUS domain, Koga (古河藩) — 12 platoons totalling 576 troops plus a 4-unit, 28-man artillery corps — printed to the right of the ○小諸藩 marker. The rest of the page is Komoro Domain (小諸藩, Shinano): a gross assessed yield (草高) of 28,772.689 koku, broken by the 内 sub-lines into 15,804.4211 koku established paddy (本田) and 12,968.268 koku new paddy (新田). Regular land tax in rice (正租米) is 9,665.695 koku and miscellaneous tax in rice (雜税米) 245.654 koku. Two tax-in-kind commodities close the page — buckwheat 5.1 koku and soybean 0.462 koku — each carrying a cash-conversion warichu (代金 17 ryo; 代永 2 kan 310 mon) and a 此米 rice-equivalent (2.125 and 0.289 koku); all conversions reconcile at 1.25 to of rice per ryo.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Institutions at a Glance (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 6 (Komoro)
pages.page_topic: Komoro domain — population by status, households, koku yield, and cash tax
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left (continuation) page of the Komoro (小諸) domain entry in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran (1870). It records a total population of 31,910 (16,357 male; 15,553 female) in 6,743 households, with status counts for samurai (士族: 681 persons / 127 households), foot-soldiers (卒族: 926 / 152), shrine personnel (社人: 60 / 13), mountain ascetics (修驗: 37 households), and the outcaste groups eta (穢多: 122 households) and hinin (非人: 8 households). Fiscal figures give a total current yield (現石) of 10,016.23 koku, a derived rice figure (此米) of 102.467 koku, and a cash sum (金) of 550 ryō 2 bu plus eisen 269 kan 233 mon 4 rin, with an editorial note that the miscellaneous tax revenue is folded into the main kokudaka figure.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (Hansei Ichiran), fascicle 6, Koromo section
pages.page_topic: Komoro civil/religious/military tail; Koromo kokudaka opening
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf concludes the Komoro (小諸藩) entry in fascicle 6 and opens the Koromo (擧母藩) entry. Komoro's tail fields, printed to the right of the ○擧母藩 marker, record 64 villages, 136 shrines, 54 temples, 108 Buddhist clergy (僧), 143 Shugendō ascetics (修驗), and outcaste populations of 573 eta and 42 hinin, together with a two-platoon infantry of 120 men plus 42 officers and a 26-man artillery corps. Left of the marker, Koromo's block begins: a nominal assessment of 20,000 koku (高貳萬石), a detailed figure of 18,262.848 koku inclusive of new-field development (內新田込高共), and shrine-temple land of 58.14 koku. The running header names （擧母）; the printed page number is 十 (10).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Koromo)
pages.page_topic: Koromo domain kokudaka, genmai (net tax-rice) breakdown, and cash tax revenues (fascicle 6)
pages.page_summary_en: This interior page of Fascicle 6 records the fiscal accounts of Koromo domain (挙母藩, a Naitō holding in Mikawa Province). The assessed kokudaka is 2,125.385 koku, with a further provisional ~4,300 koku of substitute land (代地) in Katsukita-gun, Mimasaka, still under transfer and to be surveyed later. The five-year-average genmai (net tax rice) is 5,231.1958 koku, itemized into 正租 5,051.8072, 口米 147.9556, 雑租 24.722, and 雑税 6.711 koku, which sum exactly to the total. Cash levies under the 諸産物及諸税數 heading total 502 ryō 3 bu 1 shu in gold (雑税 204, 諸運上 119, and 普請役夫金 179 ryō), plus a 永 (eisen) figure of 28.2 mon.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview, Fascicle 6 (Koromo)
pages.page_topic: Koromo domain — kokudaka, five-year-average tax, households
pages.page_summary_en: This page is the complete Hansei Ichiran entry for Koromo domain (挙母藩), a 20,000-koku Mikawa-province holding of the Naitō house. Its nominal kokudaka is 20,000 koku, while the total assessed high including reclaimed land is 22,634.907 koku, of which 2,634.907 koku is new field (so old fields = 20,000). The five-year-average land tax is rendered as 16,127.307 bales of rice (four-to bales, including the miscellaneous taxes of both Mikawa and Mimasaka) plus two cash sums: 203 ryō 3 bu 2 shu in miscellaneous-tax money and 298 ryō 2 bu in various imposts and construction-corvée. The domain counts 4,778 total households, of which 23 are shrine-family households, 39 temples, 30 halls, 20 yamabushi households, and 36 households of town-detached watchmen and outcastes.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō (Overview of Domain Administration), Fascicle 6 (Koizumi)
pages.page_topic: Koromo demographic tail & Koizumi kokudaka/tax head
pages.page_summary_en: This page straddles two domains, divided by the single ○小泉藩 marker. To its right stands the demographic tail of Koromo Domain's (挙母藩) entry: total population 18,746 (9,489 male / 9,257 female), with parenthetical counts of clergy and outcastes; 100 samurai households (461 persons: 230 M / 231 F), 200 sotsu households (446 persons: 211 M / 235 F), and 79 villages. To its left, Koizumi Domain's (小泉藩) entry opens with an assessed yield (kokudaka) of 11,202.617 koku, net tax rice (現米) 5,330.2326 koku, a regular-rice component (正米) 189.7224 koku, and total tax rice (合米) 5,519.955 koku (= 現米 + 正米), followed by 2,109 total households, with a note that the governor's single household is subtracted. The running header and marker both name Koizumi (fascicle 6, printed page 13); a red-ink editorial note dates the survey to the twelfth month of Meiji 2 (1869).

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions (Hansei ichiran), Fascicle 6 — Koizumi
pages.page_topic: Koizumi domain population and household census by status
pages.page_summary_en: This page is the population/household census of Koizumi domain (小泉藩, a small Katagiri fudai domain in Yamato) in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei ichiran. The total population is 9,223 persons (4,564 male, 4,659 female). The status breakdown gives shizoku 165 households / 680 persons, sotsu 91 households / 288 persons, and commoners (平民) 1,483 households / 6,841 persons, together with small religious and outcaste groups: 57 temples with 66 monks, 3 convents with 11 nuns, 1 shugen (mountain-ascetic) household of 1 person, 293 eta households / 1,273 persons, and 11 hinin households / 43 persons. A marginal note records that the governor (知事) and his four family members — 5 persons in all — are accounted for separately from the tabulated totals.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Komono)
pages.page_topic: Komono kokudaka/tax head + Koizumi demographic tail
pages.page_summary_en: The left (marked) block opens the entry for Komono domain (○菰野藩, Ise; Fascicle 6): base assessed yield 11,000.94 koku plus 1,385.447 koku of newly-opened paddy, for a combined total (合高) of 12,386.391 koku. Its five-year-average regular land tax is recorded in rice — a main assessment (本高) of 12,468.171 bales and 847.105 bales from miscellaneous new fields — which, the two combined and converted to koku, equal 5,326.276 koku. The right block is the demographic tail of the preceding domain, Koizumi (小泉藩): 21 villages, 22 shrines, 2 shrine-attendant (社家) households with a population of 4 (male 3, miko 1), and 4 onbō (煙亡) households with a population of 20 (male 8, female 12). Both male/female splits reconcile to their totals; the kokudaka components fall 0.004 koku short of the printed combined total, a minor source inconsistency.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview, Fascicle 6 (Komono)
pages.page_topic: Miscellaneous taxes, tax totals, households and population by status (Komono han)
pages.page_summary_en: This is a continuation data page for Komono han (菰野藩), Ise province, in the sixth fascicle of the Hansei ichiran, identified only by the running header 藩制一覧表第六（菰野）; no maru domain-marker appears on the leaf, so the whole page belongs to Komono. It records the domain's miscellaneous taxes — 396.677 koku of rice (annotated as mountain-land and labor levies) and 118.810 kan-mon in cash (annotated as tea and bamboo taxes) — then the totals of 5,822.953 koku of tax rice (合米) and the same 118.810 kan-mon of total cash (合錢). Population and household figures follow: 1,981 total households and a total population of 10,064 (the male/female split left blank in the source, marked マゝ), itemized as 90 samurai (shizoku) households / 480 persons (236 male, 244 female), 17 foot-soldier (sotsu) households / 91 persons (51 male, 40 female), and 1,839 commoner (farmer-artisan-merchant) households. NOTE: the printed 總戸數 reads 千九百八拾壹戸 = 1,981, not 1,980 as recorded in MASTER (which dropped the 壹); the scan is unambiguous.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Komatsu)
pages.page_topic: Komatsu domain kokudaka (with tail of Komono demographics)
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page of Hansei Ichiran fascicle 6 is filed under Komatsu (小松藩) and carries the complete kokudaka block for that domain: a base assessment of 10,000 koku plus three supplementary yields — 132.468 koku of new paddy (新田高), 1,416.643 koku of progressively surveyed new paddy (追々改出新田), and 1,761.876 koku of new and mountain dry fields combined (新畑山畑共) — summing to a total (合高) of 13,310.987 koku. The columns to the right of the ○小松藩 marker are the demographic tail of the preceding domain, Komono (菰野藩): a commoner population of 9,335 (4,595 male / 4,740 female), 6 shrine-priest households with a population of 35, 29 temples with 123 resident clergy, 125 shrines, and no eta/hinin. The printed page number is 17.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Komatsu) — running header (provenance)
pages.page_topic: Komatsu land tax, miscellaneous taxes, and household/facility counts (5-yr avg)
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fascicle-6 civil/economic entry for Komatsu (Iyo-Komatsu) Domain. It records the 1864–1868 five-year-average official land tax (正租米) as 4,666.078 koku of net rice plus 277.740 kan-mon of cash, then a miscellaneous products-and-taxes block (諸産物及諸税): 83.444 koku of fixed-rate rice levied on upland/paddy/pond land — of which 81.444 koku was the amount actually delivered — together with 187.004 kan-mon of cash (including the tea-monopoly fee) and 610 ryō of gold (including the mulberry-paper monopoly fee). The domain reported 3,029 total households, and among its facilities 20 temples, 21 hermitages, one storehouse, and one town storehouse. Two figures correct the project dataset: the 5-yr-avg net rice is 4,666.078 koku (not the recorded 4,660.718), and a "delivered amount" row of 81.444 koku is present on the page but absent from the dataset.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Tendō) — running header / provenance
pages.page_topic: Komatsu domain demographics; opening of Tendō domain kokudaka
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand leaf (Fascicle 6, printed page 19) carries the demographic tail of Komatsu domain (小松藩), then the opening of Tendō domain (天童藩), the two separated by the ○天童藩 maru-marker. Komatsu's register records a total population of 14,018 (male 7,325, female 6,693), itemized as 83 shizoku households / 423 persons, 40 sotsu households / 316 persons, and 100 eta (outcaste) households / 408 persons, alongside 19 villages, 16 shrines, 16 halls, 8 shrine-priest households, and one row-house (長屋) and one mint site (錢場所). The male and female totals each carry a warichu note subtracting clergy — shrine attendants, monks/nuns, and mountain ascetics — to give lay remainders of 7,261 and 6,668. Left of the marker, Tendō opens with a nominal kusadaka of 21,156.4976 koku and an assessed 18,000 koku; the running header names 天童 even though the bulk of the page's data is Komatsu's.

pages.domain_hi_name: 天童（藩制一覧表第六（天童））
pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō (Domain-System Survey Table), Fascicle 6 (Tendō)
pages.page_topic: Tendō domain — regular land tax, miscellaneous tax, households and status counts
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the Tendō-han (天童藩) entry in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran, recording the domain's tax and household figures (a five-year average, 五ヶ年平均). The regular land tax (正租) is 5,863.72355 koku of rice plus 5,168 ryō 2 bu in cash; expressed wholly in rice (此米) it totals 7,592.58825 koku, of which 1,728.8647 koku was commuted to cash payment (金納) and 5,863.72355 koku paid in kind, with an additional assessed yield (込高) of 3,156.49749 koku. Miscellaneous tax (雜税) comes to 35.69853 koku of rice and 70 kan 536.54 mon in cash. The domain had 2,551 households in total, including 127 shizoku and 189 sotsu households. (Scan-based corrections to the master dataset: 此米 = 7,592.58825 not 7,592.4825; the commuted-rice figure = 1,728.8647 not 1,728.0647; and the miscellaneous-tax cash line 永七拾貫五百三拾六文五分四厘 is an additional field not previously captured.)

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Tendō)
pages.page_topic: Population and household census (Tendō)
pages.page_summary_en: The left leaf of Hansei Ichiran fascicle 6, continuing the demographic entry for Tendō domain (天童藩, a small ~20,000-koku holding in Dewa). It records a total population (人員) of 13,393 — 6,762 male and 6,631 female — broken down by status: 642 shizoku, 535 sotsu, 12,046 commoners, 47 shrine-attendants (社家), 54 Buddhist monks plus a further 53 Ikkō-sect clergy (僧 一向宗), and 16 eta (outcastes). Household and facility counts follow: 2,220 commoner households, 12 shrine-attendant and 3 eta households, 12 Shinto shrines, and 23 Buddhist temples. The status sub-counts and every male/female split reconcile exactly to the 13,393 total, and small warichu notes flag manservants/maidservants (下男/下女) inside the clergy figures.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview, Fascicle 6 (Akita)
pages.page_topic: Akita domain: kokudaka, land and miscellaneous taxes, households and population
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand leaf opens the Akita-han (秋田藩) entry in Fascicle 6 of the Han Administration Overview. It records a nominal assessed yield (草高) of 332,038.779 koku, a regular tax (正税) of about 90,983 ryō rendered in money, and miscellaneous taxes (雜税) of 13,038 koku of rice plus two money accounts — 175,069.22 ryō of product taxes (諸産物税) and 12,868 ryō of other duties on mountains, rivers, fields, livestock, forest and sake-brewing — which sum to the 貳口合 total of 187,937.22 ryō (a five-year average). Demographically it reports 77,456 total households and 435,267 total inhabitants, of which the shizoku (samurai) class numbered 3,219 households and 15,514 persons (7,506 male, 8,008 female).

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview, fascicle 6 (Akita)
pages.page_topic: Akita status-group & institutional demographics (households and population)
pages.page_summary_en: Left half of a demographic spread for Akita domain (秋田藩), fascicle 6 of the 藩制一覧表. Reading right to left, it tabulates households (戸數) and population (人口, each split 男/女) for a run of status and institutional categories: sotsu-class lower samurai 卒族 (1,977 households / 8,059 persons), samurai-household servants 士族下部 (1,131 / 12,535), Shinto shrine-priest families 社家 (278 / 844), Buddhist temple population 寺院 (881 households / 4,786 persons, flagged as an April count 但四月調), a mining population 鑛山 (1,386 / 12,030), and the eta outcaste class 穢多 (89 / 386); a final column records 529 temples (寺院 五百二十九ヶ寺). Every male+female split reconciles exactly to its stated total. No maru-marker (domain boundary) appears, so the entire page belongs to Akita — a continuation of the demographic block begun on the facing right page.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Akita)
pages.page_topic: Akita domain population & status breakdown (Meiji 3/1870 census)
pages.page_summary_en: A single-domain continuation page for 秋田藩 (Akita) in fascicle 6 of the 藩制一覧表, giving the domain's 庚午 (Meiji 3 / 1870, 9th month) demographic census. It records a total 76,755 households (惣戸數) and 413,493 people (同人口), broken down "of which" (内) into shizoku 21,202, sotsu 6,929, shrine-office personnel 3,219, Buddhist clergy 1,911, and eta/ban/hinin outcaste classes 944, plus 7 kazoku nobles (男3/女4), 3,460 shrines (本社 3,055 + 末社 405), and 18 Shugendō households. These 庚午 totals are lower than the undated counts on the preceding page (435,267 people / 77,456 households on p23R), indicating population decline; every gender sub-count reconciles to its status total. A top-of-column restatement "同人口 1,911" (plain numerals, red-ink editorial insertion) duplicates the domain's clergy (僧) figure.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 — (Akashi)
pages.page_topic: Akashi domain — civil register (population, households, kokudaka, land tax)
pages.page_summary_en: This is the opening page of the Akashi (明石藩) block in Fascicle 6 (civil register) of the Han-sei Ichiran, in the bound lower volume (Vol.2 下). It records an official kokudaka (表高/高) of 80,000 koku against an assessed gross (草高) of 90,304.109 koku — the 10,304.109-koku gap attributed to new-field (新田) development — plus 805.8+ koku of vermilion- and black-seal shrine-and-temple land. Fiscally it reports a five-year-average (1864–1868) land tax of 43,235.01754 koku of rice and 1,848 ryō of miscellaneous cash tax (231.11012 koku rice-equivalent), for a combined 現米 total of 43,466.12766 koku. Demographically the domain had 16,896 households and 76,004 people (38,890 male / 37,114 female), of whom the samurai class held 481 households and 1,805 persons. The lone column to the right of the ○明石藩 marker — a 66-person ditto-population count surveyed 1870/10 — is the tail of the preceding Kubota (Akita) domain.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 6 (Akizuki section)
pages.page_topic: Akashi clergy/sotsu demographic tail; Akizuki kokudaka opening
pages.page_summary_en: A two-domain boundary page in Fascicle 6 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran. The right two-thirds carry the tail of Akashi domain's (明石藩) demographic register — its lower-samurai (sotsu) and religious-community counts: 905 sotsu households (population 3,226 = 1,654 male / 1,572 female), 442 Shinto shrines, 292 Buddhist halls (堂), 2 hermitages (庵), 175 temples, and household/population figures for shrine-priest (社家: 33 hh, 134 persons), miko (神子: 6 hh, 12 persons), temple clergy (寺院人口: 377 persons), and Shugendō ascetic (修驗: 17 hh, 76 persons) communities. At the ○秋月藩 marker the page turns to Akizuki domain (秋月藩), whose kokudaka opens here: base assessment (草高) 50,000 koku plus new-field land (新田高) 1,783.62539 koku, giving a total (合高) of 51,783.62539 koku. An isolated maru-marker at the far left introduces Akizuki's 現石 (actual-assessed-koku) tax section, whose text continues on the facing page. The running header names Akizuki, though most of the page's data belongs to Akashi.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Akizuki)
pages.page_topic: Akizuki domain finances: land tax, miscellaneous tax, current koku, and products
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the fascicle-6 economic survey of Akizuki (秋月藩), a Chikuzen sub-domain of Fukuoka. As a five-year average it records the regular land tax (正租) — 17,490.129 koku of rice plus 2,050.904 koku of soybeans — and the miscellaneous tax (雜税) — 1,246.266 koku of rice, 153.068 koku of soybeans, and roughly 32.27 kanme of silver, the silver re-expressed as 67.229 koku or 203.239 bales at the stated market rate of eight ryō per koku. The domain's current assessed yield (現石) is given as 20,803.741 koku, and its listed products (産物) are 1,759 kin of raw wax (cast in balls of 80 kin each) and 800 boxes of kudzu (8 shō per box). An editorial note dated 1870/12/18 flags that the domain's submitted report and the compiled main text do not agree.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, fascicle 6 (Akizuki)
pages.page_topic: Akizuki products and population / household status breakdown
pages.page_summary_en: A single-domain page for 秋月藩 (Akizuki, a ~50,000-koku sub-domain of Fukuoka in Chikuzen), from fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran. It opens with two products — laver (壽海苔) 6,000 sheets and coal (焚石) 2,000,000 kin — then gives the grand totals of 6,014 households (戸數) and 33,084 persons (人員), followed by an "of which" (内) status breakdown. The itemised statuses are shizoku 205 houses / 1,212 persons, sotsu 701 / 3,232, Shinto priests 16 / 91, temples 35 / 188 clergy, townsfolk 448 / 2,318, and Yasu-district peasants 2,317 houses / 13,394 persons across 40 villages (two of them shared-tenure villages under Fukuoka domain). Each population figure carries a male/female split; the itemised households and persons sum to about 62% of the recorded totals, so the register enumerates a coherent subset rather than the full population.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第六（朝日山）
pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, fascicle 6 (Asahiyama)
pages.page_topic: Akizuki domain demographics — district households/population, outcaste and religious counts, villages and shrines
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the demographic block of Akizuki domain (秋月藩) in Hansei Ichiran fascicle 6, covering two of its districts. Geza district (下座郡) held 679 households and 3,916 people (2,036 male, 1,880 female) across 17 villages; Kama district (嘉麻郡) held 1,613 households and 8,733 people (4,515 male, 4,218 female) across 25 villages. Recorded separately are 170 eta (outcaste) households with 965 persons (526 male, 439 female) and 33 hinin (18 male, 15 female, in 18 households counted within the peasant household total), while shugenja are folded into the temple counts; domain-wide totals given here are 82 villages (3 shared with Fukuoka domain) and 75 shrines. The ○朝日山藩 marker in the far-left margin opens the following Asahiyama-han section, and the printed page number is 29.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第六（朝日山）
pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 6 (Asahiyama)
pages.page_topic: Domain land assessment and land tax (kokudaka, komidaka, tax rice, cash, misc. tax)
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fascicle-6 fiscal entry for Asahiyama Domain (朝日山藩) in the 1870 Hansei Ichiran land-administration survey. The domain's nominal assessed yield (kusadaka) is 50,000 koku, held across 29 towns and 21 villages in Murayama District of Uzen Province and 19 villages in Sakata and Asai Districts of Ōmi Province; adding a supplementary komidaka of 580.88 koku gives a total assessed yield (gōdaka) of 50,580.88 koku, of which 5,331.66 koku is mujidaka (assessment carrying no cultivated land). On the tax side the page records land-tax rice (konomono narumai) of 13,120.38 koku, miscellaneous tax rice (zassei) of 3,047.53 koku, and cash levies in eiraku and gold; the five-year-average regular land tax (seiso, in current koku) is 16,172.32 koku.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第六（朝日山）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (Hansei Ichiran), fascicle 6, Asahiyama section
pages.page_topic: Asahiyama domain — tax subtotals, population and household counts (fascicle 6 civil tail)
pages.page_summary_en: The left half of printed page 31 completes the fascicle-6 civil return for 朝日山藩 (Asahiyama, a small Echigo domain). It closes the fiscal section — miscellaneous tax of 50 ryo 2 bu 1 shu in gold; a large eisen figure of 479 kan 230 mon 3 bu 2 rin 7 mo; a combined "gold-and-eisen" subtotal (529 ryo 3 bu / 42.8 mon) with its rice equivalent (282 bales); and a two-portion rice total (二口合) of 43,488 bales — then gives the demographics: 6,797 households and 35,874 people (17,940 male, 17,934 female). Of these it itemizes the warrior class (士族, 272 households / 1,398 persons) and foot-soldiers (卒, 401 households / 1,794 persons), each with an internally consistent male/female split. No maru-marker appears, so the entire page is 朝日山 data.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第六（朝日山）
pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō (Table of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 6 (Asahiyama)
pages.page_topic: Households & population by social class; shrines and temples (Asahiyama)
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the household-and-population return for Asahiyama Domain (朝日山藩) in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran; the running header names 朝日山, and MASTER confirms the whole page is this single domain. A subtotal at the top (合) records 673 households and 3,192 persons (1,511 male, 1,681 female) — most plausibly the warrior/administrative classes (士族・卒) whose class-by-class breakdown ran on the preceding page. The commoner (平民) entry gives 5,347 households and 28,401 persons (14,182 male, 14,219 female), spread across Murayama district in Uzen and the Sakata and Asai districts in Ōmi, plus one outcast (非人) household of a single person counted separately. The shrine-and-temple (社寺) section, sited within Murayama district of Uzen, lists 7 Shinto shrines and 137 Buddhist temples totalling 748 households and 4,775 persons, itemised as 175 shrine, 569 temple, and 4 Nishinomiya grand-kagura-master households.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 6 — filed under the Amagasaki (尼崎) section, though most of the page completes the preceding Asahiyama (朝日山藩) entry: shrine/temple lands and clergy, village and town counts.
pages.page_topic: Asahiyama shrine/temple lands & clergy, village/town counts; opening of the Amagasaki entry
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page of fascicle 6 mostly completes the entry for Asahiyama (朝日山藩): it records the domain's religious establishment — 11 shrines, 3,051 koku of shrine land (社領) and 3,559 koku of temple land (寺領) — together with the attached clergy (2 Shinto priests and 41 Buddhist monks, plus their women and servants), and geographic counts of 40 villages and 29 towns. A double-column note explains that the 40 villages are scattered across Murayama district in Uzen (Dewa) and the Sakata and Asai districts of Ōmi, and a closing line states that Asahiyama's household and population totals were given on the preceding page. At the lower left the ○尼崎藩 marker opens the Amagasaki entry, giving its assessed yield of 40,000 koku (草高) and a territory of 84 villages across five districts of Settsu. The running margin header files the page under the Amagasaki (尼崎) section.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, fascicle 6 (Amagasaki)
pages.page_topic: Amagasaki kokudaka breakdown, land & miscellaneous taxes, households and population (fasc. 6)
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page continues the Amagasaki (尼崎藩) civil/economic register in fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran; the ○尼崎藩 boundary marker and the 草高 total stand on the facing right page (lower_p029_right), so every column here belongs to Amagasaki. The domain's assessed land is split between Settsu-province holdings (5 districts, 84 villages = 38,301.47939 koku) and Harima-province holdings (3 districts, 50 villages = 13,180.593 koku), which together with 1.0 koku of newly-reclaimed field yield the combined total of 51,483.07239 koku. The five-year-average tax take is a regular land tax of 25,722.98685 koku of rice plus 1,104.36862 kan-mon in cash, and miscellaneous taxes of 1,871.12069 koku of rice plus 162.447212 kan-mon in cash. The page closes with 10,613 households and a population of 49,403, followed by an 内 ("of which") marker that opens the status breakdown continuing on the next spread.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview, Fascicle 6 (Amagasaki)
pages.page_topic: Amagasaki domain population by legal status (households and persons)
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fascicle-6 demographic table for Amagasaki domain (尼崎藩), recording households (戸數) and persons (人員) by legal status. The noble house (華族) numbers 4 (1 male, 3 female); the samurai class (士族) 360 households / 1,742 persons, and the lower-samurai (卒) 287 households / 1,376 persons. Commoners (平民) dominate at 9,767 households and 45,759 persons, alongside 24 Shinto-priest (社家) households (89 persons), 175 Buddhist-temple (寺院) households (437 persons), and the Edo-period outcaste groups eta (穢多, 602 households / 2,715 persons) and hinin (非人, 71 households). Every population total is split into male (男) and female (女) counts that sum exactly to the printed total.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Administration Survey (Hansei Ichiran), Table/Fascicle 6 (Ashimori)
pages.page_topic: Ashimori kokudaka block; tail of Amagasaki villages/shrines/personnel
pages.page_summary_en: This page from Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran opens the entry for Ashimori Domain (足守藩) in Bitchū province, signalled by the circle-marker ○足守藩. Ashimori's nominal assessment is 25,000 koku; adding 5,898.689 koku of reassessed new fields (改高新田) gives a stated total (合) of 30,898.689 koku (25,000 + 5,898.689 = 30,898.689). Of that holding, 13,855.1035 koku is recorded as 29 villages in Kayō district, Bitchū, with a further 5,894.33 koku of reclaimed new field (改出新田) in the same district. The columns to the right of the marker complete the preceding Amagasaki Domain (尼崎藩) entry: 134 villages, 324 shrines plus 237 branch shrines, and 207 personnel (114 male, 93 female; 114 + 93 = 207).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran, Table No. 6 (Ashimori)
pages.page_topic: Fascicle-6 land tax and kokudaka return — Ashimori domain, including its Iwashiro/Shinobu exclave
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the fascicle-6 (land-tax / kokudaka) return for Ashimori domain (足守藩). The right-hand block gives a grand-total kokudaka of 19,749.4335 koku (○合), a five-year-average land tax (正租) of 8,182.1998 koku in genmai, miscellaneous tax (雜税) of 1.69775 koku, gold (金) 173 ryō, and Eiraku cash (永) 84 mon. The left-hand block itemizes the domain's exclave in Shinobu district of Iwashiro province: 11 villages assessed at 11,144.8965 koku (高) plus 4.359 koku of newly-opened paddy (外高), subtotalling 11,149.2555 koku (○合), with its own five-year-average land tax of 1,880.1284 koku. The internal check reconciles exactly (11,144.8965 + 4.359 = 11,149.2555). Both ○ symbols mark subtotals, not domain boundaries; no maru+藩 domain marker appears, so the whole page belongs to Ashimori.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (Hansei Ichiran), fascicle 6, Ashimori (足守) section — running margin header (provenance)
pages.page_topic: Products, miscellaneous-goods taxes, grand total, and household count (産物・雑品税・戸数)
pages.page_summary_en: The tail of Ashimori domain's (足守藩, a ~25,000-koku Bitchū domain of the Kinoshita house) fascicle-6 civil entry. It lists the domain's products — raw cotton, cotton cloth, lamp oil, cast-metal pots/kettles, and charcoal/firewood for the home territory, plus oil-pressing, fishing, and water-wheels for a detached holding at Iwashiro-Senoue (岩代瀬上) — and the miscellaneous-goods taxes on them: 1.69775 koku of rice and 173 ryō / 84 mon in cash for the home territory, and 67 kan 474 mon 6 bu of Eiraku cash for the exclave (noted as already included in the total). The grand total (惣計) tax is 701 ryō 3 bu 1 shu plus 31 mon 6 bu, and the household count is 4,324. No maru-marker appears on the page: the entire sheet belongs to Ashimori, and the running header reads 藩制一覽表第六（足守）.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, fascicle 6 (Ashimori)
pages.page_topic: Population & household register (足守藩)
pages.page_summary_en: This page from fascicle 6 (人員/demographics) of the Hansei Ichiran records the household-and-population return of 足守藩 (Ashimori, a ~25,000-koku domain of the Kinoshita house in Bicchū). Total registered population (人員) = 17,453. Of this, the samurai orders are 士族 (153 households / 633 persons: M 301, F 332) and 卒 (151 households / 347 persons: M 215, F 132), giving a samurai subtotal of 304 households / 980 persons (M 516, F 464 — fully internally consistent). The commoner (平民) population is reported for two districts: the home district 備中國賀陽郡 (3,111 households / 12,139 persons: M 6,327, F 5,812) and a detached holding — a post-Boshin administrative assignment — in 岩代國信夫郡 (823 houses / 4,254 persons printed), combined into a commoner-household total of 3,934 (= 3,111 + 823). The 岩代 enclave block is internally inconsistent: its printed male 2,188 + female 2,606 = 4,794, its own printed district total reads 4,254, and the grand-total arithmetic (17,453 − 980 − 12,139) implies 4,334 — three irreconcilable figures, a source-level error flagged here.

pages.page_header_en: Han-System Overview, Fascicle 6 (Ashimori)
pages.page_topic: Ashimori religious institutions, households, population, outcastes, and governor's family
pages.page_summary_en: A continuation page of the Ashimori (足守藩) entry in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei ichiran, covering religious institutions and demographic totals for the domain's holdings across two provinces (printed in abbreviation as 備 and 岩). It records a populace (人口) of 16,393 (8,515 male / 7,878 female), 30 shrines, and 85 temples (11 of them unoccupied), with clergy comprising 73 monks, 16 shugendō practitioners (10 male / 6 female), 2 nuns, and 61 shrine attendants across 21 households (33 male / 28 female); a marginal note flags that one temple is Jōdo Shinshū. The two-province combined section (兩國合) gives 4,324 households and a total personnel count (人員) of 17,453, plus 290 outcastes (穢多; 154 male / 136 female) with a note of 2 more besides, and a governor's family of 4 (2 male / 2 female).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Akō)
pages.page_topic: Land tax and rice revenue (fiscal)
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fiscal (land-tax and revenue) block for Akō Domain (赤穂藩), a 20,000-koku domain in Harima province, from Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran-hyō. Against a nominal assessment (草高) of 20,000 koku, the five-year-average regular land tax (正租) is 8,404.9306 koku of rice, with a further 914.53306 koku of supplementary income (外ニ) drawn from inspection-assessed fields, floodplain fields, and salt-flats covering 341 chō 3 tan 9 se 3 bu. Additional rice levies are the kuchimai surtax (口米, 197.3704 koku, same average), corvée-labor rice (夫米, 497.5452 koku), and a small fishing-net levy (網役米, 0.596 koku). All revenue figures are stated as five-year averages in rice equivalent (現米).

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Akō)
pages.page_topic: Akō domain — fascicle 6 miscellaneous rice & cash revenues (salt levies, product taxes, grand totals)
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the Fascicle 6 (economic) entry for Akō domain (赤穂藩), listing its miscellaneous rice and cash revenues. Rice levies comprise a grass-land levy (草米, 16.366 koku), boatmen's rice (水主米, 154.8 koku), and an upland levy (山手番, 23.055 koku); the salt-flat levy (鹽濱運上) yielded 813 ryō 2 bu plus 110 mon, with a marginal note that this levy was abolished and replaced by a new 3,000-ryō salt tax (鹽稅金). A combined cash levy on four commercial items — rice brokerage (米仲買), sardine nets (鰯網), sake brewing (酒造), and a pine-branch license (松枝冥加) — totaled 14 ryō 3 bu 3 shu plus 205 mon, and the domain held 11 forest sites (山林) and 4 groves (籔). The grand totals are 10,209.19626 koku of rice (惣合米) and 828 ryō 1 bu 3 shu plus 315 mon in cash (惣合金); the salt-flat levy plus the four-item levy reconcile exactly to the cash grand total.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 6 (Akō)
pages.page_topic: Akō domain: cultivated area, households/population by status, temple & shrine land, salt product
pages.page_summary_en: This is a continuation page of the Akō (赤穂) domain entry in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran survey (printed page 45); it carries no domain marker, and the running header 藩制一覧表第六（赤穂） confirms the whole leaf belongs to Akō. It records the domain's total cultivated area (反別 ≈ 11.77 chō), a household-and-population block broken down by status — shizoku 580 persons / 132 households, sotsu 433 / 129, lower sotsu (下卒) 649 / 214, with printed totals of 1,657 persons and 475 households — and tax-exempt land grants: temple land (寺領) 81.846 koku and shrine land (社領) 59.4246 koku, each with its own cultivated-area sub-note, totalling (惣計) 211.5768 koku. The domain's notable product (産物) is salt (鹽), for which Akō was historically renowned. The household sub-counts reconcile exactly to 475, but the status populations sum to 1,662 against the stated total of 1,657 — a five-person discrepancy internal to the source.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Akō)
pages.page_topic: Commoner & religious demographics, households, livestock (Akō)
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page completes the fascicle-6 civil-demographic register for Akō (赤穂藩), read right to left. It tallies commoners (平民: 7,266 households, 32,211 persons), outcastes (穢多: 104 households, 486 persons), livestock (1,492 cattle, 28 horses), 45 Shinto shrines, shrine-priest families (社家: 8 households, 35 persons), Shugendō practitioners (修驗: 2 households, 11 persons), 48 Buddhist temples with 324 clergy, and the governor's own household (知事初家族: 13 persons). The closing grand totals record 7,896 households (the 48 temples included) and 33,067 persons; the latter excludes the governor's household per the note 但知事ハ除ク. Every male/female split and the population grand total reconcile exactly (32,211+486+35+11+324 = 33,067).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran Table, Fascicle 6 (Ayabe)
pages.page_topic: Ayabe domain — kokudaka and land-tax survey
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the complete kokudaka-and-tax entry for Ayabe domain (綾部藩, Tanba province, Kuki house). The nominal assessed base (草高) is 19,500 koku; two supplements — Shimada-allotment rice (島田分米込高, 1,506.742 koku) and new-field additional yield (新田改出高, 55.43896 koku) — bring the grand total (合) to 21,062.18096 koku, of which 1,724.462 koku is untaxed-land koku (無地高). Petty imposts (小物成高) amount to 298.99 koku, equal to about 2 kan 989.9 monme in silver (10 monme/koku). The five-year-average tax figures are regular land tax 4,530.7782 koku (genmai), silver-paid regular tax 1,075.304 koku, soybeans 512.7 koku, and miscellaneous taxes 1,412.4468 koku, with a note that silver payments were consolidated at a rate of 8 ryō per koku.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Ayabe)
pages.page_topic: Ayabe domain — tax rice, silver, products, shrines/temples, households and population (fascicle 6)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the fascicle-6 fiscal, product and demographic record for Ayabe (綾部) domain, a small Tanba han. Its total net tax rice (合現米) is 7,160.959 koku and its silver revenue 2,989.9 monme; the three listed products — tea, silk thread and cotton — are entered only as qualitative notes recording that output is limited and that no fixed quota can readily be set. The domain contains 4,284 households and 18,373 people, of whom the shizoku number 762 (367 male, 395 female) living in 153 households. Religious establishments comprise 72 shrines and 39 temples (one of them Ikkō-shū), endowed with 36 koku of shrine-and-temple land.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Han Administration at a Glance, Fascicle 6 (Ayabe)
pages.page_topic: Sotsu and commoner (heimin) population, households and religious institutions by district — Ayabe domain
pages.page_summary_en: Continuation page of the Ayabe (綾部) demographic section, fascicle 6; it carries NO maru-marker, so all fifteen data columns belong to Ayabe. It opens with the sotsu (卒) status class: 323 persons (156 male, 167 female) in 67 households. The commoner (平民) block is then broken out by the two Tanba districts of the domain. Ikaruga-gun (何鹿郡, 9 villages): 8,914 commoners (4,404 male / 4,510 female) in 2,156 households, with 47 shrines (15 attendants: 7 m / 8 f), 24 temples (of which 1 Ikkō-shū), 56 monks and 9 nuns. Amata-gun (天田郡, 18 villages, marked 同上 "ditto"): 7,311 commoners (3,649 male / 3,662 female) in 1,674 households, with 24 shrines (16 attendants: 7 m / 9 f). Every male+female split reconciles exactly to its stated total.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 6 — (Annaka)
pages.page_topic: Ayabe demographics tail and Annaka kokudaka opening (fascicle 6)
pages.page_summary_en: This page closes Ayabe's fascicle-6 population block and opens Annaka's entry. Reading right to left, it finishes Ayabe's Amata-district holdings (10 temples, 23 monks, 6 nuns), then records the detached Funai-district holding: 4 villages with 469 people (235 male, 234 female), 101 houses, 1 shrine with 5 shrine personnel (2 male, 3 female), and 5 temples with 8 monks. Domain-wide outcaste entries follow — 450 eta (204 male, 246 female; 102 households) and 144 hinin (79 male, 65 female; 31 households) — plus the governor's family of 10 (4 males, one of them the governor himself, and 6 females). After the ○安中藩 marker, Annaka's block begins with a kusadaka of 30,000 koku (17,000 koku castle-attached, 13,000 koku in Shimōsa) and a supplementary output assessment (komidaka, new fields, and re-survey increases) of 3,125.7415 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Table No. 6 (Annaka)
pages.page_topic: Annaka Domain taxes, products, and exempt land (Table 6 continuation)
pages.page_summary_en: Continuation of Annaka Domain's entry in Table 6 of the Hansei Ichiran (1870 domain survey). The page completes the land-register figures — 970 chō 4 tan 8 bu of assessed acreage for the supplementary parcel and a combined total (合高) of 33,125.7415 koku — then reports the five-year-average regular tax: 7,311.683 koku in actual rice plus 2,611 kan 360 mon in cash, each followed by a red-ink deduction line (3,948.161 koku and 383 kan 7 mon of assorted deductions). Miscellaneous taxes add 328 kan 450 mon in ei cash and 284 kan 674 mon in copper coin. The products section lists raw silk and silkworm-egg cards (untaxed, per the printed note), and tax-exempt lands are located within Usui and Gunma districts of Kōzuke Province.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Survey Table No. 6 (Annaka)
pages.page_topic: Shrine-temple exempt land, temple and shrine-personnel counts, household and population totals
pages.page_summary_en: Continuation of the Annaka domain entry in fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran (1870 Dajōkan domain survey). The page records shrine-temple exempt land: 38 chō 6 tan 9 se 23 bu in the main holdings plus 8 chō 4 tan 7 [bu] in the domain's detached districts of Sōsa, Katori, and Kaijō (printed as Shimotsuke Province, evidently a misprint for Shimōsa), combining to a printed total of 47 chō 1 bu (the components sum to exactly 47 chō 1 tan). It further lists 42 Buddhist temples (of which 4 Shugendō practitioners), one additional temple, 10 and 13 shrine personnel, temples in 73 villages with one temple on exempt land under another authority's administration, and the domain totals of 6,035 households and 27,034 persons; an editorial note marks three of the temple-shrine lines as red marginal writing in the original manuscript.

pages.page_header_en: Han Governance Survey, Table 6 (Annaka)
pages.page_topic: Annaka domain demographics: households and population by status group
pages.page_summary_en: Continuation of the Annaka domain entry in fascicle 6 (households and population) of the Hansei Ichiran. The page records 158 shizoku households (709 persons: 333 male, 376 female) and 76 sotsu households (252 persons: 130 male, 122 female), totalled in the source as 234 households and 961 persons (463 male, 498 female); all sums are internally consistent. Commoners number 5,499 houses with 25,103 persons (12,941 male, 12,162 female); shrine personnel 112 persons (58 male, 54 female) in 35 households. The religious establishment comprises 110 Buddhist temples (32 holding vermillion-seal grants, 47 without resident priest) and 18 yamabushi households (1 with a vermillion seal), with a temple-and-yamabushi population printed as 123 (55 monks, 16 males, 17 yamabushi, 34 females — components sum to 122, one short of the printed total). Printed book page 53.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Administration Survey, Table 6 (Asada)
pages.page_topic: End of Annaka's civil block (outcastes, shrines, villages, governor's family) and start of Asada's kokudaka
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-6 page closes Annaka Domain's civil-survey block and opens Asada Domain's. For Annaka it records 157 outcaste (eta/hinin) households totalling 735 persons (375 male, 360 female), 97 shrines (79 in Kōzuke Province, 18 in Shimōsa), and 65 villages (42 in Kōzuke, 23 in Shimōsa) besides the post town of Annaka-juku, ending with the governor's family of five (the governor, his heir, his wife, and two daughters). Left of the ○麻田藩 marker, Asada Domain's block begins with a kusadaka of 10,807.519 koku plus 415.849 koku of newly developed field assessment, for a combined total of 11,223.368 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Administration Survey, Table 6 (Asada)
pages.page_topic: Asada domain five-year-average tax receipts, households, and population
pages.page_summary_en: Continuation of the Asada domain (麻田藩, a small Settsu-province domain) entry in fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran. The page records five-year-average annual receipts: a regular land tax of 5,208.592 koku of rice — of which 5,145.604 koku fell under fixed (jōmen) assessment — plus miscellaneous taxes of 6.1274 koku in rice, 5 ryō 2 bu 2 shu in gold, and 113 kan 248 mon in copper cash, the money items being explained as license (unjō) and myōga fees on ponds and rivers, sake brewing, and water mills, all noted as fixed annual payments. It then opens the demographic block: 2,228 households and a population of 10,341 persons, split 5,272 male and 5,069 female, with the status-class breakdown continuing on the following page.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran Table, Fascicle 6 (Asō)
pages.page_topic: Population by status group (Asada Domain)
pages.page_summary_en: Continuation of Asada Domain's (麻田藩, Settsu Province, ~10,000 koku) fascicle-6 status census. The page enumerates households and persons by legal status: shizoku 77 households / 313 persons, sotsu 60 / 148, shrine priests 5 / 20, Buddhist temples 51 with 85 clergy (54 monks, 17 women, 3 laymen, 11 nuns), Shugendō practitioners 1 household / 2 persons, commoners 2,034 households / 9,773 persons, and — recorded separately with the prefix 外ニ — eta outcastes 89 households / 415 persons, for roughly 10,756 persons in all. The domain's army is a single platoon of 72 men (12 of them officers), noted as already counted within the shizoku and sotsu rows, and 29 Shinto shrines are listed excluding branch shrines. The ○麻生藩 marker at the far left opens Asō Domain (Hitachi Province), whose data begins on the following page.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Survey Table, Fascicle 6 (Asō)
pages.page_topic: Asō domain kokudaka, land-tax and household/population totals
pages.page_summary_en: Opening data page of the Asō domain block (a small Hitachi-province domain) in fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran. Its assessed yield (kusadaka) is 14,582.2585 koku including komi-daka and new fields; after deductions for wasteland, the jin'ya compound and kuwashita exemptions the taxable remainder is 11,769.0162 koku.
