The combined take (toriai) is 4,618.796 koku of rice plus 30.6486 kan-mon in ei cash (converted at 2.5 koku per kan-mon), of which the regular land tax is 3,945.1066 koku — exactly 11,271.733 bales at 3 to 5 shō per bale — plus 32.28294 kan-mon, with miscellaneous taxes of 22 ryō 3 bu 1 shu in gold, 34.0276 kan-mon in ei, and 12.36 kan-mon in copper cash. The page closes with 1,723 households and a population of 9,092, beside which the 1928 editors note the original manuscript carried 9,249 in red ink.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran Table, Fascicle 6 (Asō)
pages.page_topic: Asō Domain population status breakdown, shrines, temples, and infantry
pages.page_summary_en: Continuation of the Asō Domain (Hitachi Province) entry in fascicle 6, giving the status breakdown of the domain population of 9,092 reported at the end of the previous page. The listed statuses are shizoku 405 (234 male, 171 female), sotsu 195 (142 male, 53 female), shrine functionaries 36, Buddhist clergy 29, shugen ascetics 3, blind 1, eta 15 (in 4 households), and hinin 19 (in 2 households); the domain also counts 12 shrines and 68 temples. According to the 1928 editor's marginal note, the parenthesized entries reproduce passages written in red ink in the original 1870 manuscript, among them the note that the figures were revised on the basis of the survey of the ninth month of Kōgo (Meiji 3, autumn 1870). The military line records a single infantry platoon of 60 men with 10 officers.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Table 6 (Ashikaga)
pages.page_topic: Ashikaga domain tax rice, taxes, households, and status populations
pages.page_summary_en: The Hansei Ichiran fascicle-6 block for Ashikaga domain (Shimotsuke). It records tax rice on a five-year-average basis across the domain's four districts — 15,112.73728 koku in total, an annual mean of 3,022.54746 koku, equivalent to 8,635.32295 bales — plus miscellaneous taxes of 7 kan 178.18 mon in permanent cash, 4,058 households, and a population of 17,878 (printed male/female split 8,765/9,014, which sums only to 17,779 — an inconsistency in the source print). Separately noted "besides" the main counts are 53 eta households with 262 persons (printed split 148/122) and 419 shizoku (211 male, 208 female). An artillery squad of 36 men belonging to the preceding Asō domain's block overflows onto the head of the page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Institutions Survey (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 6 (Ashikaga)
pages.page_topic: Ashikaga population by status; religious institutions and special-status households
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-6 continuation page for Ashikaga Domain (Shimotsuke Province) records a demographic and religious-institution breakdown. It lists 114 shizoku (samurai) households and 37 sotsu households comprising 108 persons (60 male, 48 female). The religious/special-status section gives 18 Shinto-priest households (70 persons: 34 male, 36 female), 81 Buddhist temples with 79 monks, 3 hermitages (庵), 5 dormitory-halls (寮), 1 nenbutsu hall, and 267 shrines (small shrines included); plus special-status households of 4 ferrymen (船越), 13 bell-ringers (鉦打), 5 monkey-trainers (猿引), and 1 shrine-attendant. Marginal notes state that Shinto priests and the categories below are counted within the domain totals, and flag the following twelve lines as vermilion writing in the original.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 6 — Anji (安志藩)
pages.page_topic: kokudaka and school/temple land holdings with five-year average revenue
pages.page_summary_en: Left half of a fascicle-6 fiscal-survey spread carrying the seam between two domains. The right-hand columns close out the Ashikaga Domain (足利藩) block: a 100-koku school-land holding in Ashikaga district yielding 14.09175 koku of rice plus 12 ryō 2 bu 2 shu in gold and 543 mon in cash, temple-held land (寺院受領高) of 232.836 koku, and five-year-average totals of 74.24451 koku of rice, 6.25 ryō in gold, 10,530.463 mon in ei accounting cash, and 71,753 mon in zeni. Left of the ○安志藩 marker the Anji Domain block opens: a grass yield (草高) of 10,000 koku lying within three districts of Harima Province, an additional 9.69465 koku of new-field yield (新田高), and a combined assessment (合高) of 10,009.69465 koku — the components sum exactly. Anji's own five-year-average section is headed at the far left and its figures continue on the following page.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Anshi)
pages.page_topic: Anshi domain land tax, miscellaneous taxes, and products
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fiscal survey of Anshi (安志) domain, a small 10,000-koku fudai holding in Harima province. Its regular land tax (正租) is reported as 4,967.493 koku of actual rice (a fixed-rate assessment that varies with disaster years and is paid entirely in kind), and its miscellaneous tax (雜稅) as 6.231 koku of rice plus 163.9375 ryō in cash (163兩3分3朱 with a 2.972-monme silver remainder), the cash converting to 20.4959 koku at an 8-ryō-per-koku rate. Summing these components yields the printed present-koku total (現石合) of 4,994.2199 koku, an internal check that reconciles exactly. The domain's products — sedge-thread (菅絲), tea, tobacco, and soy sauce — are all untaxed, with a note that paper-money borrowing the previous year prompted efforts to market these goods and build up commerce.

pages.page_header_en: Han-System Survey Table, Fascicle 6 (Anshi)
pages.page_topic: Anshi Domain population and household census
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the demographic return for Anshi Domain (安志藩, Harima Province; Hansei Ichiran fascicle 6), a small ~10,000-koku Ogasawara holding. It records 2,596 total households and a population of 10,037. The breakdown gives shizoku 67 households / 274 persons, sotsu 74 / 252, sub-sotsu retainers (卒以下) 44 / 102 — together 185 households and 635 persons (the latter figure including the 7 monks of the domain's 3 prayer-temples) — plus commoners (平民) 2,367 households / 9,254 persons and 43 shrine-attendants (社人). Marginal notes state that shrine/temple stipendiaries are combined into the household total and that shrine-attendants, monks, and eta are counted within the population, which accounts for the 44-household and ~105-person shortfall between the itemised classes and the grand totals.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 6 (Asao)
pages.page_topic: Anshi domain administrative summary (tail) and Asao domain kokudaka (head)
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page of Fascicle 6 spans two domains: it completes the administrative summary of Anshi Domain (安志藩) and opens the entry for Asao Domain (浅尾藩), whose block begins at the ○淺尾藩 circle-marker. The Anshi fields (right of the marker) record 82 temple clergy (男42 + 女40), 8 shrine-priest households, 21 temples, 47 villages, 12 outcaste (eta) households, and 50 troops (10 of them officers), followed by its officials — a vacant governor (知事) line, 1 senior councillor (大参事), 2 acting senior councillors (権大参事), and a note that junior-councillor (小参事) posts are omitted as low-grade appointments in a small domain. The Asao fields (left of the marker) give a base assessment of 10,000 koku (per the 1869/巳-year survey), a revised addition of 98.93874 koku for a total of 10,098.93874 koku, and a rice land-tax of 3,574.92098 koku. The eta population is printed as 17 (十七) but its male/female split (36 + 34) sums to 70, indicating a 十七/七十 transposition in the movable-type print.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Asao)
pages.page_topic: Asao Domain: population, households, temples/shrines, outcaste groups, and tax totals
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf records the 1870 Hansei Ichiran (藩制一覧表, fascicle 6) survey figures for Asao Domain (浅尾藩, a small Bitchū domain). It reports 1,642 households and a population of 6,674 (3,550 male, 3,124 female) across 16 villages, together with 26 Buddhist temples (36 monks, 2 nuns) and 133 Shinto shrines. Small status-group populations are listed separately: 7 shrine-attendant households (20 persons), 96 eta households, and 39 onbo households. Fiscal totals are 3,907.07 koku of rice (合米) and 833.11 ryō of money (合金), with a principal money levy of 764 ryō and miscellaneous taxes of 100.68 koku and 67 ryō. (The eta population's printed total, 311, does not match its male+female subtotal of 211 — an internal inconsistency in the source.)

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 6 (Sakura)
pages.page_topic: Sakura domain taxes, households, religious institutions, and population
pages.page_summary_en: This continuation page of fascicle 6 (第六) records the fiscal and demographic returns of Sakura domain (佐倉藩). Regular tax (正稅) was 47,265.618 koku of rice plus 2,343.757 kan of eiraku cash; miscellaneous tax (雜稅) comprised 2,442.308 koku of rice, 604.626 kan of eiraku cash, 49.125 ryō of gold, 1,213.235 kan of copper cash, and 16.995 koku of salt. The domain held 19,791 households and a population of 111,265 persons. Under an "of which" (内) marker the page lists religious institutions: 21 Shinto priests (神主), 16 shrine officials (神職), 9 shrine families (社家), 501 temples, 40 mountain ascetics (修驗), and 1 onmyōji.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Survey (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 6 (Sakura) — outer running header / provenance
pages.page_topic: Sakura domain: population male/female split, clergy & special-status head-counts, and shizoku/sotsu household and population totals
pages.page_summary_en: A single-domain continuation page for Sakura (佐倉藩), fascicle 6 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran survey. It opens with the 内 breakdown of the domain's total population — 55,724 men and 54,976 women (110,700 total; the grand total itself sits on the preceding right-hand page) — then enumerates religious and special-status groups in two stacked registers: 24 kannushi, 16 shinshoku, 19 shrine attendants, 362 Buddhist monks, 39 Shugendō ascetics, 53 physicians, 1 onmyōji, 11 dancer-priests, 20 zatō, 9 blind persons, 10 dōshin, and 1 nun. It closes with the warrior tallies — 521 shizoku households (3,021 persons: 1,502 M / 1,519 F) and 1,110 sotsu households (4,469 persons: 2,763 M / 1,706 F) — plus one monkey-trainer household (10 persons) and one leprosy-afflicted household (7 persons). Every 内 male/female warichu sum-checks against its parent total.

pages.page_header_en: Han Regulations Overview, Fascicle 6 (Shinoyama)
pages.page_topic: Shinoyama kokudaka, land tax and products; tail of Sakura demographic fields
pages.page_summary_en: The right-hand (earlier-read) columns complete the tail of Sakura domain (佐倉藩): 19 districts, 738 shrines (a figure originally in vermilion, plus 53 shrine-places held in common), 21 eta households totalling 156 persons (73 male, 83 female), and 14 hinin households totalling 81 persons (42 male, 39 female). The circular marker ○篠山藩 then opens Shinoyama domain, whose scattered holdings lay in Tanba, Settsu and Tajima provinces. Shinoyama's assessed kokudaka is 60,000 koku plus 8,222.17626 koku of newly-reclaimed land, totalling 68,222.17626 koku (合高); regular land tax in rice (正租) is 30,898.79233 koku and miscellaneous rice taxes (雜稅) 5,390.16026 koku, with cash dues (永) of 204 kan 860 mon 9 bu, charcoal 372 bales, and firewood 7,757.3 loads. A marginal note dates the Shinoyama figures to the Kōgo (1870) 10th-month survey.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle (Table) 6 (Sasayama)
pages.page_topic: Sasayama domain: notable (untaxed) products and household census by status
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page continues the Sasayama-domain (篠山藩) return in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran. The upper-right column heads a list of the domain's notable products, all flagged as untaxed (右無税): tea 13,500 kanme, raw silk 410 kanme, ceramics 7,500 packloads (駄), tobacco 34,400 kin, and cocoons 1,779.5 kanme. The remainder is a household census totalling 13,616 households (戸數), broken down (内) by status: 413 shizoku, 495 sotsu, 11,840 commoners (農工商), 269 temples, plus small counts of shrine families (19), yamabushi (3), onmyōji (4), crematory/grave keepers (23), outcaste watchmen (41) and 509 eta. The ten status components sum exactly to the printed 13,616 total.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第六（佐土原）
pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Sadowara)
pages.page_topic: Sasayama population/status breakdown and Sadowara kokudaka/land-tax
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand leaf of Fascicle 6 straddles two domains, divided by the single ○佐土原藩 domain-marker. To the RIGHT of the marker lies the tail of Sasayama-han's (篠山藩) demographic block: a total population of 58,723 persons, broken down by status into commoners (農工商 52,281), shizoku (2,158), sotsu (1,466), eta (2,204), Buddhist clergy (267), non-persons/guards (208), cremators (61), yin-yang diviners (19), shrine households (53) and mountain ascetics (9), together with 166 Shinto shrines. To the LEFT of the marker begins Sadowara-han's (佐土原藩) fiscal block: an assessed yield (高) of 27,070.713 koku carrying a 183.466-koku revised deduction (改減高引) and 6,375.5462 koku of additional yield (外二高), with land tax (正租) of 17,055.35265 koku paid in rice. The printed status sub-counts sum to 58,726, three above the stated 58,723 total — a minor source-level non-footing. Printed page number 74.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第六（佐土原）
pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview, Fascicle 6 (Sadowara)
pages.page_topic: Products, miscellaneous taxes, samurai households, and population
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fascicle-6 (economic) survey for Sadowara Domain (佐土原藩), a small Hyūga-province domain. The right-hand columns close out the domain's tribute/tax figures — soybeans 3,605.79135 koku, salt 50.29606 koku, and a cash levy of 9,108.924 kan-mon — after which the section header 諸産物及諸税 ("various products and taxes") introduces paper (800 rolls, at 6,000 sheets per roll), half-cut paper (500 rolls, at 11,000 sheets per roll), and raw wax (3,000 jin), all recorded as five-year averages, plus a five-year-average miscellaneous forest/river/marsh tax of 5,329.124 kan-mon. It closes with 854 samurai (shizoku) households and a total population of 3,778 (male 1,893; female 1,881 — the printed total exceeds the male+female sum by four).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran, fascicle 6 (Saijō)
pages.page_topic: Sadowara household/population demographics by status; Saijō kokudaka opening
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page of fascicle 6 closes the civil register of Sadowara Domain (佐土原藩, a Shimazu cadet branch in Hyūga) and opens that of Saijō Domain (西條藩, a Kishū-Tokugawa branch in Iyo). The Sadowara block, read right-to-left, tabulates households and population by status: 883 sotsu (lower-samurai) households totalling 3,133 persons (1,715 m / 1,418 f), 5,171 commoner households totalling 18,666 persons (9,583 m / 9,083 f), 209 shrine (Shintō) households totalling 806 persons (437 m / 369 f), and 8 temples with 37 persons (33 m / 4 f); every male-plus-female pair sums exactly to its stated total. Left of the ○西條藩 boundary marker, Saijō's entry begins with an assessed yield (高) of 40,801.8 koku, of which 30,000 koku is the anciently-granted amount (前々拝領高) and 3,149.99 koku the honden-included figure (本田込高), the remaining breakdown carrying onto the facing page. A vermilion editorial note records that the figures derive from the tenth-month survey of the Snake year (Meiji 2 / 1869).

pages.page_header_en: Han Survey Table, Fascicle 6 (Saijō)
pages.page_topic: Saijō domain — land tax, miscellaneous taxes, and samurai/soldier household and population counts
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand sheet continues the Saijō (西條) domain entry in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei ichiran. It records the domain's regular land tax (正租) of 16,913.966 koku of rice, together with a new-paddy/reassessed-output increment of 7,651.81 koku and roughly 209 chō of village land left unassessed because its yield was not fixed. Miscellaneous cash taxes are itemized as 923.32 ryō (fixed minor imposts), 192.01 ryō (variable imposts), and 635.03 ryō (mountain-district dues), plus an occasional-tax item of 32.10 koku of rice. Household and population figures are given for the samurai class (shizoku: 292 houses, 1,501 people — 709 male, 792 female) and the soldier classes (heisotsu: 153 houses, 725 people — 361 male, 364 female; keisotsu: 295 houses). The printed folio number is 77.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Saijō)
pages.page_topic: Saijō domain: population, status-tier personnel breakdown, and religious households
pages.page_summary_en: A continuation page of the fascicle-6 demographic entry for Saijō Domain (西條藩). It opens with a samurai-class personnel total (士族人員) of 1,252 — 615 male, 637 female — followed by a nine-line breakdown that was originally written in red ink in the manuscript and here parenthesized as marginal entries. The breakdown gives civil officials (文官), troops (兵隊), and unassigned/no-post men (無役) across three status tiers: shizoku (104 / 85 / 183), heisotsu foot-soldiers (79 / 46 / 72), and keisotsu light-troops (111 / 106 / 147); the 兵隊 counts also note platoon strengths (2, 1, and 2 small platoons). The page closes with religious households: 28 Shinto-priest houses (社家) holding 137 people (63 male, 74 female) and 39 Shugendō/yamabushi houses (修驗). No maru-marker appears, so the entire page belongs to Saijō, as confirmed by the running header 藩制一覽表第六（西條）and page number 七十八 (78).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Saijō)
pages.page_topic: Saijō demographics (town/temple/shugen) and land-tax revenue (正税・雜税)
pages.page_summary_en: This left page continues the 西條藩 (Iyo Saijō, fascicle 6) entry with commoner demographic and fiscal data compiled from the 1870 (庚午) survey; there is no maru-marker on the page, so every column belongs to Saijō. It records a town/rural (在町) population of 54,400 in 11,281 households (27,215 male / 27,185 female), 89 temple buildings (寺院堂庵) with 192 clergy (172 male / 20 female), and 181 persons (88 male / 93 female) attached to the 39 shugen lodges (修驗) whose category-head stands on the preceding page. The regular tax (正税) is entered as 18,187.584 koku of rice plus a further 11.30469 koku and a cash sum of 90 ryō 1 bu 3 shu, and the miscellaneous tax (雜税) as 814.148 and 140.86088 koku of rice; a warichu note flags these tax lines as originally red-ink marginalia drawn from a single register.

pages.page_header_en: Han Regulations Overview, Fascicle 6 (Saeki) — running header
pages.page_topic: Land-tax / fiscal record of Saeki domain
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fascicle-6 (land-tax and fiscal) record for Saeki domain (佐伯藩), a 20,000-koku Mōri domain in Bungo province. Its base kokudaka (高) of 20,000 koku plus 1,952.21043 koku of newly-reclaimed field (新田改出高) gives a total assessed kokudaka (合) of 21,952.21043 koku; the tax rice actually collected (此取米) is 9,858.895 koku, itemized (内譯) into 7,626.37 koku paid in kind (現石納高) and 2,232.525 koku paid by substitution (代納高). The substitute payment is valued at 12,884.46816 kan of eizeni (此永); the total money assessment (此金) is 1,126 ryō 3 bu 2 shu (at 8 ryō/koku), total rice (合米) is 19,153.89357 koku, miscellaneous taxes (雑税高) total 18,926.08383 kan, and the domain reports 191 shizoku households (士族戸數). The entire leaf is Saeki; although the project index also tags 三田藩 here, no Sanda marker or data is physically present (Sanda's record begins on the next leaf, p53).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Saeki)
pages.page_topic: Status-group population & household census (Saeki)
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page completes the Saeki (佐伯藩) entry in fascicle 6 of the Hansei Ichiran, a status-group population and household census. The domain's total population is 65,366 (male 33,724, female 31,642) living in 12,173 households across 26 villages, with 22 Shinto shrines and 32 Buddhist temples. Itemised status groups include 937 samurai (shizoku, M436/F501), 1,247 sotsu (foot-soldier class, M613/F634) in 252 households, 28 shrine-priest (shake) households (165 persons), 10 Shugendo households (46 persons), a temple population of 326 (289 monks + 37 women, plus 1 nun), and small outcaste groups (eta: 2 households/8 persons; hinin: 22 households/127 persons). A vermilion editorial note records the domain's military as two infantry platoons, one drawn from the samurai class and one from the sotsu class.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview, Fascicle 6 (Sanda)
pages.page_topic: Kokudaka and land-tax accounts of Sanda domain (Settsu / Tanba)
pages.page_summary_en: This page records the fiscal accounts of Sanda domain (三田藩), whose lands lay in Settsu and Tanba provinces. Its assessed kokudaka was 36,000 koku, with an additional 1,717.337 koku of newly reclaimed paddy (新田高), giving a combined total (合高) of 37,717.337 koku. Regular land tax (正稅) in rice came to 12,220.655 koku from the Settsu holdings and 2,289.828 koku from Tanba, and miscellaneous tax (雜稅) added 558.997 koku of rice plus 127 kan 632 mon in cash in Settsu and 197.833 koku of rice in Tanba, together with soybean (大豆) levies of 20 and 1.6 koku. A red-ink editorial note attributes the kokudaka figure to the Meiji 2 survey.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, fascicle 6 (Mita)
pages.page_topic: Mita domain civil/fiscal survey — households, population, status, temples/shrines, land tax
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page carries the fascicle-6 (civil) survey for Mita domain (三田藩), in Settsu. It records 4,438 households and a total population of 20,332 (10,376 male, 9,956 female), including 667 samurai/shizoku (226 male, 441 female) and a 16-household hinin-ban watch of 80 persons (42 male, 38 female); religious institutions number 69 temples (with 95 monks and 18 nuns) and 60 shrines. Fiscal figures are a regular land tax (正税) of 14,530.483 koku of rice and miscellaneous taxes (雑税) of 758.43 koku of rice plus 127.632 kanmon in cash, with marginal red-ink notes recording 240 foot-soldiers and that the sotsu class is counted within the rural population. The ○鯖江藩 marker at the far left opens the next domain, Sabae, whose data begins on the following page — everything to its right on this page belongs to Mita.

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 6 (Sabae)
pages.page_topic: Sabae domain: kokudaka, land/product tax, products, shizoku & sotsu households and population
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf is the fascicle-6 entry for Sabae domain (鯖江藩, Echizen), assessed at 40,000 koku plus 66.951 koku of newly reclaimed paddy (改出シ新田) for a total assessed yield of 40,066.951 koku. Its regular tax in actual rice (正税現米) was 12,404.4216 koku, and a product tax (産物税) of 5 kan 761.8 mon in ei-cash was levied on four taxed products — hōsho paper, lime, whetstone, and ajiro woven hats — while eight further products (raw silk, paper-mulberry bark, birch, ramie cloth, lacquer bowls, moxa, straw matting, and rapeseed) were listed as untaxed. The domain counted 311 shizoku households with a population of 1,377 (621 male, 756 female) and 303 sotsu households with a population of 1,289 (667 male, 622 female). No maru-marker is present; the domain is identified only by the running header, and the page carries printed page number 84.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第六（狹山、吉井）
pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Sayama, Yoshii)
pages.page_topic: Civil register (Sabae overflow) plus kokudaka and revenue (Sayama)
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page of Fascicle 6 carries three domains. Its bulk is the tail of the 鯖江 (Sabae) civil register, printed to the right of the ○狹山藩 marker and therefore belonging to the preceding domain: 5,718 households and 27,151 people (13,793 male / 13,358 female), 8 shrines, 8 shrine-attendant houses (39 people), 78 temples (294 temple residents = 152 monks, 11 nuns, 8 lay men, 123 lay women), 4 yamabushi houses (17 people) and 3 outcaste (穢多) houses (13 people). To the marker's left the 狹山 (Sayama) entry opens with an assessed kokudaka of 11,615.7026 koku and collected revenue of 5,467.72984 koku of rice, its regular and miscellaneous taxes recorded as entirely undetailed (正雜稅其他一切不詳). The ○吉井藩 (Yoshii) marker then opens at the far left, its figures continuing on the next page.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Survey, Fascicle 6 (Sano)
pages.page_topic: Kokudaka, land tax and household figures for Sano (plus the tail of Yoshii)
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page of Fascicle 6 mainly records Sano Domain (佐野藩), a 16,000-koku domain whose lands lay in Shimotsuke (1 district), Kōzuke (4 districts) and Ōmi (1 district). Its combined assessed kokudaka is 17,162.56328 koku — a 16,000-koku base plus 1,162.56328 koku of additional land (外高, annotated 込高, "included in the total"). Regular land tax (正租) was 5,108.36512 koku of rice plus 501 kan 39 mon 8 rin in cash (永), and miscellaneous taxes (雜稅) 232.35608 koku plus 430 kan 870 mon in cash; the domain had 2,518 households, of which the page lists 64 shrines and 5 Shinto-priest households before the breakdown continues on the facing page. The three rightmost data columns are the tail of the preceding Yoshii Domain (吉井藩, a 10,000-koku domain): its regular and miscellaneous taxes are noted as "entirely undetailed," though its collected rice (此收納) was 2,155.89537 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Sano)
pages.page_topic: Sano domain population and clergy/status demographics
pages.page_summary_en: A continuation page of the Sano (佐野) domain return in Fascicle 6 of the Hansei ichiran, recording population and religious/status demographics. The total population (人員) is 11,893 (6,075 male, 5,818 female). The samurai orders comprise 111 shizoku households (473 persons: 213 male, 260 female) and 119 sotsu households (628 persons: 329 male, 299 female); the governor's own family numbers 2 (1 male, 1 female). Religious tallies include 56 Buddhist temples, 1 training hall, 4 hermitages, 3 practitioner households, 63 monks, 15 shrine-family men, 14 shrine women and 24 temple women.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran (Survey of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 6 — (Sanuki)
pages.page_topic: Sanuki kokudaka and averaged land/miscellaneous taxes (plus Sano's outcaste-status and village tail)
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand leaf of Fascicle 6 opens the entry for Sanuki Domain (佐貫藩, Kazusa; Abe house), whose ○-marker sits mid-page: everything to its right is the closing tail of the preceding Sano Domain (佐野藩), everything to its left is Sanuki. Sanuki is assessed at a 16,000-koku base plus 199.92195 koku of additional land (外高) — annotated by a warichu as komidaka together with previously-opened new paddy — for a combined 16,199.92195 koku, a sum the page states exactly. Under a 平均 ("average") heading it records regular land tax (正租) of 4,000.82626 koku of rice plus 1,838 kan 957 mon in ei-cash, and miscellaneous taxes (雜稅) of 8.971 koku plus 412 kan 595 mon — an effective land-tax incidence of about 24.7 percent of the combined assessment, against 29.8 percent for neighbouring Sano. Sano's four closing columns give 3 eta households (10 persons: 6 male, 4 female), 1 hinin male, and 36 villages; the leaf carries printed page number 88.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview (Hansei ichiran), Fascicle 6 (Sanuki)
pages.page_topic: Product tax and status-group household and population counts
pages.page_summary_en: The left half of printed page 89 in Hansei ichiran fascicle 6, continuing the entry for Sanuki domain (Kazusa province, base kokudaka 16,000 koku), whose ○佐貫藩 marker stands on the facing right-hand leaf. It opens with a product tax of 200 ryō in gold, then walks the domain's population by status group: 16 kazoku (7 male, 9 female); 91 shizoku households holding 401 persons (204 male, 197 female); 29 sotsu households holding 110 persons; 53 shrines served by 19 Shinto-priest households (80 persons); 47 temples with 78 clergy; and 3,314 commoner households totalling 16,908 persons (8,447 male, 8,461 female) — some 96 percent of the enumerated population. Every male-plus-female split on the page reconciles exactly against its printed total. Two vermilion editorial notes (原朱) qualify the figures: one dates the household and population counts to the Kōgo (1870) survey, the other preserves a Mi-year (1869) count of 180 shrines and 48 temples that departs sharply from the 53 shrines and 47 temples printed in the table itself.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 6 (Sakurai)
pages.page_topic: Sakurai kokudaka and tax opening; Sanuki's outcaste and village tail
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 90 of fascicle 6 of the 1870 Hansei ichiran-hyō. The five columns right of the maru-marker close out Sanuki domain's (佐貫藩) record: 14 eta households totalling 97 persons (52 male, 45 female), 9 hinin households totalling 26 persons (14 male, 12 female), and 48 villages. The ○櫻井藩 marker then opens Sakurai domain, whose entry gives a kokudaka (高) of 10,179.11318 koku, regular land tax (正租) of 2,882.93654 koku in delivered rice plus 437.98321 kan in cash (永), miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 290.67734 koku plus 89.23593 kan, and status counts of 5 kazoku (2 male, 3 female) and 85 shizoku households — a land-tax take of about 28 percent of assessed yield. A brace above the tax columns is labelled 附箋 (fusen, "attached slip"), the reprint's editors recording that those figures stood on a paper slip attached to the original manuscript rather than in its main text.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Administration Survey (Hansei ichiran-hyō), Fascicle 6 — Sakurai
pages.page_topic: Sakurai population by status group, shrines and temples
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 91, the continuation of the 櫻井藩 (Sakurai) entry in fascicle 6; the block was opened by the ○櫻井藩 marker on the facing recto (p. 90), and since no marker appears on this leaf every column belongs to Sakurai. Fourteen columns give the domain's population broken out by status group, each count followed by its own 人員 total and a 内 male/female split: the 85 shizoku households returned on the facing page hold 321 people (149 male, 172 female); 25 sotsu households hold 54 (30/24); 2,623 commoner households hold 12,866 (6,422/6,444); 5 shrine-priest (社家) households hold 24 (15/9); and 5 households of peasants on shrine land hold 26 (13/13). The page closes with 59 shrines, 42 temples whose resident population is 57 (54 male, 3 female), and a single watchman's hut. All six male+female splits reconcile exactly with their printed totals.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第六（岸和田）
pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, fascicle 6 (Kishiwada)
pages.page_topic: Appendix kokudaka and five-year-average taxes (Sakurai); Kishiwada entry opens
pages.page_summary_en: The right two-thirds of this page completes Sakurai domain's fascicle-6 entry, which began on printed page 九十 and continues from 九十一. It gives 27 villages; a registered headcount of 39 persons (20 male, 19 female) belonging to the watchman's-hut category carried over from the preceding page; and, under a brace headed 符箋 ("attached slip") with the qualifier 別冊 ("separate appendix"), an alternative kokudaka of 10,162.19517 koku plus five-year-average tax figures: paddy main tax 3,158.58065 koku of hulled rice, upland main tax 276.88845 koku with 533.654104 kan in cash, and miscellaneous tax 47.15785 koku with 82.020827 kan in cash. Left of the ○岸和田藩 marker, Kishiwada domain's entry opens with a base kokudaka of 53,000 koku plus 6,028.3232 koku of newly reclaimed field, totalling 59,028.3232 koku — an arithmetic identity that confirms the reading. The running head names Kishiwada even though most of the page's data is Sakurai's, so it must be treated as section provenance rather than a column label.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第六（岸和田）
pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview Table, Fascicle 6 (Kishiwada)
pages.page_topic: Kishiwada domain: averaged rice tax, status-group households and population, villages, shrines and temples
pages.page_summary_en: The verso of PDF leaf 58, printed book page 93, carrying the second half of Kishiwada domain's entry in fascicle 6 of the 1869–70 Dajōkan 藩制一覽表 survey. It records an averaged annual regular rice tax of 29,099.633 koku (正稅) plus 3,686.4111 koku of miscellaneous tax (雜稅) — jointly 32,786.0441 koku, or roughly 49% of the 59,028.3232-koku 合高 printed on the facing recto (p. 92) — alongside 93 villages, 274 shrines and 190 temples. The status-group counts are 華族 8 persons, 士族 552 households / 2,212 persons, 卒 851 households / 2,393 persons, and 平民 12,459 households / 58,748 persons, giving 13,862 households and 63,361 people in all; every 男＋女 split on the page sums exactly to its printed parent total. A five-column note in small type at the head of the page, flagged （原朱） as written in vermilion in the manuscript original, adds 17 Shinto shrine-priest (社家) households, 50 persons, of whom 35 male.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 6 (Kikuma)
pages.page_topic: Kikuma's opening kokudaka and tax block; Kishiwada's outcaste counts carried over
pages.page_summary_en: The ○菊間藩 marker opens the Kikuma entry mid-page, with a warichu naming the four provinces its holdings lay in (Kazusa, Echigo, Mikawa, Izu). Kikuma's block runs leftward from there: kokudaka 54,653.55489 koku; regular tax (正租) of 15,623.46883 koku of rice plus 653.54918 kan in ei-sen and 2.776 kan in copper cash; miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 2,162.40931 koku, 2,156.704105 kan, 19.018 momme of silver and 3.007 kan of cash; and a further 653.26 koku of shrine-and-temple land. The two columns to the right of the marker close the PREVIOUS domain, 岸和田藩 (Kishiwada), whose entry ends on the facing page lower_p058_left (printed 93): eta 2,108 persons (1,076 male / 1,032 female) and hinin 241 (89 / 152). The top-margin head-note is Kishiwada's too — 「女子十五人」 completes the red-ink 社家 note begun on p058_left (35 males + 15 females = the 50 persons stated there), and 「外ニ非人二十一人 男九人 女十二人」 adds 21 more hinin.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran (Domain Administration Survey), Fascicle 6 — (Kikuma). Running header / provenance, printed in the outer (low-x) margin.
pages.page_topic: Shrine-temple land taxes and exempt-land breakdown
pages.page_summary_en: Page 95 closes Kikuma domain's fiscal register in fascicle 6, running on from page 94 with no new ○marker, so every column is Kikuma's. It carries two sub-accounts that sit below the domain-level totals recorded on the facing page. First, the shrine-and-temple land account opened there by 外 社寺領高 653.26 koku: a komidaka supplement of 20.87533 koku, of which 35 koku is precinct-exempt and yields no revenue, taxed at 367.59901 koku of rice, 152.3557 kan of ei, 18.985 kan of copper cash and 1.12198 koku of soybeans in regular tax (正租), plus 13.736 koku of rice, 1.3631 kan of ei and 983.228 kan of copper cash in miscellaneous tax (雜稅). Second, the exempt-land account: 除地高 110.323 koku, itemised as 100 + 6.913 + 3.41 koku — a breakdown that sums exactly to the printed total. The 100-koku parcel is the exempt land of Hikozaemon, a peasant of Sanbongi village in Echigo, whose revenue the domain says it will report only after investigation; 6.913 koku is precinct-exempt with no revenue; and the 3.41 koku that does yield revenue bears 0.57288 koku of rice in regular tax.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Kikuma)
pages.page_topic: Status households, populations, and religious establishments
pages.page_summary_en: The tail of Kikuma Domain's fascicle-6 civil register, given over entirely to status households, their populations, and religious establishments. Read right to left, it records shizoku 131 households / 551 persons, quasi-shizoku 191 / 842, sotsu 329 / 1,403, commoners 14,314 / 70,190, and shrine-priest (shake) houses 45 / 239 — every one of the five given with an 内 male/female split that sums exactly to its stated total. The privileged tiers together account for 651 of 15,010 households (4.3%) and 2,796 of 73,225 persons (3.8%), so the commoner block carries roughly 96% of the domain's recorded population. The religious counts close the entry: 202 shrines, 214 Buddhist temples, and 98 Buddhist halls (堂) — note the 45 shake households against 202 shrines, implying most shrines had no resident priestly house.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 6 (Kitsuki)
pages.page_topic: Residual rice, miscellaneous taxes, households by status
pages.page_summary_en: Book page 98 of fascicle 6 continues the civil register of Kitsuki (杵築藩), a 32,000-koku fudai domain in Bungo province; no ○ marker is printed here — the ○杵築藩 boundary stands on the preceding, unscanned book page 97 — so every column on the leaf belongs to Kitsuki. The page records residual rice of 19,885.6211 koku and miscellaneous taxes of 258.7243 koku of rice plus 1,690 ryō 3 bu 2 shu in cash (with 58 mon 9 bu 7 rin reckoned in ei), then a total of 12,251 households broken out ten ways: 392 hanshi, 300 hansotsu, 5 "baisotsu" (which the compiler flags マヽ/sic, apparently for 陪卒), 115 shrine households, 118 celibate-clergy temples, 23 Ikkō-shū temples, 25 Shugendō ascetics, 15 blind priests, 10,771 farmers and 487 merchants — a set that sums exactly to the printed total. The population of 51,535 then opens its own status breakdown, of which only the hanshi line (990 male, 990 female) fits before the register runs on to the next page; that 1,980 matches the shizoku count independently attested for Kitsuki in the Meiji Shiyō.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō (Survey of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 6 — (Kiyosue)
pages.page_topic: Kiyosue kokudaka, land tax, and status-group households
pages.page_summary_en: This right half of PDF spread 62 (printed book page 100) opens the fascicle-6 civil entry for Kiyosue (清末藩), a 10,000-koku Mōri branch house in Nagato province. Kiyosue reports a base kokudaka of 10,000 koku plus 13,091 koku odd of yield newly brought out from new fields (新田打出高), for a total 合高 of 23,091 koku odd; regular land tax (正租) runs 6,888 koku of rice plus 767 kan of cash, with a further 873 kan in miscellaneous taxes (雜稅). Its status counts are 9 kazoku (3 male, 6 female), 195 shizoku households totalling 848 persons (429 male, 419 female), and 165 sotsu households totalling 677 persons (370 male, 307 female) — every male/female pair sums exactly to its printed total. The single column standing to the right of the ○清末藩 marker (華族 6 persons: 3 male, 3 female) is the page-spilled closing field of the preceding domain, Kitsuki (杵築藩), whose block runs back through book pages 97–99.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 6 (Kiyosaki section) — running header (provenance)
pages.page_topic: Five-year average main-tax receipts, itemised
pages.page_summary_en: Book page 102 continues Kiyosaki (Kiyozaki — i.e. Itoigawa in Echigo; 10,000 koku, Matsudaira) domain's fascicle-6 civil register, itemising the five-year average 正租納高 (main land-tax receipts) whose heading stands at the foot of the preceding page-side. Seven 一-marked items run right to left: rice 3,722.2298 koku, being the two-thirds of the collected torimai paid in kind plus the sashimai surcharge; gold 7,238 ryō with 3.678 monme silver, the commuted one-third, equal to 1,682.889 koku of rice; gold 291 ryō with 10.892 monme, the soybean levy commuted to cash, equal to 33.282 koku of soybeans; ei 84 kan 571 mon 1 bu of komononari from Uonuma district (restated as 84 ryō 2 bu + 4.27 monme); silver 11.96785 kanme of komononari from Kubiki district (restated as 199 ryō 1 bu + 12.85 monme); gold 461 ryō 1 bu from the various unjō licence levies; and 54 kan 527 mon of copper cash, likewise unjō. Both cash restatements close exactly at the standard 60-monme-per-ryō rate. The leaf ends with the 1928 editors' note that the next ten lines are red-ink marginalia, and with the red-ink heading 又　庚午調 ("again — the 1870 survey"), which opens a second, Kanoe-uma restatement carried onto the facing page.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō (Table of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 6 (Kiyosaki)
pages.page_topic: Tax revenue and status/household population
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues 清崎藩 (Kiyosaki, a small post-Boshin Echigo domain) from its ○-marker two printed pages earlier; no marker appears here, so the whole page is Kiyosaki's. Reading right to left it gives the domain's two tax lines — regular land tax of 5,397.0203 koku in hulled rice (正租現米) and miscellaneous tax of 975.0131 kan in eiraku cash (雜稅永) — then walks down the status register: 5 kazoku (2 male, 3 female), 72 shizoku households holding 359 people (186 male, 173 female), and 46 sotsu households holding 138 people. Below these come 4,046 households, plus 10 shrine-priest houses, 42 temples and 13 Gyōnin-ha ascetic houses marked 外 ("in addition"), and a closing population of 21,392 (10,515 male, 10,670 female) — about 5.2 persons across the 4,111 listed houses. Two of the four male/female splits fail to reconcile with their own printed totals (the sotsu 76+65=141 against a printed 138, and the closing 10,515+10,670=21,185 against a printed 21,392), and the editors' vermilion warichu notes at the top flag variant manuscript readings of 11 for the 10 shrine-priest houses and 55 for the 42 temples — signs of a domain return transmitted with unresolved internal disagreement.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第六（喜連川）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 6 — Kitsuregawa (喜連川藩): assessed yield and average land-tax receipts
pages.page_topic: Kitsuregawa assessed yield with its paddy/upland split, and the average annual land tax in rice, cash and upland grains
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the Kitsuregawa (喜連川藩) entry in Fascicle 6: the ○喜連川藩 marker stands at the far right, so the whole page is Kitsuregawa. The domain's assessed yield (高) is 10,209.5195 koku, broken down by the 内 ("of which") marker into 5,694.4276 koku of paddy (田方) and 4,515.0919 koku of upland (畑方) — the two components sum to the printed total exactly. Under the 平均 ("average") heading the survey itemizes the average annual land-tax take: 1,788.40984 koku of rice (31.4% of the paddy assessment), 102 kan 926.8623 mon in eiraku cash (永) and 1,051 kan 282 mon in copper cash (錢), plus five upland crops rendered in kind — soybeans 102.8964 koku, barnyard millet 82.49035 koku, perilla 1.248 koku, and sesame and adzuki beans at 0.192 koku each. The running header names Kitsuregawa, matching the data, and the bottom margin carries printed book page 107.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第六（喜連川）
pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 6 (Kitsuregawa)
pages.page_topic: Villages, households, population and status-group counts
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 108 of the Hansei Ichiran, fascicle 6, continuing the return for Kitsuregawa domain (喜連川藩, Shimotsuke) that opened on the preceding leaf (page 107) with its assessed kokudaka of 10,209.5195 koku. The page records 17 villages, 683 households and a population of 3,549 — split 1,752 male and 1,797 female, two figures that sum exactly to the stated total — together with 171 shizoku and 433 shizoku family members. The remaining columns enumerate religious and status groups: 9 Shinto shrine households (38 persons), 4 Shugendō households (16 persons), 11 temples (92 persons), 25 ban-hinin and 28 eta. A head-note in the top margin, （原朱）卒族不詳, states that the sotsu (lower-samurai) figure was left unrecorded in the original manuscript — the single gap in the domain's status return, and the reason no sotsu column is printed between 士族 and 同家族.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō (Table of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 7 (Yūki)
pages.page_topic: Yūki opening: territory, kokudaka, land tax + red-ink variant addendum
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand leaf (printed page 百九 = 109) opens fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran-hyō and with it the entry for Yūki domain (結城藩, Shimōsa) — the facing leaf, page 108, is still fascicle 6 (Kitsuregawa). A two-part warichu under the ○結城藩 marker lists Yūki's holdings across four provinces and six districts: Yūki honchō plus 55 villages — 12 in Yūki district (Shimōsa), 10 in Haga and 3 in Tsuga (Shimotsuke), 12 in Makabe and 1 in Ibaraki (Hitachi), 15 in Musha and 2 in Yamabe (Kazusa). The body gives an assessed yield (高) of 26,369.32159 koku and a regular land tax (正租) of 11,370 four-to bales of rice (= 4,548 koku) plus 1,686.112 kan of ei-cash, dated by a vermilion top-margin note to the fourth month of 1870. Four further columns, flagged 以下十行欄外朱書 as a ten-line red-ink marginal addendum quoting "one [variant] copy," report a 支配地總高 of 17,000 koku and restate the same rice and cash figures — exactly — as five-year averages.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview Table, Fascicle 7 (Yūki)
pages.page_topic: Product-tax ledger, shrines and temples, households and population
pages.page_summary_en: The middle leaf (printed page 110) of Yūki domain's fascicle-7 return, carrying no maru-marker: the ○結城藩 marker stands on page 109 and the block runs on to page 111. The right half reproduces Yūki's own Product-Tax Investigation Ledger (産物稅取調帳): 35 ryō from the Yūki-town pongee-and-cotton wholesalers Tahei and Chōemon, 3 bu from the Kubota-village brokers Gonbei, Hanjūrō and Kyūzaburō, totalled with a 〆 mark at 35 ryō 3 bu and repeated in the 雜稅 field — a trivial 35.75 ryō of commercial revenue against a 17,000-koku domain — followed by the declaration that silkworm eggs, white cotton and everything else went untaxed. The left half gives the establishment and demographic counts: 206 shrines, 36 halls, 116 temples, 3,452 households and 17,192 persons. The population resolves in an unusual way: the 内 split of 8,682 males and 8,337 females covers only the lay population, and the 173-person remainder is made up exactly by the separately enumerated religious and professional categories (13 Shinto priests and 3 shrine attendants here; 128 monks, 10 physicians, 6 mountain ascetics, 4 blind performers, 8 lay devotees and 1 shugendō practitioner on the facing leaf).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Yūki)
pages.page_topic: Status & household registers (shizoku, eta, clergy)
pages.page_summary_en: The left half of PDF page 67 (printed book-page 111) completes Yūki Domain's household-and-population register in fascicle 7, continuing the 内 ("of which") breakdown of the commoner population begun on the facing right page. Six occupational/religious categories are itemised — 僧 128, 醫師 10, 道心 8, 山伏 6, 座頭 4, 修驗 1 — after which the 外 marker opens the registers counted outside the commoner totals: 穢多 60 households / 278 persons (男 146 + 女 132 = 278 ✓) and 鉦打 4 households / 6 persons (男 4 + 女 2 = 6 ✓). The samurai register follows: 士卒戸數 231 households, itemised under 内 as 133 shizoku + 74 sotsu + 24 households under kinshin (house-arrest), summing exactly to 231; their population is 950 persons, of whom 士族妻子 (shizoku wives and children) number 289 male + 324 female = 613. The remaining status lines (卒族同斷 256, 謹愼同斷 82) print on p068R to the right of the ○湯長谷藩 marker and therefore still belong to Yūki; those three lines sum to 951 against the printed total of 950 — a one-person inconsistency in the source.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第七（湯長谷）
pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Survey (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 — (Yunagaya)
pages.page_topic: Yunagaya kokudaka and five-year-average land tax; tail of Yūki's dependant counts and standing troops
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 百十二 (112) of fascicle 7 opens the entry for 湯長谷藩 (Yunagaya, Iwaki) at an ○湯長谷藩 marker roughly mid-leaf. Yunagaya's assessed yield is 壹萬四千石 (14,000 koku), drawn from 31 villages in Iwaki Province (Iwasaki and Kikuta districts) and 3 villages in Tanba Province (Hikami and Ikaruga districts), plus a further 1,223.019 koku of reclaimed and resurvey-added land; its five-year-average land tax is 2,927.7373 koku of rice, 194.064 koku of soybeans, 570 kan 885 mon 1 bu in ei, 1,037 ryō 3 shu in gold, and 426 mon in copper cash — a vermilion note in the top margin cautions that these are the two provinces' combined figures. Everything to the right of the marker is the tail of 結城藩 (Yūki), carried over from printed page 111: the male and female dependants of the sotsu (144 and 112) and of those under kinshin confinement (40 and 41), whose totals (256 and 81) close exactly against Yūki's 人員九百五十人 with the 613 shizoku dependants on the facing page. Yūki's entry ends with its standing force — one infantry platoon of 60 men and 60 rifles — flagged by an editorial note that the two lines following were written in vermilion in the original.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第七（湯長谷）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 7 — Yunagaya section (running header; provenance, not data)
pages.page_topic: Yunagaya han — unjō/miscellaneous tax receipts and status-group household & population counts
pages.page_summary_en: This page is the interior of the 湯長谷藩 (Yunagaya, Iwaki, 14,000 koku) block in fascicle 7 of the 藩制一覧表. Its right half records non-land tax receipts: 65 ryō of komononari miscellaneous tax, then 220.5 ryō in gold plus 4.671 kan in ei and 1,329.406 kan in copper cash, with split-column notes assigning the gold to unjō on coal and sundries (石炭諸運上) and the cash to unjō on assorted goods (品々運上) — coal dues being the signature revenue of a domain sitting on the Jōban coalfield. Its left half is the status census: 85 shizoku households holding 359 persons (男160 + 女199), 25 sotsu households holding 80 persons (男41 + 女39), 38 komono menials, and 1,905 commoner households, of which 16 are shrine-priest (社家) and 4 are shugendō (修驗) households. Both male/female splits reconcile exactly to their printed totals.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Miharu (三春藩): kokudaka and land taxes
pages.page_topic: Miharu's kokudaka (草高 = 本田 + 新田) and its 正租 / 雜 land-tax block, opening at the ○三春藩 marker
pages.page_summary_en: This left half-leaf (book page 117) of the seventh fascicle opens Miharu domain's (三春藩) civil entry: the ○三春藩 marker stands mid-page, and everything to its left is Miharu's. The headline kokudaka (草高) is 61,740.8208 koku, resolving exactly into 50,002.692 koku of established fields (本田 — effectively the domain's nominal 50,000-koku rating) and 11,738.1288 koku of newly opened fields (新田). The tax block records regular land tax (正租) of 10,749.12044 koku rendered in rice (米納) plus 13,805.17978 koku assessed for cash commutation (金納) — together 39.8 percent of 草高, close to the conventional four-tenths rate — the cash itself given as 4,026.3879 ryō (此金) and restated as 503.29849 koku of rice (此米) at the eight-ryō-per-koku rate declared in the 但石八兩立 note; a miscellaneous levy (雜) of 602.31763 koku of rice closes the leaf, and these lines sum exactly to the 12,581.34-koku 合米 total printed on the next leaf. The four columns to the right of the marker are not Miharu's but the tail of Mito domain's (水戸藩) entry: shrine land (社領) of 1,003 koku with a current assessment of 1,071.712, and temple land (寺領) of 1,152.6 koku with a current assessment of 1,501.127.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Miharu) — running header
pages.page_topic: Miharu domain: cash tax, total tax-rice, households, population and status-group counts
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 118 of Hansei Ichiran fascicle 7 — the second and final civil-economy page of the Miharu (三春) block, which opens with the ○三春藩 marker on the facing page 117 and gives way to ○宮津藩 on the next page 119. The page closes the domain's tax accounts (miscellaneous cash levy 5,812.8275 ryō; its rice equivalent 726.60344 koku at the printed rate of 8 ryō per koku; grand total 合米 12,581.34 koku) and then reports demography: 7,253 commoner households and 38,619 people, 904 shizoku-and-sotsu households and 2,724 people counted separately (外ニ), plus small status groups — 79 shrine-priest households (458 people), 109 temples (130 clergy), 6 Shugendō households (32 people), 3 Hiruko households, and 12 outcaste households (63 people). The rice arithmetic closes exactly: the four printed 米 figures across pages 117–118 (10,749.12044 + 503.29849 + 602.31763 + 726.60344) sum to the 合米 total of 12,581.34, which also confirms the cash figure as 5,812.8275 ryō. The headline 人口 does not close: the printed male (17,034) and female (16,156) split sums to 33,190, some 5,429 short of the printed 38,619, and two small printed ink marks sit against the very digits (八 and 九) that the shortfall implicates.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Table (fascicle) 7 — (Miyazu)
pages.page_topic: Miharu's samurai-class demographics and military tail; opening of Miyazu's kokudaka block
pages.page_summary_en: Book page 119 of Hansei Ichiran fascicle 7 (藩制一覽表第七) records the junction of two domain entries. The five columns right of the ○宮津藩 marker close out 三春藩 (Miharu, Mutsu): five infantry platoons at 60 men each (300 troops), one and a half artillery sections, 445 shizoku households / 1,587 persons (783 male, 804 female), 459 sotsu households / 1,137 persons (630 male, 507 female), and a 20-koku 受領高 — household and population figures that sum exactly to the 904 households and 2,724 persons p071R reports as Miharu's aggregate samurai class, confirming the attribution. Left of the marker, 宮津藩 (Miyazu, Tango) opens with 草高 70,718.194 koku, resolved as 高 70,000 plus 718.194 koku of 新田改出高, against which 内 itemises deductions of 5,402.784 koku (永荒地・鍬下引, five-year average) and 127.073 koku (社寺寄附地), totalling 合 5,529.857 — the subtraction that yields the 殘 65,188.337 koku printed as Miyazu's first field on p072R. A run of three isolated glyphs (州・傳・寺) prints low in the 受領高 column; it is genuine ink but belongs to no field.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Miyazu section) — running header (provenance)
pages.page_topic: Miyazu land-tax totals and household/population counts
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 120 lies wholly inside the Miyazu (宮津藩) block of Hansei Ichiran fascicle 7: the ○宮津藩 marker stands on printed page 119 and the next marker, ○水口藩, on page 121, so no domain boundary falls on this leaf and every column is Miyazu's. The tax half carries the remainder figure 殘 65,188.337 koku forward from the preceding page and then itemises the levy — regular land tax 25,295.164 koku, miscellaneous tax rice 1,843.366 koku, and miscellaneous tax cash 1,284.736 kan, the last converted at almost exactly 50 kan per koku into the 但現米 note of 25.695 koku; the three rice figures sum precisely to the 都合米 total of 27,164.225 koku, or 41.7 per cent of the 殘 base. The demographic half records 520 shizoku households (2,298 persons) and 311 sotsu households (1,048 persons) ahead of a general count of 14,579 households and 65,696 people, whose printed male/female split of 32,976 and 32,720 reconciles to the total exactly. A closing entry places 200 households of Kūyadō-school mendicant-bowl practitioners (hachitataki) outside the ordinary household roll.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 — Minakuchi section (running header, provenance)
pages.page_topic: Miyazu status-group demography and troops; opening of the Minakuchi kokudaka/tax block
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 121 of Hansei Ichiran fascicle 7 straddles two domains, divided by the ○水口藩 maru-marker at mid-page. Right of the marker the page completes 宮津藩 (Miyazu)'s status-group demography: the 1,021 persons (M 529 / F 492) of the 200 Kūya-dō alms-practitioner households carried over from p.120, then 非人 58 households / 275 persons (M 137 / F 138), 穢多 162 households / 949 persons (M 482 / F 467), 社人 51 households / 188 persons (M 98 / F 90), 227 temples housing 442 people (377 monks, 7 nuns, 58 women), and a standing force of 239 troops. Left of the marker the 水口藩 (Minakuchi, Ōmi) block opens with 表高 25,000 koku, a 込高新田 new-field increment of 1,491.88614 koku, 正租 land tax of 11,333.161 koku of rice, and 雜稅 miscellaneous tax of 363.418 koku — a regular tax take of about 42.8% of the implied 26,491.886-koku gross. Every male/female and status split on the leaf sums exactly to its printed total, and that arithmetic net is what exposed two MASTER transcription errors (非人 male, 穢多 female).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Table Seven (Minakuchi)
pages.page_topic: Minakuchi households, population and status/clergy breakdown
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the demographic block of 水口藩 (Minakuchi, Omi province) in Table 7 of the Hansei Ichiran, opening with a currency remainder (金一分 = 0.25 ryo plus eisen 10 kan 532.333 mon, and 錢一貫文) carried over from the preceding leaf. Minakuchi returns 4,704 households and a population printed as 20,356, against male 10,154 and female 10,196 which sum to 20,350 — a six-person discrepancy the compilers marked with a 〔ママ〕 ("sic") glyph. The 内 breakdown gives 356 shizoku households holding 1,391 people (718 male, 673 female) and 88 sotsu households holding 150 people (96 male, 54 female), both of which reconcile exactly. Religious and outcast counts close the page: 5 shake, 5 onmyoji and 9 yamabushi households against a combined 94 persons (a second 〔ママ〕 — the 39/59 split sums to 98), 98 temples with 76 monks of whom 51 are Shinshu plus 44 women, and 63 hinin (32 male, 31 female).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覧表), Fascicle 7 — Mibu (壬生藩): opening of the Mibu block (assessed yield, households, population); the columns right of the marker close out Minakuchi.
pages.page_topic: Mibu kokudaka, households and population; Minakuchi's closing outcaste, shrine and military columns
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the Mibu (壬生藩) entry in Fascicle 7 of the 1870 domain survey: the ○壬生藩 marker sits at mid-page and everything to its left is Mibu's. Mibu reports an assessed yield (草高) of 49,061.9401 koku — its formal 30,000-koku kokudaka plus 19,061.9401 koku of yield disclosed by cadastral survey and new-field revision (檢地出高・新田改出込高), which sum exactly to the total — together with 3,288 households spread across the two provinces of Shimotsuke and Shimōsa (野總二州) and a population of 18,213 (9,300 men, 8,913 women). The columns to the right of the marker close out the preceding Minakuchi (水口藩) entry, running on from p.122: 410 outcaste (穢多) persons (208 men, 202 women), 86 shrines (神社), two 50-man infantry platoons plus 28 men from the commander down, a 24-man artillery unit (砲隊) and 20 drum-and-fife players (鼓笛手). Minakuchi's block then ends with a small appended holding of 29.3 koku attributed to the temple Daitoku-ji (大德寺), whose five-year average regular tax (正税五ヶ年平均) is 6.8416 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō (Table of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 7 (Mibu)
pages.page_topic: Mibu domain demographic return: households, population, status and outcaste sub-counts
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 124 of fascicle 7 continues the household-and-population return for Mibu Domain (壬生藩, Shimotsuke); the ○壬生藩 marker stands on the facing page 123 and the next marker (○三日月藩) does not appear until page 125, so every column here belongs to Mibu. Reading right to left, the page first closes out the Shimotsuke–Shimōsa (野總二州) holding carried over from page 123 with its outcaste supplements — eta, 169 persons in 34 households (95 male, 75 female), and hinin, 25 persons — and then records a village count of 91, which the 1928 editors gloss as 欄外朱書 (added in red in the margin of the manuscript). A second territorial block follows for the Yamato–Harima (和播二州) exclaves: 1,119 households and 5,353 persons (3,718 male, 2,635 female), plus onbō 28 persons in 5 households and hinin 13 households / 16 persons. The page closes with the domain-wide status groups — shizoku 207 households and 827 persons, sotsu 230 households and 866 persons, and shrine personnel 23 households and 121 persons — and carries two editorial （ママ） "sic" marks where the printed totals fail to match their own male/female splits (169 against 170, and 5,353 against 6,353).

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第七（三日月）
pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覽表), Fascicle 7 — the printed header names 三日月 (Mikazuki), the domain that only OPENS on this leaf; most of the page is the tail of Mibu (壬生藩). Provenance, not an attribution of the data.
pages.page_topic: Close of Mibu's religious-personnel register plus its red-ink army note, then the opening kokudaka and land-tax columns of ○三日月藩 (Mikazuki)
pages.page_summary_en: This left leaf of PDF spread 74 (printed page 百二十五 = 125, fascicle 7) spans a domain boundary at its single ○三日月藩 marker. Everything to the RIGHT of the marker closes Mibu's (壬生藩) civil register: 117 temples (寺) and 78 shrines (社); 84 Buddhist clergy (僧), broken out as 75 male and 9 female; 4 nuns (尼); 6 shugen/yamabushi households (修驗) totalling 25 people (11 male, 14 female); and 6 gong-beater households (鉦打) totalling 10 people (7 male, 3 female). A bracketed editorial note, （以下二行欄外朱書）, flags that the next two lines stood in red ink in the manuscript margin: 12 infantry companies at 30 men each (兵隊十二小隊〔一隊三十人〕), totalling 合三百六十人 = 360 troops — the arithmetic closes exactly. To the LEFT of the marker, Mikazuki (三日月藩), a small Mori house in Harima, opens its entry with an official kokudaka of 15,000 koku (高 壹萬五千石), a further 560.487 koku of newly opened land (外ニ … 新開地), and a main land tax (正租) of 7,498.10954 koku of rice plus 1,397.8906 koku of soybeans.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覽表), Fascicle 7 — the printed header names 峯山 (Mineyama), the domain that only OPENS on this leaf at its ○ marker; ten of the page's thirteen substantive columns are the tail of Mikazuki (三日月藩). Provenance, not an attribution of the data.
pages.page_topic: Mikazuki's household, population and status register, then the opening kokudaka of ○峯山藩 (Mineyama)
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 126 of fascicle 7 closes the civil register of Mikazuki Domain (三日月藩, a 15,000-koku Mori house in Harima) and then opens the entry for Mineyama (峯山藩) at the page's single ○ marker. Everything right of that marker is Mikazuki's: a miscellaneous cash tax (雜稅) of 484 kan 641 mon; shizoku, 156 households and 679 persons (344 male, 335 female); sotsu, 155 households and 664 persons (340 male, 324 female); a domain total of 4,823 households and 17,945 persons (9,459 male, 8,486 female); 12 shrine-personnel households holding 55 people (27 male, 28 female); 54 temples, hermitages and shugendō establishments housing 112 religious (64 monks, 21 nuns, 27 women); and an army of three platoons. Left of the marker Mineyama opens with an assessed kokudaka of 11,144.441 koku plus a further 155 koku of newly opened paddy and dry field. Every male/female pair on the page sums exactly to its printed total and the temple breakdown closes on 112, while Mineyama's two figures reconcile precisely with the 合高 of 11,537.331 koku on the facing leaf (page 127) once its 237.89 koku of 込高 is added — a cross-page check that also shows the facing leaf's fiscal columns belong to Mineyama, not to Mikazuki.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Mineyama)
pages.page_topic: Mineyama domain assessed yield and land-tax revenue (fascicle 7)
pages.page_summary_en: This page is the tax half of 峯山藩's (Mineyama, Tango province) entry in fascicle 7 of the 藩制一覧表, printed book page 127. It closes the domain's assessment — a 込高 supplement of 237.89 koku lifting the 合高 to 11,537.331 koku — then sets out revenue in three blocks: 正租 (regular land tax) at 5,955.63293 koku of rice, 47.5 ryō gold, 730.1 mon ei and 481 mon copper cash; 雜稅 (miscellaneous taxes) at 67.124 koku, 1 ryō, 6,323.02 mon ei and 1,426 mon cash; and the 正雜合 combined total at 6,022.75693 koku, 48.5 ryō and 7,053.12 mon ei, each carrying a conversion note (此米, 此金). Every component sums exactly to its printed total, and the 合高 reconciles with the 高 (11,144.441 koku) and 新田畑 (155 koku) printed on the facing right-hand page. The block overruns the foot of this page and finishes on lower_p076_right, which carries the combined group's copper-cash total and the closing 合米.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Survey, Fascicle 7 (Mineyama)
pages.page_topic: Tax conversion tail and household/population register
pages.page_summary_en: Page 128 of the Hansei Ichiran, fascicle 7, carrying the closing revenue lines and the complete household/population register of Mineyama Domain (峯山藩). The revenue tail restates a copper-cash levy of 1 kan 911 mon as 3 shu 35 mon in gold and 0.02413 koku in rice, adds a further 0.88164 koku carried over from the preceding leaf, and closes with a combined rice total (合米) of 6,029.72502 koku. The register reports 1,754 households and 9,337 people (4,556 male, 4,781 female), including 65 shizoku households with 250 people and 127 sotsu households with 383 people; the shizoku figure carries an editorial （ママ）"sic" because its own male/female split sums to 251. Four status groups are listed separately: 9 shrine-attendant (社人) households with 33 people, 26 temples with 52 people, 17 hachiuchi (鉢打) households with 82 people, and 1 chasen (茶筅) household with 8 people.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第七（三日市）
pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Mikkaichi)
pages.page_topic: Kokudaka build-up, households and population
pages.page_summary_en: The left half of spread 76 (printed book page 129, fascicle 7) opens the entry for 三日市藩 (Mikkaichi), a 10,000-koku Yanagisawa domain in Echigo. The three columns standing to the right of the ○三日市藩 marker still belong to the preceding domain, 峯山藩 (Mineyama, whose block occupies the facing right half at book page 128): 穢多 60 households / 255 people, 非人番 11 households / 55 people, and a 兵隊 of two platoons. Mikkaichi's own block builds its assessment from a base 高 of 10,000 koku plus 込高 101.3967 and 改出新田 1,213.101, printed as a 合高 of 11,314.4077 koku, from which 273.7095 koku is deducted for landslide, river-washout and sand-inundation losses (山崩川欠砂入引), leaving a 殘 of 11,040.6982 koku. The domain records 1,505 households and a population of 8,224 (4,164 male, 4,060 female), of whom 107 are shizoku.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō (Table of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 7 — (Miyagawa). Provenance only; on this leaf it agrees with the main data, since Miyagawa's entry opens here at the ○宮川藩 marker.
pages.page_topic: Close of the Mikkaichi civil block, then Miyagawa's opening kokudaka, land tax, households and population
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 130 of fascicle 7 spans a domain boundary at its single ○宮川藩 marker. The five columns to the RIGHT of the marker close out the Mikkaichi (三日市藩, Echigo) block that opens on the facing page: 48 villages, 10 Buddhist temples, an eta (outcaste) return of 1 household and 13 persons, 38 sotsu-rank retainers, and an army of two platoons totalling 80 men. To the LEFT of the marker, Miyagawa (宮川藩, Ōmi Province) opens its civil register with a base assessment of 13,000 koku plus 198.3078 koku of re-surveyed newly reclaimed land, against which it returns a regular land tax of 4,139.69206 koku of rice — a nominal take of 31.8 percent of the base kokudaka — and miscellaneous taxes of just 25.7813 koku. The domain records 1,586 households and 6,735 people, or about 4.25 persons per household; the half-size male/female split below the total gives 3,307 men and 3,428 women, which sums exactly to the printed figure.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions at a Glance, Fascicle 7 (Mineoka)
pages.page_topic: Status-group population, shrines and temples; kokudaka, land tax and demography
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf closes Miyagawa domain's fascicle-7 entry and opens Mineoka's. Miyagawa's tail, occupying the two-thirds of the page right of the ○峯岡藩 marker, registers 60 temples (74 monks, 50 women, 2 nuns) and 46 shrines, then its samurai-class establishment: shizoku 145 men and 167 women, sotsu 70 men and 12 women, and 40 fusotsu (porter-attendants), which the following column totals as 右戸數 — 95 households, 434 persons — a sum that reconciles exactly (312 + 82 + 40 = 434). Two outcaste groups close the block: 41 eta (23 male, 18 female) and 6 hinin (2 male, 4 female). Left of the marker, Mineoka enters at 15,071.145 koku assessed yield against 4,393.9743 koku of land-tax rice (29.2 per cent), with 1,976 households and a printed population of 11,040 — a figure that sits 60 above its own male/female split of 5,385 and 5,595, an inconsistency in the source itself rather than a transcription error.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 — (Mikusa)
pages.page_topic: Mineoka's status/population tail and the opening of Mikusa's kokudaka and land-tax block
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 133 of Hansei Ichiran fascicle 7 carries two domains. To the right of the ○三草藩 marker the survey finishes 峯岡藩 (Mineoka, Awa; entry opened on the preceding leaf): 66 shizoku households totalling 334 people, 62 sotsu households totalling 325, one shrine-priest household of 3, 15 temples housing 127 (49 monks plus 42 men and 36 women), 6 eta households of 48, 68 shrines, and a military establishment of just 58 men. To the left of the marker 三草藩 (Mikusa, Harima) opens with a sōdaka of 10,379.05068 koku, which the page itself decomposes exactly into a base 高 of 10,000 koku plus 379.05068 koku of komidaka new fields — the arithmetic signature of a minimum-threshold 10,000-koku domain — against a regular land tax (正租) of 4,678.56896 koku of rice and a miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 158.7226 koku. One figure does not reconcile: Mineoka's sotsu male 159 and female 66 sum to 225 against a printed population of 325, a hundred-koku-style dropped-digit error in the source itself (325 − 159 = 166), recorded here verbatim rather than silently corrected.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview (Hansei ichiran), Fascicle 7 — (Miike)
pages.page_topic: Mikusa domain's population/status/temple/military tail, then the opening of Miike domain's kokudaka
pages.page_summary_en: Page 133 of fascicle 7 carries the tail of Mikusa domain's return (Harima; kusadaka 10,379.05068 koku per the facing page) and then opens Miike's. Mikusa is recorded with 1,976 households against a printed population of 8,961; its retainer body was 79 shizoku households (309 persons) and 75 sotsu households (188 persons), alongside 9 temples with 10 cloisters and 15 monks, 3 shrine-attendant households, 5 Gyōnin-ha households and 4 eta households (23 persons); its force was three platoons totalling 126 men, and the block closes with 10 koku of former vermilion-seal land held by Okuyama-dera. The ○三池藩 maru-marker then opens Miike's block with a kusadaka of 11,997.38574 koku. Two readings depart from the project's MASTER file — the female population is 女四千三百十四人 (4,314, not 4,344) and Miike's kusadaka is 千九百九十七 (11,997.38574, not 11,977.38574) — and the printed population total falls 129 short of its own male/female split.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Miike section)
pages.page_topic: Land tax + coal tax, Chikugo & Iwashiro holdings
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues Miike's fascicle-7 civil entry: it carries NO maru-marker of its own (the ○三池藩 marker sits on the preceding page, lower_p078_left), so every column on it belongs to Miike. It splits the domain's assessed land into its two scattered holdings — 5,071.80144 koku across five villages in Chikugo Province and 6,925.5843 koku across six villages in Date District, Iwashiro Province — and for each prints the regular land tax (Chikugo: 860.95657 koku rice, 605.10844 koku ōgome, 278.70642 koku soybeans; Iwashiro: 1,727.9909 koku rice plus 246.8558 kan in Eiraku cash) and the miscellaneous taxes. The page closes with the tax on the Miike coal mines: 2,526.8458 ryō in gold, converted at the printed rate of 8 ryō per koku into 315.85573 koku of hulled rice. Two independent arithmetic nets confirm the readings — the two territory kokudaka sum to exactly the 草高 of 11,997.38574 koku printed on lower_p078_left, and the coal-tax gold divided by 8 reproduces the printed 此現米 to the 才 place.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Miike)
pages.page_topic: Miike domain households, population and status breakdown
pages.page_summary_en: A continuation leaf of the 三池藩 (Miike) entry in fascicle 7, carrying the domain's demographic return with no maru-marker of its own. Miike reports 1,757 households and a population of 8,961 (4,508 male, 4,453 female); the 内 ("of which") breakdown that follows lists 123 shizoku households with 503 persons (251 male, 252 female), 63 sotsu households with 183 persons (97 male, 86 female), and 16 eta households with 78 persons (35 male, 43 female) — a selective subset rather than an exhaustive partition. The religious fields record 24 shrines, while the 寺 (temples) field prints its label with no figure at all. The page closes with two lines the editors flag as vermilion in the original (以下二行原朱書), enclosed in a single bracket spanning both columns: 68 heishi and 38 heisotsu, 106 men under arms.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 7 (Shizuoka)
pages.page_topic: Kokudaka and land-tax revenue
pages.page_summary_en: This page opens the Hansei Ichiran fascicle-7 (fiscal) entry for Shizuoka Domain — the 700,000-koku holding granted to the Tokugawa house under Tokugawa Iesato after the Restoration — and records a total assessed yield (高) of 699,182.24817 koku across Suruga (7 districts), Mikawa (7 districts) and Tōtōmi (11 districts). A further 538.81 koku is entered as 外 ("outside" the assessment), with an interlinear note explaining that this land had not yet been transferred from Toyohashi Domain and that an inquiry over its receipt was still pending. Regular land tax (正稅) is returned as 185,738.02411 koku of rice plus 2.265 koku of soybeans and three cash lines — 1,239.775387 kan in eiraku reckoning, 9,336.357 kan in bita (debased copper), and 123.04 kan in coin; miscellaneous taxes (雜稅) add 22,668.50006 koku of rice, 469.03184 koku of barley, 422.56086 koku of soybeans and 0.24 koku of adzuki beans, with the schedule continuing on the facing page. Rice alone thus amounts to roughly 29.8% of the assessed yield. An editorial note in red ink dates the return to the tenth month of the kanoe-uma year (Meiji 3 / 1870).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Shizuoka)
pages.page_topic: Shizuoka domain: remaining tax dues in kind and cash, timber levies, and the opening of the products list
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left-hand continuation of the 静岡藩 return in fascicle 7 of the 藩制一覧表; the ○静岡藩 marker itself stands on the facing right-hand page, so the whole page belongs to Shizuoka and carries no domain boundary. The columns record the tail of the domain's dues — buckwheat 0.24 koku, salt 73.373 koku, 18 hoe handles, silver 68.95 monme — followed by three separate cash reckonings: ei 3,554.353233 kan, bita (debased copper) 1,106.776 kan, and copper cash 2,685.316 kan. An 外 ("besides") sub-heading then introduces a timber group of roughly 14,600 round logs, 200 pieces of squared timber, and about 100 flat-stock finished goods, closed by the note 右十分一運上 — a one-tenth unjō duty taken on the foregoing. The page ends by opening the 産物 (products) section with the domain's signature commodity, tea, at over 123,909 kanme (roughly 465 tonnes); the products list runs on to the next page.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Shizuoka section) — running header, provenance
pages.page_topic: Shizuoka products and household/population counts
pages.page_summary_en: A continuation leaf inside the 静岡藩 (Shizuoka) block of fascicle 7 — no maru-marker prints here, and the running header 藩制一覽表第七（靜岡） confirms every column belongs to Shizuoka. Ten product columns run right to left: paper (半紙・半切紙, 51,500 kan), sugar (白・黑砂糖, 115,100 kanme), dried bonito (鰹節, 7,260 kanme), shiitake (2,187 koku), indigo (8,064 kanme), bupleurum root (柴胡, 1,300 kanme), Ryukyu tatami facing (508,000 sheets), cotton wool (54,730 kanme), cotton cloth (20,000 tan) and roof boards (9,900 pieces); two of these — the paper and the sugar — are pairs of commodities set in a two-line warichu that share a single figure. The three leftmost columns carry the population data: 藩士戸數 10,093 samurai households with 人員 48,064 persons, and a domain total 戸數 of 157,297 households, whose matching 人口 of 777,011 prints on the facing leaf. A red-ink warichu adds a 水附名籍 register of 597 households and 2,795 persons, and a headnote cautions that shizoku and sotsu, and male and female, are not broken out and that the samurai households are presumably subsumed within the 157,297 total.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第七（新發田）
pages.page_header_en: Han Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Shibata)
pages.page_topic: Shizuoka population tail; Shibata kokudaka and taxes
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the boundary between two fascicle-7 domain entries. Its five right-hand columns close 靜岡藩 (Shizuoka)'s civil register: a domain population of 777,011 (men 391,788 + women 385,223, reconciling exactly), which pairs with the 157,297 households printed as the last column of the preceding page, plus two small status categories — 轉士 (8 households / 36 persons) and 穢多非人 (1,651 households / 7,709 persons). The ○新發田藩 marker then opens Shibata's entry, giving a total kokudaka of 139,102.18735 koku held within Kanbara district of Echigo and Shinobu district of Iwashiro, of which 此譯 ("the breakdown thereof") itemises the Echigo portion at 132,399.04313 koku. Shibata's Echigo taxes follow: land tax (正租) of 64,170.0563 koku of rice, and miscellaneous tax (雜稅) of 5,035.4176 koku of rice, 26 ryō 1 bu in gold, and 308.677985 kan in eiraku cash. A red-ink note dates the return to the second month of the kanoe-uma year (Meiji 3 / 1870).

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第七（新發田）
pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Survey (Hansei ichiran), Fascicle 7 — (Shibata)
pages.page_topic: Shibata domain land tax and levies (fascicle 7), continued
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the 新發田藩 (Shibata, Echigo) entry in fascicle 7 of the Hansei ichiran; the domain's maru-marker ○新發田藩 stands on the preceding page in reading order (lower_p081_left, printed p.139), so every column here belongs to Shibata and no domain boundary falls on the leaf. The right-hand columns close out the miscellaneous levies (雜稅) on Shibata's Echigo–Kanbara parcel — silver 75.55364 kan, copper cash 5,106.61 kan, perilla seed 0.694 and 253.3462 koku, soybeans 3,073.0258 koku and barnyard millet 178.0974 koku — with marginal notes separating a fixed in-kind levy (但定納ニ付代米不相渡, "no rice-equivalent is paid") from levies commuted to rice (但代米渡正納之事). The middle columns open the domain's second, detached parcel, 6,702.24422 koku 「岩代國信夫郡ノ内」 (Shinobu district, Iwashiro), with its own regular tax of 1,366.6696 koku of rice and miscellaneous levies of 37.9781 koku of rice plus 122.49166 kan of ei. The three leftmost columns are domain-wide totals — rice 70,610.1216 koku, gold 26.25 ryō, ei 431.169645 kan — each of which reconciles exactly against the components printed here and on p.139, and the totals block runs on to p.141 with silver and copper cash.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第七（新發田）
pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Shibata)
pages.page_topic: Shibata specie holdings, tax-exempt temple land, and samurai households and population
