pages.page_summary_en: A continuation leaf from the Shibata (新發田) entry in fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran; the running header names the domain and no maru-marker appears, so the whole page belongs to Shibata. The right-hand columns record the domain's specie: 75 kan 556 monme 6 fun 4 rin of silver and 5,106 kanmon 610 mon of copper cash. The centre carries an eight-line block — flagged by an editorial note as having been written in vermilion in the original manuscript — listing tax-exempt land (除地) in Shinobu district, Iwashiro Province, granted in six parcels to five temples (東安寺, 法輪寺, 長福寺, 東源寺, 勝念寺) and to the ascetic Sankai (行人山海), under a printed total of 7.34 koku of rice that exceeds the sum of its own six parcels (7.21 koku) by 0.13. The left-hand columns give the samurai establishment: 870 shizoku households with a population of 4,783 (2,336 male, 2,447 female), followed by 1,017 sotsu households whose population count carries over to the next leaf.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第七（新發田）
pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview, Fascicle 7 (Shibata)
pages.page_topic: Households, population, shrines, temples and eta households
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the fascicle-7 return for 新發田藩 (Shibata, Echigo). No maru-marker appears anywhere on the page, so every column belongs to Shibata; the domain is identified only by the running header 藩制一覽表第七（新發田）. The page opens with a population of 5,685 (3,091 male, 2,594 female) carried over from the household entry that ended on the preceding leaf, then gives 33,282 households and a population of 178,986 (91,202 male, 87,784 female). Religious establishments are broken out by province: within Echigo (越後國ノ内), 856 shrines with 763 attached persons and 178 temples with 1,975; within Iwaki (岩城國ノ内), 2 shrine-priest households with 17 persons and 7 temples with 4 men. It closes with 12 eta (穢多) households totalling 132 persons, evenly split 66 male and 66 female.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō (Survey of Domain Institutions), Fascicle 7 — running header keyed to Shimabara
pages.page_topic: Shibata's outcast/ferryman households, kazoku and army; opening of Shimabara's kokudaka and land tax
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page closes 新發田藩 (Shibata, Echigo) fascicle-7 block and opens 島原藩 (Shimabara, Hizen). For Shibata it records 13 hinin households holding 97 people (51 male, 46 female), 17 ferryman (渡守) households holding 149 people (80 male, 69 female), and a kazoku house of 10 (4 male, 6 female), followed by a 兵員 military block: 3 infantry battalions — glossed in a warichu as 60 men to a platoon and 8 platoons to a battalion, i.e. 1,440 foot — plus 200 gunners, 24 cannon, and 2,000 small arms. The ○島原藩 marker then opens Shimabara, whose lands are given as 肥前高來郡 together with 豐後宇佐郡 and 豐後國東郡 across the strait, at a kokudaka (高) of 74,872.3111 koku, explicitly noted as base high plus new-paddy and dry-field reclamation increases. Its regular tax (正税) is stated in 現米 (rice actually delivered) at 36,945.7416 koku, roughly 49 percent of the assessed high.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 — (Shimabara)
pages.page_topic: Shimabara taxes, national products, and 華族/士族/卒 status counts
pages.page_summary_en: Book page 144, the tax-products-and-status leaf of the Shimabara (島原藩, Hizen) civil entry in Fascicle 7. There is no domain marker on this side: the ○島原藩 marker, the assessed 高 of 74,872.31111 koku and the opening of the 正稅 account (現米 36,945.74116 koku) all stand on the preceding page 143 (lower_p083_left), so the whole page is Shimabara. It closes the 正稅 account with 8,280 koku of miscellaneous grain and 2,571 ryō (plus 134.7 ei-mon) in cash, then records 雜稅 of 2,919.6896 koku in current rice (inclusive of kuchimai, fumai and komonomari) and 3,361 ryō in cash (inclusive of kuchikin, fukin, sundry unjō and komonomari). Under 國産 it lists 990 head of farm cattle and horses — 240 oxen and 750 horses — yielding 15 ryō 500 mon in licence duty, and 3,500,000 kin of camphor seed returning 3,000 ryō in profit; the status register then opens with 3 kazoku (1 male, 2 female), 369 shizoku households totalling 2,220 persons (1,070 m + 1,150 f), and 888 sotsu households totalling 4,322 persons (2,062 m + 2,260 f), with the commoner and domain-wide totals continuing on page 145 (lower_p084_left).

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey (藩制一覽表), Fascicle 7 — Shimabara (島原藩): household and population register by status and religious category
pages.page_topic: household and population counts by status/religious category, with domain totals
pages.page_summary_en: This is the left leaf of Shimabara's fascicle-7 household-and-population return, continuing the register that begins on the facing right leaf; no ○ domain marker appears, so the whole page is 島原藩. Reading right to left it records the town-and-village households (市鄉 34,839) and their population (165,615 = 83,239 male + 82,376 female), then the religious and outcaste categories — 神社 (shrines: no figure printed, marked 不詳 in a head-note above the column), 社家 138 houses / 678 persons, 修驗 5 / 22, 山伏 2 / 9, 寺院 113 temples / 772 persons (539 monks + 233 women), 尼庵 2 / 4, 穢多 225 / 1,353, 非人 8 / 53. It closes with the domain totals 合戸數 36,590 households and 合人員 175,051 persons (87,961 male + 87,090 female). The totals close exactly across the spread: 36,590 − 35,332 (this leaf's components) = 1,258, precisely the facing leaf's 1 kazoku + 369 shizoku + 888 sotsu households.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Shinjō)
pages.page_topic: Shimabara army units; Shinjō kokudaka, taxes and troops
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand half of the fascicle-7 spread straddles a domain boundary. The six army columns to the right of the ○新庄藩 marker close Shimabara's (島原藩) military return: a 1st and a 2nd battalion of six 40-man companies each (240 apiece), a 遊擊 flying battalion of three 30-man gun companies (90), four standing platoons at 60 men (240), seven reserve platoons on the same establishment (420), and three artillery companies of 20 (60) — with a small editorial note, （以下三行附筆）, warning that the last three of those columns were appended to the original return. Left of the marker, Shinjō's entry opens: an assessed 高 of 103,434.7983 koku across 59 villages in Mogami district, Uzen; regular land tax of 25,280.77101 koku of rice; miscellaneous taxes of 186 ryō 13.585 monme in specie plus 770 kan 948 mon in copper cash; 630 koku of shrine-and-temple land; and a force of seven 60-man infantry platoons (420) with a single 36-man artillery section. A vermilion note in the top margin above the 高 column records that the 藩制 return itself carried no base kokudaka and that the figure was taken instead from the tax register (租稅錄).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 — (Shinjō)
pages.page_topic: Status-group households & population
pages.page_summary_en: Book page 147 continues Shinjō domain's fascicle-7 civil register with its status-group household and population table; the block opened on the facing right-hand page (book page 146), where the ○新庄藩 marker stands, so this side carries no boundary marker and is entirely Shinjō's. Reading right to left, the page records 200 reserve troops, then households and people by status: 521 shizoku households (1,255 persons plus 1,446 women), 761 sotsu households (1,005 persons plus 436 women), 2 Shinto-priest households (8 male, 8 female), 96 temples (207 male, 74 female) with 4 of them priestless, 91 shugen households (202 male, 61 female), and 7,944 commoner households totalling 47,405 people (25,023 male, 22,382 female). It closes with the two outcaste categories, 2 eta households (8 male, 6 female) and 10 hinin households (29 male, 23 female). The commoner split validates exactly against its printed total (25,023 + 22,382 = 47,405), and across all status groups the page yields 9,427 households and 52,173 people.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Survey (Hansei Ichiran-hyō), Fascicle 7 — (Shigehara)
pages.page_topic: Kokudaka, land deductions and land-tax
pages.page_summary_en: Fascicle 7, printed page 148, carries the entire fiscal opening of Shigehara domain (重原藩), a small jin'ya-holding house with 88 villages spread across the Aomi, Kamo, Shitara and Hazu districts of Mikawa. Its gross assessment (草高) is 28,352.28558 koku "including komidaka"; five 內 deductions totalling 2,842.45158 koku — dominated by 2,521.90385 koku of permanently ruined ground (river washout, sea encroachment, landslide and ponded land) against just 24.06714 koku for the domain's own jin'ya and village-granary plots — leave a printed 殘高 of 25,509.804 koku. An editorial note, （以下二行原朱書）, flags the next two lines as written in vermilion in the original: the five-year-average tax rice (此取米) of 9,877.06762 koku, less 1,569.2116 koku remitted for crop failure on paddy and dry fields, which resolves into 正租 8,168.9281 koku and 雜稅 138.92846 koku. Both internal arithmetic nets close to within 0.03 and 0.00054 koku respectively — small slips in the source, and a strong independent check on the transcription.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Overview Table, Fascicle 7 (Shigehara)
pages.page_topic: Households, population by status, and religious establishments
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the civil and religious returns of Shigehara Domain (重原藩, Mikawa) from fascicle 7 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran; it bears no maru-marker and continues the domain's block from the facing right-hand page. The domain reports 8,100 households and a population of 34,789 (17,623 male, 17,166 female), within which the non-commoner statuses are 235 shizoku households (949 persons) and 107 sotsu households (258 persons), alongside 10 shrine-priest and 3 shugendō households. Its religious establishment comprises 582 Shinto shrines and 73 Buddhist temples, staffed by 63 shrine personnel (31 male, 32 female), 388 Buddhist clergy (275 male, 113 female), and 6 shugendō practitioners. Shrine and temple lands held tax-exempt under vermilion-seal grant total 303.09 koku together with 9,986 tsubo.

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Table Seven (Shingū)
pages.page_topic: Kokudaka and tax closing block (fascicle 7)
pages.page_summary_en: Book page 150 carries the closing block of 重原藩 (Shigehara)'s fascicle-7 entry, not 新宮藩's: the ○新宮藩 maru-marker is the page's leftmost column, so every substantive column stands to its right and belongs to the preceding domain. A compiler's note records that the governor's family, the eta and warships are not entered, with warships glossed 不所持 ("none held"). Six lines flagged as red-ink marginalia give the 1865–1869 (乙丑–己巳) five-year averages — 正租 8,351.64362 koku plus 雜稅 1,663.9262 koku, footing exactly to the printed 合〆 10,015.56982 koku — bracketed as the 辛未 (1871) survey. The main columns then restate, on the authority of the five-year-average register, 草高 28,352.28554 koku, 正租 7,737.79882 koku and 雜稅 1,148.2914 koku with cash converted to rice; that 草高 matches 重原藩's 28,352.28558 koku printed under its own marker on lower_p086_right, whereas 新宮藩's own 草高 opens the next page at 35,743.104 koku.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Administration Survey (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 (Shingū)
pages.page_topic: Shingū domain kokudaka, five-year-average tax yields, and household/population counts
pages.page_summary_en: The whole of this page is the civil/economic register of Shingū Domain (新宮藩, Kii province), continuing from the facing right-hand half of the spread where the ○新宮藩 marker opens the entry. It records a kusadaka of 35,743.104 koku plus a further 6,569.6662 koku of 改出新田 (new fields added by re-survey), and — as a five-year average — a main land tax of 15,190.6316 koku of rice, 797.44791 koku of miscellaneous tax rice, 9,678.6875 ryō in gold, and 19.592 kan of copper cash. The demographic block gives 9,592 total households and 54,377 people (27,512 male, 26,865 female), of whom the shizoku account for 502 households and 1,892 people (874 male, 1,018 female) and the sotsuzoku for 350 households and 1,265 people (637 male, 628 female). Every male+female pair sums exactly to its printed total, a check that corrects three MASTER readings and recovers the 卒族 population row MASTER omits.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō (Table of Domain Administration), Fascicle 7 — Shingū
pages.page_topic: Non-commoner household and population counts (chūgen, temples, yamabushi) with a seven-line red-ink marginal breakdown of the temple population
pages.page_summary_en: The tail of Shingū domain's fascicle-7 block (the ○新宮藩 marker stands on p. 87 recto; no marker is printed on this leaf), covering the non-commoner household and population categories: 91 chūgen households holding 235 people (161 male / 74 female), 176 temples with 178 residents (161 male / 17 female), and 24 yamabushi households with 118 people (61 male / 57 female). A bracketed editorial note, 「（以下七行欄外朱書）」, flags the next seven columns as red-ink marginalia, and the count is exact — the 1928 editors open a bracket at 「（寺人口」 and close it seven columns later, after 「人口三十一人…女十五人）」. Those seven lines itemise the temple population as 145 monks and 2 nuns, then — separated by the collation formulae 「右一二云」 and 「又一二云」 — a Monto-sect (Jōdo Shinshū) component of 5 temples with 31 residents (16 male / 15 female). The marginalia reconcile exactly with the main text (145+16=161 male, 2+15=17 female, 147+31=178), so the red block is a complete partition of the temple population rather than a competing count, and the contrast between the 145:2 and 16:15 sex ratios is precisely the difference between celibate clergy and Shinshū's married priestly families.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran (Survey of Domain Administration), Fascicle 7 (Shimodate)
pages.page_topic: Shimodate's kokudaka and tax receipts (block opening), after the close of Shingū's population return
pages.page_summary_en: Book page 153 opens the fascicle-7 entry for Shimodate (下館藩, a 20,000-koku Ishikawa house in Hitachi) at the ○下館藩 marker. Left of the marker Shimodate returns a base kokudaka of 20,000 koku plus a further 2,116.186 koku of reclaimed new paddy (外…込高新田), assessed on a five-year average fixed rate (五ヶ年平均定免) that yields 6,027.4448 koku of land tax in rice, 33.281 koku of miscellaneous rice tax, 10,646.8125 ryō in gold and 644.417416 kan in eiraku cash — a land-tax take of about 30 percent of the base kokudaka. The five columns to the right of the marker are not Shimodate's: they close the preceding domain Shingū's (新宮藩) return with 180 eta households totalling 759 persons (1 monk, 391 male, 367 female — summing exactly to the printed total), 254 shrine sites but no Shinto priests, a six-person governor's household, and no transport vessels. The running header names only 下館, so on this page the header is provenance for the block that opens here rather than a label for everything printed on the leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview Table, Fascicle 7 (Shimodate) — the printed parenthetical agrees with the data; every column on this leaf is Shimodate's. Provenance, not a value.
pages.page_topic: Shimodate's miscellaneous-tax cash, the red-ink product tax, vermilion-seal shrine/temple land, households and population
pages.page_summary_en: The middle leaf (printed page 百五十四 = 154) of Shimodate domain's (下館藩) fascicle-7 return, carrying no maru-marker: the ○下館藩 marker stands on printed page 153 (pdf 88-left) and the block runs on to page 155 (pdf 89-left), where ○芝邨藩 opens. Reading right to left it completes the domain's miscellaneous-tax (雜稅) receipts in cash — 139 ryō 1 bu 2 shu in gold, 138 kan 297.044 mon in eisen, and 62 kan 451 mon in copper — continuing the 雜稅米 of 33.281 koku that closes the previous leaf; against a 20,000-koku domain these are trivial sums. A bracketed group of four lines, flagged by the editorial note （以下四行欄外朱書） as having stood in red ink in the manuscript margin, records a product tax (產物税) of 200 ryō on freeze-dried tofu (氷豆腐) from the domain's administered district in Kawachi Province, and 137.7 koku of vermilion-seal land (朱印地) is booked under the category label 社寺領 (shrine-and-temple lands). The leaf closes with the demographic counts: 2,827 total households and 15,182 people (7,768 male, 7,414 female), of whom 255 households and 1,156 people (590 male, 566 female) were shizoku — a samurai share of 7.6% of the population and 9.0% of households.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Shibamura)
pages.page_topic: Shimodate status-group households and population; Shibamura's entry opens
pages.page_summary_en: This page closes Shimodate domain's fascicle-7 entry and opens Shibamura's. Everything printed to the right of the ○芝邨藩 marker is Shimodate's status-group tail: 64 sotsu households (148 people, 94 M / 54 F), 15 shrine households (50 people), 104 temples with 62 resident clergy, 26 eta households (195 people), 19 hinin households (68 people), 126 shrines, a governor's household of 3 (2 M / 1 F), three districts (Makabe in Hitachi, Ishikawa and Furuichi in Kawachi), 52 villages, and no transport vessels. Left of the marker Shibamura's entry begins with a warichu note giving its own three districts (Shikijō, Yamanobe, Shimoshimo) and 25 villages, then its kusadaka of 10,021.959 koku, qualified as including revised newly-reclaimed-field yield. The running head reads 藩制一覽表第七（芝邨）, naming Shibamura even though the bulk of the page's data belongs to Shimodate — a provenance label, not an ownership label.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō, fascicle 7 (Shibamura)
pages.page_topic: Shibamura Domain — taxes and demographics (1869 main survey + 1871 marginal update)
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the entire fascicle-7 entry for Shibamura Domain (芝邨藩, a small ~10,000-koku Oda house in Yamato province), identified only by the running header — there is no maru-marker, so every column belongs to Shibamura. The right block is the 1869 (己巳, 10th month) main survey, reporting five-year-average regular land-tax rice of 4,818.81731 koku and miscellaneous-tax rice of 60.88241 koku. A two-column editorial note flags that the following five lines are red-ink marginal additions and dates the main survey to 1869/10; the left block is a supplementary survey of the 2nd month of 1871 (辛未) giving regular tax 5,079.66734 koku, miscellaneous tax 132.4245 koku, 1,625 total households, and a population of 7,338 (male 3,662 / female 3,676), of which 117 shizoku households and 474 shizoku persons plus 77 sotsu households. Male + female sub-counts reconcile exactly to both population totals.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Administration Survey (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 — Shibamura
pages.page_topic: Temple / shrine / outcaste establishment counts and populations (Shibamura, fascicle 7)
pages.page_summary_en: The left leaf of Shibamura domain's (芝邨藩) fascicle-7 return, continuing a religious-and-status demographic block. There is no maru-marker anywhere on the page, and the running header names 芝邨, so the entire page belongs to Shibamura (the block opens mid-way, carried over from the preceding right leaf). It records establishment counts — 18 temples (寺院拾八戸), 10 Buddha halls (佛堂十字), a separate 寺 count of 17 (寺十七字), 39 shrines (神社三十九座), 7 shrine-family households (社家戸數七戸) and 49 outcaste households (穢多戸數四十九戸) — paired with populations: a temple population of 75 (30 monks, 6 nuns, 13 lay men, 26 lay women), a shrine-family population of 39 (13 M / 26 F) and an outcaste population of 242 (114 M / 128 F), plus three further bare 人口 figures of 138 (96 M / 42 F), 43 (15 M / 28 F) and 38 (28 M / 10 F). A mid-page editorial note, （以下五行欄外朱書）（一二云）, flags five of the columns as figures that originally stood as red-ink marginalia in the source. Printed page number 157.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 — Shiiya
pages.page_topic: Shiiya Domain: land yield, taxes, households, and population
pages.page_summary_en: This page of the Hansei Ichiran (fascicle 7) records Shiiya Domain (椎谷藩), a small Echigo domain. Its nominal assessed yield (草高) is 10,000 koku, supplemented by 746.11776 koku of new-field yield (外/新田), for a combined total (合) of 10,746.11776 koku. Regular land-tax rice (正租米) averaged 4,337.69926 koku over the five years from Kōshi (1864) to Boshin (1868), and miscellaneous-tax rice (雜稅米) was 67.67749 koku. The domain comprised 2,303 households and a population of 10,918. Editorial notes record that the governor's family (知事家族) and transport vessels (運輪舶) were not entered.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Shiiya)
pages.page_topic: Domain demographics — households and population by status group
pages.page_summary_en: This left page continues the Shiiya (椎谷藩, Echigo) entry of the Hansei Ichiran domain survey, fascicle 7, printed page 159. It records the domain's total population by sex (male 5,329; female 5,589 = 10,918) and by status group: 66 samurai (shizoku) households / 218 persons; 47 sotsu (foot-soldier) households / 167 persons; 1 shrine-family (shake) household / 4 persons; 36 temples and 18 halls housing 171 persons; and 18 outcaste (eta) households / 117 persons. The governor's family numbers 3 (1 male, 2 female), and an editorial note records that shrine [populations] were not registered. No maru-marker appears on the page, so all figures belong to Shiiya.

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Administration, Fascicle 7 (Shimotsuma)
pages.page_topic: Shimotsuma domain kokudaka, land tax, and household/status counts
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf carries the economic and household block for Shimotsuma domain (下妻藩), a 10,000-koku base holding (本高一萬石) whose gross assessed yield (草高) reaches 12,232.245 koku including komidaka and newly-opened fields. Its land tax (正租) is 1,992.626 koku of rice plus 1,035.522 kan of cash; miscellaneous tax (雜税) is 2.353 koku of rice plus 36.666 kan of cash; exempt shrine/temple land within the domain (管轄内社寺領除地) totals 394.481 koku, with a note that the red-and-black-seal parcels cannot be distinguished. The domain has 1,786 households, of which 64 are shizoku (one of them an ichimon collateral house), 19 sotsu, 27 associate-shizoku, and 25 associate-sotsu; its holdings span parts of Hitachi, Musashi, and Shimotsuke across 33 villages. The three census-tail columns at the top right (郡三郡 / 村三十二ヶ邨 / 軍艦船ナシ) overflow from the preceding domain, Shiiya (椎谷藩).

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 — (Shimotsuma)
pages.page_topic: Shimotsuma population, status classes, and religious/outcaste household counts
pages.page_summary_en: The left half of printed page 161 continues the Shimotsuma (下妻藩) return in Fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran. It records a total population of 8,805 (male 4,485 / female 4,320) and breaks out the privileged and religious classes: 士族 249, 准士族 104, 卒族 40, 准卒族 59, plus 社人 (shrine attendants) 29, 寺侶 (Buddhist clergy) 95, and 山伏 (mountain ascetics) 11 persons. Margin counts on the right give 社家 15 shrine households, 寺院 61 temples, 山伏 3 dwellings, 穢多番非人 41 outcaste households, and a combined shrine-temple tally of 79 buildings (alternatively reckoned as 64 temples). No maru-marker appears on the leaf, so every column belongs to Shimotsuma.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview, Table 7 (Shizuku)
pages.page_topic: domain statistics: outcaste/servant population, shrines, governor's family, ships, kokudaka and land tax
pages.page_summary_en: This page from fascicle 7 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran carries the end of Shimotsuma domain's (下妻藩) entry and the opening of Shizuku domain's (志筑藩), divided by the ○志筑藩 section marker. The Shimotsuma columns record 255 eta/hinin (130 male, 125 female), 12 temple-front and tenant households, a further population of 80 (57 male, 23 female), 30 unregistered bond-servants (29 male, 1 female), 58 shrines, a governor's family of 10, and a note that warships are not recorded. Shizuku's block reports an assessed yield (草高) of 10,110 koku including new-field development, a principal land tax (正租) of 1,837.849 koku of rice plus a cash levy (永) of 325.26074 kan, a rice-equivalent (此米) of 40.658 koku, and miscellaneous tax (雜税) of 90.79915 koku in perilla and beans. The printed page number is 163.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 — (Shizuku)
pages.page_topic: Population, households, and tax-in-kind conversions (Shizuku domain, Fascicle 7)
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand leaf continues the Shizuku (志筑) domain block in Fascicle 7 of the Han-sei Ichiran — a Hitachi-province domain of roughly 10,000 koku held by the Honda house. At the head it records tax-in-kind conversions: a rice figure of 45.3996 koku (reckoned at 1 koku = 4 ryō) and an ei-cash sum of 184.49608 kanmon whose rice equivalent, 23.062 koku (reckoned at 1 koku = 8 ryō; 184.49608 ÷ 8 = 23.062, arithmetic checks), follows. It then gives the domain's demography: total population 5,568 across 888 households — including 73 shizoku and 38 sotsu households, a governor's family of 9, 56 shrine-lay persons, 19 temple clergy, 10 shrine-priest households, 9 temples and 10 shrines. Note that the printed male/female split of the total population (男 2,694 + 女 2,674 = 5,368) falls 200 short of the printed total 5,568, a source-level inconsistency; the scan prints 女二千六百七十四人 (六百), whereas MASTER records 女2874.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview, Fascicle 7 (Shishido)
pages.page_topic: Shishido domain fiscal & demographic return (kokudaka, land tax, households, population)
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the fascicle-7 (civil and fiscal) return for Shishido Domain (宍戸藩), a 10,000-koku fief of twenty-seven villages in Ibaraki district, Hitachi Province. Its gross assessed yield (草高) is 10,499.666 koku; the main land tax (正租) is 1,531.6374 koku of rice plus 115.883 koku of soybeans and 602 kan 449 mon in cash (永), and a miscellaneous tax (雜稅) adds 4.427 koku of rice and 69 kan 427 mon 4 bu in cash. The domain reports 978 households (with shizoku households explicitly not tallied) and a population of 6,309 (3,201 male, 3,108 female), plus 5 shrine-attendant and 7 shugen households and 40 temples. The two notes at the upper right — 船艦不記 (no warships recorded) and 穢多非人支配地ニ無御坐候 (no eta/hinin in the controlled land) — belong to the preceding domain, Shizuku (志筑藩), overflowing to the right of Shishido's marker.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview (Hansei Ichiran), fascicle 7 (Shichinohe)
pages.page_topic: Tail of Shishido population/status counts + opening of Shichinohe land-and-tax figures
pages.page_summary_en: This fascicle-7 (財政/民政) page straddles two domains. To the right of the sole maru-marker sit the last seven columns of Shishido-han (宍戸藩) social-status counts: shizoku 190 (男98/女92, plus 28 servants), sotsu 59 (男23/女36), shrine-people (社人) 29 (男16/女13), Buddhist clergy (寺侶) 55 (男46/女9), and Shugen ascetics (修驗) 31 (男13/女18), together with two "not recorded" notations for the governor's family (知事家族不記) and the outcaste population (穢多等不記). The marker ○七戸藩 then opens Shichinohe-han: assessed yield (草高) 10,384.647 koku, land-tax rice (正租) 1,150.0209 koku, gold tax 174 ryō (plus 永40.1 mon), copper cash 3,695.838 kan, and miscellaneous tax (雜稅) 232.25 ryō. The running header and page number (165) belong to the Shichinohe entry.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 — (Shichinohe)
pages.page_topic: Shichinohe domain — population, households by status, and cash/tax revenues
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page of Fascicle 7 records the Shichinohe domain (七戸藩) of northern Mutsu. Total population is 15,527 (male 8,406, female 7,121) across 2,994 households; the status breakdown gives 240 shizoku and 50 sotsu households, 12 shrine-family and 2 outcaste households, and 18 temples, with population by status of 1,680 shizoku, 350 sotsu, 84 shrine personnel, and 54 clergy. Four fiscal lines list cash revenues of 300 ryō (kelp / dried-abalone / sea-cucumber tax), 60 kan (sardine pressed-lees tax, ~10,100 me), roughly 1,800 ryō together with ~850 horses and ~50 cattle in annual miscellaneous taxes, and 2,665.422 kan. No domain marker appears; the entire page is Shichinohe.

pages.page_header_en: Overview of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 7 (Hirado)
pages.page_topic: Hirado domain kokudaka and tax revenue (fascicle 7)
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page continues the Hirado (平戸) domain entry in Fascicle 7 of the Hansei ichiran, recording assessed landholding and tax revenue. The combined kokudaka (合高) is 120,912.301 koku; on the same page a component 高 of 49,212.301 koku and a separate 10,000-koku cadet (branch) holding are given, the latter tied to a junior branch of the Matsuura house (末家 松浦, Junior Fifth Rank). Regular land tax is stated as 50,422.2531 koku (己/1869 survey vintage) and as 51,121.6155 koku of rice (正租米), while miscellaneous cash taxes total 11,149.125 ryō, split into gold (此金 7,654.5 ryō; 諸税金 3,175.6875 ryō) and copper-cash (錢 76,540.769 kan, plus 312 mon). Editorial notes state the figures rest on the public-storehouse expense ledger (公廛入費帳) and are five-year averages for the 辛未 (1871) survey.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 — (Hirado)
pages.page_topic: Hirado demographic summary + start of Hirado-Shinden sub-domain
pages.page_summary_en: This left page (printed p.183) closes the Hirado (平戸藩) entry of Fascicle 7 with its household/population block: 31,991 total households and a population of 148,507 (male 76,610 + female 71,897). A red-ink marginal addition, flagged by the editor's bracketed note (「但シ…（以下七行欄外朱書）本文ノ士族卒ノ内ナルヘシト考ヘル」, "the following seven lines are red-ink marginalia; treat them as [belonging] within the main text's shizoku and sotsu"), breaks the samurai classes out: shizoku = 572 households / 2,838 people, sotsu = 3,031 households / 12,521 people. A maru-marker (arc over 平戸新田) then opens the small sub-domain Hirado-Shinden (平戸新田藩): shizoku 128 households / 495 people, sotsu 112 households / 177 people as printed — though the sotsu male (258) + female (219) sum to 477, so the printed hundreds digit (百) is very likely a source error for 四百.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran, fascicle 7 (Hirado)
pages.page_topic: Hirado — minor status-group household counts and populations (temples, shrines, ascetics, blind guild, diviners, sub-vassals)
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page continues Hirado domain's (平戸藩) demographic survey in 藩制一覧表 fascicle 7, tabulating its minor status groups as paired household-and-population columns read right to left. It records sub-vassals and their servants (陪卒脇間又者: 9,009 households; population 46,839 = 24,608 male + 22,231 female), shrine-attendant families (社人: 130 households; 605 persons), mountain ascetics (山伏: 132 households; 614 persons), the blind guild (座頭: 50 households; 243 persons), yin-yang diviners (陰陽師: 31 households; 114 persons), Buddhist temples (寺: 214, with a resident population of 499), and Shinto shrines (神社: 1,813, of which 25 are Engishiki-registered Shikinai shrines). Every male+female split reconciles exactly to its stated total.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Hitoyoshi)
pages.page_topic: Kokudaka and land-tax assessment (Hitoyoshi)
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the fascicle-7 (藩制一覧表第七) land-assessment block for Hitoyoshi han (人吉藩), a small Higo domain. Its base assessed yield (草高) is 22,100 koku; three supplementary increments (外) — komidaka/shinden 35,446.9083 koku, the field-tax soybean and cash-payment portion 3,363.05815 koku, and retainer/shrine-temple land reclassified as increase-yield 2,509.36841 koku — bring the total assessed yield (合高) to 63,419.33486 koku, and the three 外 plus 草高 sum exactly to that total. The ten-year-average regular land tax is 23,995.57356 koku of rice (正租米) together with 1,179.62751 koku of soybeans (大豆). A bracketed editorial note records that village count, the governor's family, and transport vessels were "not recorded" (記セス) for this domain.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Overview, Fascicle 7 (Hitoyoshi)
pages.page_topic: Hitoyoshi domain fiscal record: land tax, cash equivalents, and households
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fiscal survey (fascicle 7) for Hitoyoshi domain (Higo province, Sagara clan). It records a regular land-tax assessment (正租高) of 23,995.57 koku; of this, a soybean portion of 1,179.63 koku is valued at 4,718.5 ryō (five-year average, 4 ryō per koku) and re-expressed as 589.81 koku of rice, yielding an actual-rice figure (現石米) of 24,585.39 koku (23,995.57 + 589.81). It also reports two cash-tax figures — 1,134.19 ryō (金) and 2,904.5 ryō in miscellaneous-tax cash (雜稅金) — and a household total of 11,299 (總戸數). A marginal note states that the following nine lines are red-ink annotations entered per the survey of 1870/8/3 and that miscellaneous taxes are otherwise not itemized.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview, Fascicle 7 (Hitoyoshi)
pages.page_topic: Hitoyoshi population and household counts by legal status
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page continues the Hitoyoshi (人吉藩) return in Fascicle 7 (藩制一覧表第七) of the 1870 Hansei ichiran, tabulating population and household counts by legal status. The total registered population is 53,577 (27,265 male, 26,312 female). It divides into samurai (士族: 3,368 people in 721 households), lower-rank retainers (卒族: 14,930 in 3,417 households), Shinto shrine personnel (社人: 547 in 127 households), Shugendō mountain ascetics (修驗: 142 in 38 households), Buddhist temple clergy (寺院: 94 in 48 households), and blind persons (盲人: 65 in 18 households). Several status blocks carry a three-way split (a status specialist plus male and female members); the shrine-personnel total of 547 is marked by the 1928 editor because its stated parts (社人 211 + female 271 + male 62) sum to 544.

pages.page_header_en: Han System Overview, Fascicle 7 (Hisai)
pages.page_topic: Hitoyoshi minority-status demographics; Hisai kokudaka opening
pages.page_summary_en: This page closes the Hitoyoshi (人吉藩) entry and opens the Hisai (久居藩) entry. For Hitoyoshi it records the tail demographic fields: 2 goze (blind female performer) households totaling 21 persons, 30 eta (outcaste) households totaling 194 persons (94 male, 100 female), and 273 shrines; the village count and the governor's family are both marked "not recorded" (記セス) and warships as "none" (ナシ). The ○久居藩 marker then begins Hisai, whose nominal yield (草高) is 43,000 koku, followed by an "of which" (内) breakdown of deducted lands amounting to 121.519 koku and 30.842 koku (main-village samurai/temple residence lots and other miscellaneous deductions). The running header files the spread under Fascicle 7 (久居), and the printed book-page number is 188.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Hisai)
pages.page_topic: Hisai domain — kokudaka assessment and tax yields (continuation)
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page continues the Hisai (久居藩) entry in fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran; it carries no domain marker, since the ○久居藩 heading falls on the preceding page, and the running header (久居) confirms the ownership. It records the domain's land assessment — an assessed high (高) of 42,878.481 koku and a new-field high (新田高) of 5,415.896 koku, against a deduction (引去) of 90.677 koku at Heki (戸木) village — together with its tax yields: a regular land tax (正租) of 19,170.4306 koku and a miscellaneous rice tax (雜稅米) of 585.739 koku, each given as a five-year average, plus cash levies of 314 ryō and 932 mon. Editorial notes flag these figures as vermillion marginalia in the original manuscript and record the averaging years (the boar-through-dragon cycle, omitting the tiger year, for the land tax; the consecutive rat-through-dragon cycle for the miscellaneous tax). Note: the assessed high reads 七十八 (…878), correcting the project dataset's 七十九 (…879).

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Overview Table, Fascicle 7 (Hisai)
pages.page_topic: Hisai domain: land yield, tax, households, and population (with red-ink variant figures)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the entry for Hisai domain (久居藩) in Fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran. It records a total assessed yield (惣高) of 58,686.165 koku — of which 81.134 koku is extension land (延高) — a current/actual yield (現石) of 24,539.1216 koku, miscellaneous tax cash (雜稅金) of 319 ryō plus 5 kan 962 mon of copper cash, 8,285 total households (總戸數), and a population of 38,310 (male 19,281, female 19,298). A red-ink marginal note ("one edition states") supplies a variant population of 37,878 (male 19,018, female 18,860). Samurai (士族) households number 297 with a samurai population of 1,399 (male 708, female 691).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran Table, Fascicle 7 (Hisai) — outer-margin running header
pages.page_topic: Status demographics — households and population by class
pages.page_summary_en: This left page continues the demographic block of 久居藩 (Hisai, a 15,000-koku Tōdō sub-domain of Tsu in Ise) in Fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran. In ruled columns it records, by status, both households and population: sotsu-class 155 households / 875 people (male 422, female 453), shrine-attendant households 17 / 98, temples 247 with 434 clergy, eta 271 households / 1,374, and hinin 25 households / 101. Six lines of red-ink marginalia (欄外朱書) — flagged by an editorial note that their date is not recorded — add a shizoku count of 1,402 (male 703, female 699) and restate the sotsu class as 1,487 (male 876, female 611), the latter conflicting with the ruled table's sotsu population of 875. Every male-plus-female split reconciles to its stated total except the temple line, whose printed components (275+178) exceed the printed total of 434.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 (Hirose)
pages.page_topic: Hirose kokudaka accounting; Hisai religious/administrative demographics
pages.page_summary_en: The page is split by the ○廣瀬藩 domain-marker near center. Everything to the right of it (read first) is the tail of the previous domain, 久居藩 (Hisai): shrine attendants 134 (M81/F53), Buddhist monks 375 (M213/F162), nuns 6, shrines 132 (of which 21 are Engishiki 式内), governor's-family 5 (M2/F3), 93 villages, and a declaration of no warships/steamers. Everything to its left is 廣瀬藩 (Hirose, an Izumo branch domain of 元高 30,000 koku): assessed gross (草高) 33,128.09 koku, a 萬引 deduction of 13,376.991 koku, a five-year average crop-loss (毛損) of 4,514.032 koku (Kōshi 1864–Boshin 1868), a remaining assessment (殘高) of 19,751.099 koku (including 480.224 koku of new field, 新田), and an actual tax yield (物成) of 9,994.491 koku at a rate of roughly 免六ツ六厘. The kokudaka arithmetic checks: 草高 33,128.090 − 萬引 13,376.991 = 殘高 19,751.099.

pages.page_header_en: Han Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Hirose)
pages.page_topic: Hirose domain — population, households, land tax and levies
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page continues the fascicle-7 (civil and economic) return for Hirose domain (廣瀬藩), a sub-domain of Matsue in Izumo Province. It records a population of 26,350 (14,089 male, 12,261 female) living in 5,873 households — among them 152 shizoku and 210 sotsu households, 30 shrine-family houses, 71 temples with 17 subsidiary hermitages, and 102 outcaste (鉢屋・穢多・隱亡) houses — with a marginal variant giving the total population as 26,396. Fiscal figures include a regular land tax (正租) of 12,338.072 koku; three surtaxes (口米 199.89, corvée rice 夫米 1,194.794, and 948.897 koku of assessed rice); a miscellaneous tax (雜税) of 1,250 bales of rice; and cash levies (錢) of 15,522.985 kan.

pages.page_header_en: Han Regulations Overview, Fascicle 7 (Hiji)
pages.page_topic: Hirose population-by-status and shrine/temple land; opening of the Hiji fiscal block
pages.page_summary_en: This page carries the tail of the Hirose (廣瀬藩) fascicle-7 entry and the opening of the Hiji (日出藩) entry, divided by the ○日出藩 maru-marker. Hirose's block records population by status — 士族 748 (M357/F391) and 卒族 761 (M396/F365) — plus religious personnel 社人 162, 寺侶 247, 鉢屋穢多隱亡 382, 修驗 8, the governor's family (知事家族) 5, and 167 shrines, followed by shrine/temple land 社寺領 122.276 koku (社領 78.558 + 寺領 43.718). Left of its marker, Hiji opens with a nominal 元高 of 25,000 koku and an assessed 草高 of 27,500.2203 koku (new fields included). The running header names Hiji and the printed leaf number is 194.

pages.page_header_en: Han Administration Survey (Hansei Ichiran), Fascicle 7 (Mori)
pages.page_topic: Land-tax accounts (fascicle 7): fief assessment, deductions, and rice/tax totals
pages.page_summary_en: This page-half records the fascicle-7 (land-tax) accounts of Mori Domain (母里藩), a 10,000-koku sub-domain of Matsue in Izumo province. The nominal fief (受領高) is 10,000 koku, while the surveyed total of administered land (支配地總高) is 9,560.931 koku; deducting an assessed 2,118.992 koku (removed by the man-biki proportional-reduction method) yields the net assessed yield (殘高) of 7,441.939 koku — an internally consistent figure (9,560.931 − 2,118.992 = 7,441.939). Tax entries include principal land-tax rice (正租米) 3,943.993 koku (also given as 365.17176 bales), miscellaneous-tax rice (雜稅米) 863.341 koku, and a remainder (殘) of 4,792.36224 koku, several qualified as five-year averages inclusive of crop loss (毛損). A single maru-marker (○母里藩) at the top-right opens the domain, so all data on this page-half belong to Mori.

pages.page_header_en: Han-System Survey Table, Fascicle 7 (Mori)
pages.page_topic: 母里藩 cash receipts, population, and household counts (fascicle 7)
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fascicle-7 (藩制一覧表第七) entry for Mori Domain (母里藩), a 10,000-koku branch house of Matsue in Izumo. It records cash receipts of 102.5 ryō from sundry transit dues (諸運上, stated as equal to 100 koku) plus 50 ryō from raw-wax sale proceeds (生蠟代出目金), summing to a combined 152.5 ryō (合金), along with an additional 2,500 tawara of rice that a marginal note says was received annually from the main house as storehouse rice. Demographic totals give a population of 8,222 (4,269 male, 3,953 female) in 1,908 total households, of which 66 are shizoku households (241 persons: 120 male, 121 female), 88 sotsu households (295 persons: 152 male, 143 female), and 2 foot-soldier households. A double-column note beside the shizoku household count flags that the main text (本書) gives the figure as 211 persons, but that the itemized breakdown is followed here.

pages.page_header_en: Overview of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 7 (Mori)
pages.page_topic: Population by status group, temple/shrine counts, governor's family (Mori domain, fascicle 7 demographics)
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fascicle-7 demographic return for Mori domain (母里藩), a small 10,000-koku branch domain of Matsue in Izumo province. It records population by status group: foot-soldiers (步卒) 75 persons, all male, continued from the preceding page; shrine-service (社務) 13 households with 72 persons (32 male / 40 female); Buddhist temples (寺院) 19, with a temple population of 59 (39 male / 20 female); the hachiya-eta outcaste group (鉢屋穢多) 43 households with 248 persons (124 male / 124 female); and non-persons (非人) with no households but 2 persons (male). The governor's family (知事家族) numbered 3 (2 male / 1 female). Village count and shrine count are both entered as "not recorded" (記セス), and the domain reports no transport vessels (運輸舶ナシ). All male/female splits reconcile with their status totals.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Sendai)
pages.page_topic: Sendai population, households, and status/clerical counts
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fascicle-7 demographic return for 仙臺藩 (Sendai); the domain's kokudaka is expressly left unrecorded ("草高等不詳細"). Sendai reports 38,962 households and a total population of 238,893 (123,143 male, 115,750 female). Status and clerical sub-counts include a samurai (兵士) population of 29,408 living in 4,262 dwellings, a foot-soldier (兵卒) population of 13,091 in 3,050 dwellings, 683 shrine-family (社家) members in 124 households, 998 mountain-ascetics (修驗) attached to 236 halls, 43 yin-yang diviners (陰陽師) in 17 households, 694 Buddhist temples, and 141 eta/outcast-hut households. Every male/female split reconciles exactly to its parent total.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Zeze)
pages.page_topic: Zeze domain kokudaka and tax revenue; tail demographic fields of Sendai
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page (printed page 209) straddles two domains. To the right of the ○膳所藩 maru-marker are the closing fields of the previous domain, 仙臺藩 (Sendai): Buddhist clergy 2,331 persons (2,219 male / 112 female), the outcaste-class population 1,138 (669 male / 469 female), 990 Shinto shrines, a governor's household of 7 (6 male / 1 female), and a note that no warships are held. Left of the marker begins 膳所藩 (Zeze), located in Ōmi and Kawachi provinces (146 villages across 9 districts) with an original assessed kokudaka of 60,000 koku. Its recorded figures are a nominal (kusadaka) kokudaka of 65,811.7681 koku, regular land tax of 24,251.5668 koku of rice, miscellaneous tax of 970.0702 koku of rice plus cash of 535 ryō 3 bu in gold and 834 kan 66 mon in copper cash, with the cash figures given as a five-year average.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Zeze)
pages.page_topic: Zeze domain — population, status households, temples, and land-tax (fascicle 7)
pages.page_summary_en: This right-hand page continues the Fascicle 7 entry for Zeze domain (膳所藩) in Ōmi province; there is no maru-marker, so every column belongs to Zeze. It records a total population of 45,723 (22,756 male + 22,967 female, which sum exactly) living in 10,185 households, of which 451 are samurai (shizoku) and 527 are foot-soldier (sotsu) households, alongside 74 shrine-family households, 273 eta and 80 hinin outcaste households, and 293 temples with 6 nunneries. A separate leftmost column gives the samurai population as 1,858 persons (871 male + 987 female). The land-tax figures — a regular-plus-miscellaneous grand total of 25,299.10 koku, regular tax of 27,872.01 koku, and miscellaneous rice tax of 1,194.83 koku — are five-year averages (years of the Rooster, Dog, Boar, Ox, and Rabbit) that appeared in the margin of the original manuscript.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 7 (Sekiyado)
pages.page_topic: Zeze status-group demographic tail meeting the start of the Sekiyado kokudaka/land-tax block
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page straddles a domain boundary in Fascicle 7. To the right of the ○關宿藩 marker sit the closing demographic columns of the previous domain, Zeze (膳所藩): status-group headcounts for lower retainers (卒族 1,787), shrine servants (社人 340), Buddhist clergy (寺侶 695), nuns (尼 17), outcaste groups (穢多 1,244; 非人 342), 110 shrines, the governor's family (3), and a "no warships held" (船艦不所持) notation, each split into male/female sub-counts that reconcile to their totals. To the left, Sekiyado's own block opens with a base kokudaka of 43,000 koku (本高) drawn from 3 districts of Shimōsa, 2 of Shimotsuke and 2 of Hitachi (131 villages, new fields included), an assessed gross yield (草高) of 52,386.28213 koku, and a regular land tax of 5,960.4342 koku of rice plus 6,775.76354 kan in eiraku cash (rice-equivalent 8,469.70443 koku). The printed page number is 211.

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 7 (Sekiyado)
pages.page_topic: Sekiyado domain miscellaneous tax (雜税) receipts
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fascicle-7 revenue return for Sekiyado domain (關宿藩) and is given over entirely to miscellaneous taxes (雜税). It opens with an "of which" breakdown carried over from the preceding page — 2,679.266 koku of rice and 283.822 kan in eiraku cash — annotated that only the fixed-assessment portion is stable and the remainder varies from year to year. A first 雜税 heading then governs four lines that the compilers flag as having been written in red ink in the original: 29.25 ryō plus 490,706 mon in petty imposts (小物成), 143.125 ryō plus 36,721 mon from timber sales (材木代), 441.125 ryō from domestic tea manufacture (國産製茶), and 212.375 ryō from licence fees (運上類). A second block, headed "the Horse-year return states" and marked as having stood in the margin of the original manuscript, gives the same category as 853.608 koku of rice, 746.625 ryō in gold, 1,341.832 kan in eiraku, and 584.508 kan in copper cash; the closing 合計 label prints here but its total carries over to the facing page.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Table (Fascicle) 7 — (Sekiyado)
pages.page_topic: Sekiyado domain — households, status populations, temples/shrines, and tax totals
pages.page_summary_en: This is a continuation leaf for Sekiyado domain (關宿藩) in fascicle 7 of the Hansei Ichiran (1870 domain survey). It records 9,605 total households; the shizoku (230 households / 1,185 persons), sotsu (324 households / 1,016 persons) and shrine-attendant (272 persons) sub-populations with male/female splits; 191 town-watchman and outcaste (eta) dwellings; and 292 temple-and-shrine buildings (38 of them prayer-halls and yamabushi residences) holding 642.3 koku of temple-shrine land. A combined regular-plus-miscellaneous tax total of 15,552.11009 koku is annotated as actual-rice tax (朱黒印 grant lands not separately distinguished), and a monetary figure of 2,146 ryō (plus ei-cash) carries over from the preceding page. The 人口 grand total (27,805 with its male/female breakdown) is NOT printed on this leaf — only the section header and the status sub-counts appear here.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 7 (Susaka)
pages.page_topic: End of Sekiyado's population tally; opening of Susaka's kokudaka
pages.page_summary_en: This page closes the fascicle-7 population return for Sekiyado Domain and opens the corresponding return for Susaka Domain. For Sekiyado it records the residual status categories — 330 Buddhist clergy (295 male, 35 female), 114 mountain ascetics (62 male, 52 female), 6 shrine mediums, 8 nuns, and 853 town-outcaste watchmen and eta (433 male, 420 female) — and closes with a total population of 49,058, against male and female components of 25,055 and 24,002 that sum to 49,057; a bracketed editorial mark printed beside the disputed digit flags the discrepancy. Three absence notations follow: no record of the governor's household, no shrine count, and no warships. To the left of the ○須坂藩 marker, Susaka opens with 13 villages and a gross assessed yield (草高) of 12,153.3708 koku, partitioned into 12,138.3708 koku of domain-administered land and 15 koku held as Kōkoku-ji temple land; a nested entry notes that 2,080.5208 koku of that total is newly reclaimed paddy added by resurvey.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle Seven (Suzaka)
pages.page_topic: Suzaka tax revenue (five-year average), households and population
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf of Fascicle 7 records Suzaka Domain's fiscal and demographic returns, all revenue figures given as a five-year average (五ヶ年平均). Land tax in rice (正租米) is 4,217.8779 koku and miscellaneous tax rice (諸税米) 6.5636 koku, summing exactly to the printed total (合) of 4,224.4415 koku; 12.6 koku of assessed land is recorded as tax-exempt (除地). On the cash side, surcharges (諸掛物永) of 70.783 kan, miscellaneous tax cash of 734.394 kan and sundry income (雜入永) of 3 kan sum exactly to the stated total of 808.177 kan, which the entry then converts to 101.0221 koku of rice (此米) at a rate of precisely 8 kan-mon per koku. The domain reports 1,518 households and a population of 11,315, of whom 5,489 are male and 5,826 female.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 7 (Suzaka)
pages.page_topic: Suzaka domain status-group households and population
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the fascicle-7 civil register for Suzaka domain (Shinano), giving household counts and paired male/female populations for each status group. Shizoku number 98 households and 431 people (213 male, 218 female); sotsuzoku 128 households and 403 people (214 male, 189 female). The religious establishment is small: 2 Shinto-priest households with 12 people, 21 Buddhist temples with 150 clergy (94 male, 56 female), and 2 Shugendō households with 4 people. The outcaste registers close the page with 43 eta households totalling 239 people (114 male, 125 female) and 7 hinin households.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 7 (Suzaka)
pages.page_topic: Suzaka: outcaste headcount, shrines, governor's household, no vessels
pages.page_summary_en: This sparse left-hand leaf closes the 須坂藩 (Suzaka) entry in fascicle 7 of the 1870 Hansei ichiran-hyō; it carries no maru-marker, so every column belongs to the domain already running from the preceding leaf, as the running header 藩制一覽表第七（須坂）confirms. Read right to left, it records a status sub-population of 44 persons (25 male, 19 female — the two components sum exactly to the printed total), 29 Shinto shrines, and a governor's household of 9 persons (2 male, 7 female, again summing to the total). The final column is the absence notation 舶ナシ, declaring that Suzaka held no vessels. The 44-person figure is far too small to be Suzaka's whole population and corresponds to the outcaste (非人) category whose heading falls on the facing page.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Iwakuni)
pages.page_topic: Iwakuni domain officials: office head-counts and roster
pages.page_summary_en: This page opens the fascicle-8 (domain officials) entry for Iwakuni Domain (岩國藩), marked by the circle-marker ○岩國藩 at the head of the block. The upper register prints four office lines: 知事 (governor) with no figure recorded, 大參事 (senior councillor) at 2 posts annotated 當時欠員 "at present vacant," 權大參事 (acting senior councillor) at 4, and 少參事 (junior councillor) at 7. The lower register prints eleven personal names in a single run — 宮莊將美, 香川景逸, 目加田喜助, 鹽谷鼎, 都野新左衞門, 今田彦馬, 藤田浪江, 三須文郎, 中村彦兵衞, 安田源三 and 大草終吉 — a count that reconciles exactly with the 4 acting senior councillors plus 7 junior councillors, the two vacant senior councillor seats supplying no names. Only one domain appears on the leaf; nothing prints to the right of the marker except the running header and the folio number 二百二十 (page 220).

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran, Fascicle 8 (Imabari)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military units (Iwakuni tail, Imabari opening)
pages.page_summary_en: This verso carries the end of the 岩國藩 (Iwakuni) entry and the opening of the 今治藩 (Imabari) entry in Fascicle 8 of the Hansei ichiran, printed book-page 221. Right of the ○今治藩 marker, Iwakuni's roster closes with three acting junior councillors (權少參事) — Kasai Jirōemon, Hara Shichiemon and Moriwaki Taizō — preceded by two further named officials, Katsura Kanzaemon and Katsura Kurōbee, whose office heading falls on the facing recto. Iwakuni's forces are recorded as two rifle battalions (銃兵二大隊) at 800 men per battalion and 50 men per company, i.e. 1,600 men, with 7 additional officers, plus one artillery battery (砲隊一砲隊) of 36 men with 11 additional officers. Left of the marker, Imabari's entry begins with its governor Hisamatsu of Junior Fifth Rank (知事 久松從五位), senior councillor Hisamatsu Osamu (大參事 久松修) and acting senior councillor Kidokoro Chikara (權大參事 城所力).

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyo, Fascicle 8 (Iiyama)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military establishment (fascicle 8)
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 222 of the Hansei Ichiran fascicle 8 (officials and troops), carrying the tail of the Imabari Domain entry and the opening of the Iiyama Domain entry. The right-hand columns, which precede the ○飯山藩 marker, complete Imabari's roster with three shōsanji (Ogawa Toshima, Taga Otoya, Ikeuchi Shigeka) and record Imabari's forces: 15 platoons of 50 men each (750 troops), of which 5 platoons are shizoku and the remainder sotsu, plus one platoon of gunners (shizoku) and one drum-and-bugle platoon (sotsu). Left of the marker, Iiyama Domain lists its governorship (chiji) as blank and staffs one daisanji, three gon-daisanji and one shōsanji — five posts matched by exactly five names, from Asano Heima through Kashiwabara Gengoemon. Iiyama's own military figures do not appear here; they continue on the following leaf.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Fascicle 8 (Inuyama)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military establishment
pages.page_summary_en: This left-hand page of fascicle 8 carries the close of Iiyama Domain's entry and the opening of Inuyama Domain's. To the right of the ○犬山藩 marker, Iiyama's official roster ends with two acting junior councillors (權少參事 二人), named below as Honda Kozaemon and Ishihara Misao, followed by an editorial note that the names above are not recorded, and then Iiyama's military establishment: a rifle corps of six platoons, two cannon, and 165 troops including officers. Left of the marker, Inuyama's entry begins: the governorship is recorded with the name lacking (名欠), with one senior councillor (Takada Tsutomu) and four acting senior councillors, of whom Chiba Takeshi and Koike Masato are named, plus two Kōgisho delegates, Honda Hikosaburō and Yoshida Shū. Inuyama's junior councillors and its own military (six platoons, 324 troops) continue on the following page.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Izushi)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and troop strength (fascicle 8)
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 224 of the lower volume closes out the fascicle-8 entry for Inuyama Domain (犬山藩) and then opens the entry for Izushi Domain (出石藩). Inuyama's official roster is completed here with 少参事 4 persons — a figure the 1928 editors flag 〔sic〕 because five names stand beneath it (神谷辛歲, 小林守男, 横井恰, 山田莊平, 八木銀次郎) — and 権少参事 5 persons (水野鎬, 平尾義造, 高田大次郎, 小川渉, 水谷眞須美); two of the shōsanji, Yokoi and Yamada, carry the small side-annotation 公用人兼, "concurrently kōyōnin." Inuyama's military follows in the fascicle-8 pattern of printing troops after officials: six platoons with a stated strength of 324 men at 48 men per platoon, so the six platoon complements account for 288 and the remaining 36 are officers and staff. The leftmost column carries only the maru-marker ○出石藩; Izushi's own figures begin on the facing page 225.

pages.page_header_en: Han-sei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 8 (Izushi)
pages.page_topic: Izushi domain officials and samurai corps
pages.page_summary_en: A fascicle-8 officials-and-military page for Izushi Domain (出石藩, Tajima, Sengoku house). Read right to left, it gives the governor Sengoku Masakata (Junior Fifth Rank, Fujiwara) and the councillor establishment: one Senior Councillor, four Provisional Senior Councillors, six Junior Councillors with one post vacant, and one Provisional Junior Councillor. A lower register prints the eleven incumbents by name — Araki Hitoshi; Kanazawa Makoto, Asami Yoshinaga, Hotta Tomochika, Sakurai Kumaichi; Ogawa Etsutarō, Nagaoka Shizumu, Shimamura Kōhei, Nishiyama Midori, Nishikawa Tomijirō; and Tanino Tō — a count that reconciles exactly with 1 + 4 + (6 − 1) + 1. The leftmost data column records the domain's samurai corps at three platoons of forty men, i.e. 120 troops.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覧表第八（岩邨、一關）
pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 8 (Iwamura, Ichinoseki)
pages.page_topic: domain officials and troop strength
pages.page_summary_en: Fascicle 8 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran, printed page 226, records the post-restoration official establishment and troop strength of Iwamura Domain (Mino) and the opening of Ichinoseki Domain (Mutsu). Iwamura reports 1 governor (chiji), 1 senior councillor (daisanji), 3 acting senior councillors, 4 junior councillors and 13 acting junior councillors, with a standing force of 3 platoons totalling 180 men; the governor's name is marked "name omitted" (名欠) and each subsequent post dittos that absence. Ichinoseki, whose marker opens at the left of the sheet, reports 1 governor (name not recorded), 2 senior councillors, 1 acting senior councillor with an editorial variant note that one account gives three, and 3 junior councillors. A trailing entry at the far right, "sotsutai, 2 platoons," stands to the right of the Iwamura marker and therefore carries over from the preceding domain's military return rather than belonging to Iwamura.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Ichinoseki)
pages.page_topic: Ichinoseki military officer ranks (fascicle 8, continued)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues Ichinoseki Domain's fascicle-8 military return, listing twelve officer posts with their establishment strengths and opening with the entry for troop numbers (兵隊數), which is marked 記セス — not recorded. The posts run from the overall commander (總兵長, 1) through the gunners' chief, artillery, transport, ordnance and inspectorate (銃士長 1, 砲隊長 1, 輜重長 1, 兵器長 1, 軍監 2) to the rifle-infantry and sapper line (銃卒長 2, 銃士次長 1, 坑兵長 1, 銃卒次長 2, 銃士小長 4) and the reserve command (豫備長 1), eighteen men in all on this page. An editorial parenthesis opened above 總兵長 carries the note （以下三十八行原朱書）, recording that the following thirty-eight lines were written in vermilion in the original manuscript; only twelve of those lines fall on this leaf, so the roster and the vermilion span both continue overleaf. The printed page number in the bottom margin is 二百二十七 (227).

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Ichinoseki)
pages.page_topic: Ichinoseki military establishment: corps and specialist headcounts
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the fascicle-8 military establishment of Ichinoseki Domain, listing thirteen offices and corps with their authorized complements in 員 (persons). The largest body is the riflemen (銃士) at 60, commanded by eight junior rifle-corps officers (銃卒小長) and two reserve rifle-corps commanders (豫備銃卒長); the artillery (砲士) numbers 6 and the scouts (斥候士) 6, with three baggage-train officers (輜重長校) and three ordnance officers (兵器管事). Support and specialist posts are small — one bandmaster (樂手長), two band physicians (樂手醫師), two clerks (筆生), and two junior army inspectors (小軍監). The two garrison categories are exceptional: the reserve-grade residence-and-fort guards (散級館砦衞士) are explicitly recorded as 無定員, having no fixed complement, while the active-grade guards (勤級館砦衞士) are printed with no number at all.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran, Table (Fascicle) Eight — Ichinoseki
pages.page_topic: Ichinoseki military establishment — troop and officer headcounts
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf continues the Ichinoseki (一關藩) military return in fascicle 8 of the Hansei Ichiran; there is no domain marker on the page, so all thirteen entries belong to Ichinoseki, the domain named in the running header. Read right to left, the page lists establishment strengths for baggage-train sub-officers (2), sapper deputy commanders (2), patrolmen (6, provisionally established), samurai-company standard-bearers (2, provisionally established), artillery-company standard-bearers (2), sotsu-company standard-bearers (4), riflemen (120), sappers (32), bandsmen together with baggage-train junior officers (2 shared under one brace), ordnance junior officers (4), sapper junior officers (2), and one orderly. Reserve troops (豫備卒) are recorded as 無定員 — no fixed establishment. The riflemen and sappers dominate the page: the twelve defined categories total 179 men, of which 120 are riflemen. The printed page number is 二百二十九 (229).

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle Eight (Iwasaki)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and armed strength
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf is the fascicle-8 entry for Iwasaki Domain (岩崎藩), a small Satake cadet holding in Dewa, and covers the domain's administrative roster and its armed strength. The governor is recorded only as Satake, Junior Fifth Rank (佐竹從五位); the given names of the senior administrators are explicitly not recorded (名記セス, with 同 "ditto" carried down the remaining posts). Below the governor sit one senior councillor (大參事), two acting senior councillors (權大參事) and three junior councillors (少參事) — seven senior administrators in all. Military strength is given as 48 soldiers (兵士四十八人) and 40 riflemen (銃卒四十人), while the organisation of the troops into units is noted as unrecorded (兵隊記セス). Two functional offices are printed as raised headings without counts of their own: the drill office (練兵方), staffed by a head instructor and one instructor and one associate instructor each, and the guard office (衛兵方), with a single watch-company commander.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Iwatsuki)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials: posts, establishment counts, and named officeholders
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf opens the fascicle-8 officials entry for Iwatsuki Domain (Musashi), marked by the circle-marker ○岩槻藩 with the note that the return was compiled in the Snake year (Meiji 2 / 1869). The three columns printed to the right of that marker are not Iwatsuki's: they are the tail of the preceding domain's military roster — 銃卒隊長 2, 番組司令 2, 銃卒五長 3 — overflowing past the next domain's marker, and MASTER assigns them to Iwasaki Domain. Iwatsuki's own establishment is given as governor (知事) 1, senior counsellor (大参事) 1, acting senior counsellor (権大参事) 2, junior counsellor (小参事) 2, and acting junior counsellor (権少参事) 4, for ten posts in all. The lower register names the holders: governor Ōoka Tadatsura, Junior Fifth Rank, followed by Fujisaki Yutaka, Aoki Ataeru, Nakakuki Yanagi, Kodama Sōgo, Murase Tamaki, Tomita Yoshi, Takagi Tōichi and Yamazaki Hachirōji — nine of the ten, the fourth acting junior counsellor continuing on the next page. Printed book page 231.

pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Administration, Table Eight (Iino)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and troop strength
pages.page_summary_en: A fascicle-8 leaf (printed page 232) whose single maru-marker, ○飯野藩, sits well to the left, so most of the sheet still belongs to the preceding domain, Iwatsuki. The right-hand two-thirds carry Iwatsuki's second, Sheep-year (未ノ年, Meiji 4/1871) return: governor "same as before", 2 senior councillors (大參事) and 1 junior councillor (小參事), named as Nakakuki Nobuchō, Takagi Kiyoatsu and Takahashi Shigemasa, with a tenth official from the domain's earlier Snake-year roster (上都準) overflowing from page 231. Iwatsuki's military follows: overall troop numbers are "not recorded" (兵隊 記セス), but companies 1-3 muster 120 men and companies 4-6, the rifle-conscript companies, another 120, with a further 28 from company commander down to the squad commanders — 268 men in all. Left of the marker, Iino Domain's own entry opens with a governor (no member count printed) and 2 senior councillors, continuing onto page 233.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 8 (Iida)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and troop strength (fascicle 8)
pages.page_summary_en: Printed leaf 233 of fascicle 8 of the Hansei ichiran-hyō, carrying the tail of Iino Domain's entry and the opening of Iida Domain's. The right-hand columns, printed before the ○飯田藩 marker, complete Iino's officer roster — 3 gon-daisanji, 1 shōsanji, 5 gon-shōsanji — and record its only military figure, two platoons of Dutch-style riflemen at 46 men per platoon (92 men) as of the fifth month of 1870, with a supplementary note giving a unit strength of 66 men; the entry closes 右庚午四月ノ調, "the foregoing is the survey of the fourth month of 1870." Left of the marker, Iida Domain's entry opens with the governorship recorded but unnamed, 3 daisanji and 3 gon-daisanji, and a lower name register listing Ishizawa Kingo, Okazawa Hitoshi, Yasutomi Minsō and Nakayama Shitomi. Iida's remaining officers (4 shōsanji and the gon-shōsanji) continue on the following leaf, page 234.

pages.page_header_en: Domain Survey Table, Fascicle 8 (Iida section) — running header (provenance)
pages.page_topic: Iida domain officials — shōsanji and gonshōsanji rosters
pages.page_summary_en: This page continues the Fascicle 8 (officials) entry for Iida domain in Shinano. It is laid out in two registers: office titles set at the top of their columns, and the corresponding rosters set bottom-flush in the same and successive columns to the left. Two rank headings appear — 小參事, given as 四員 (four officers), and 權少參事, for which no numerical count is printed. Thirteen personal names are recorded in all: the two rightmost columns (羽生孫九郎, 小林直) complete the roster of the senior rank headed on the preceding page; the next four (田總九郎兵衞, 齋藤愼吾, 松岡七郎, 杉本傳) exactly fill the four 小參事 posts; and the remaining seven (杉本愿藏, 一色英馬, 鍋木堅藏, 渡邊八郎, 石田平右衞門, 西尾爲右衞門, 中山安太郎) are the 權少參事. No domain-boundary marker occurs on the sheet, so the whole page belongs to Iida; the printed book-page number is 234.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第八（磐城平）
pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Iwakitaira)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials roster (Iwakitaira), with Iida troop total overflowing at right
pages.page_summary_en: Fascicle 8 of the 1870 Hansei ichiran records domain office-holders. The ○磐城平藩 marker opens Iwakitaira Domain's roster, which lists nine posts in a two-register layout: Governor (知事) Andō, holder of Junior Fifth Rank; Senior Councillors (大參事) Yashiro Makoto and Murakami Hajime; Provisional Senior Councillors (權大參事) Kamoshita Nakaji and a second Murakami Hajime; Muro Naoshi, annotated as the domain's representative to the Kōgisho (公議人); and three Junior Councillors (少參事), Ajioka Seiichi, Murakami Hisashi and Matsuura Kyūnai. Three columns printed to the right of the marker — the names Ichinose Kanbee and Takahara Shichibee, and a troop strength of 兵隊 貳百八十三員 (283 men) — belong to the preceding domain, Iida, whose roster began on the facing page. The printed page number is 235.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 8 (Ikusaka)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military strength (fascicle 8)
pages.page_summary_en: A fascicle-8 boundary leaf: the right two-thirds close out Iwakitaira domain (磐城平藩) and the left third opens Ikusaka domain (生坂藩) at the maru-marker ○生坂藩. For Iwakitaira the page lists five acting junior councillors of the first and second grades (一二權少參事) — Nonoyama Noboru, Murakami Hisashi, Urushibara Ugenta, Matsuura Kyūnai, and Nakamura Mohei — followed by the domain's troop strength: 20 standing samurai-rank soldiers and 20 standing rank-and-file, plus 18 reserve soldiers and 12 reserve rank-and-file, 70 men in all. Ikusaka's entry begins with its three senior officers: Governor Ikeda Masanori (知事 池田政禮), Senior Councillor Miyake Kei (大參事 三宅敬), and Acting Senior Councillor Takao Takenobu (權大參事 高尾武信). The leaf carries the printed book page 236.

pages.page_header_en: Hansei ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 8 (Ishioka)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military establishment
pages.page_summary_en: Fascicle 8 (officials and military) of the 1870 Hansei ichiran, printed book page 237. The right-hand columns close out the preceding domain, Ikusaka (生坂藩), with two named officials — Kisabe Takanobu, holding the same post as the entry carried over from the facing page, and Junior Councillor (少參事) Habara Takamasa — followed by its military return, which records the troop total as 不詳 ("not ascertained") and enumerates only officer posts: one inspector-of-troops (監軍), one platoon commander (小隊長), and one half-platoon commander (半隊長). The maru-marker ○石岡藩 then opens the block for Ishioka Domain (Hitachi, ~20,000 koku), whose administrative establishment is given by headcount: three Senior Councillors (大參事), four Acting Senior Councillors (權大參事), three Junior Councillors (小參事), two Acting Junior Councillors (權小參事), and two clerks (役司). Its forces comprise two rifle platoons of 68 men each (136 riflemen) plus twelve artillerymen (礮手), with a small variant note, 一ニ曰ク ("one account states"), giving an alternative return of four platoons totalling 200 men at 52 per platoon.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第八（今尾、伊勢崎）
pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 8 (Imao, Isesaki)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and military units (fascicle 8)
pages.page_summary_en: This is the fascicle-8 (officials and military) opening page for Imao domain (今尾藩), a small Owari cadet house in Mino. A dating note at the head of the block records that the earlier returns were surveyed on 1870/6/19 (kanoe-uma, 6th month, 19th day) while the later returns carry no stated year or month. Imao's councillor block prints five standing rank headings — 知事, 大参事, 権大参事, 小参事, 権少参事 — of which only 大参事 and 権大参事 carry names: 奧田忠 and 高野瀨和人 under 大参事, 小串右門 and 奧田又十郎 under 権大参事. The domain also reports 66 men in outside-duty offices (外役司) and six musketeer platoons (銃兵 六小隊) at a stated 50 men per platoon, i.e. 300 men. The Isesaki (伊勢崎藩) marker opens at the left edge of the page with only its 知事 heading; Isesaki's own councillors and troops continue on the facing left page (printed p. 239).

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第八（伊勢崎）
pages.page_header_en: Survey of Domain Institutions, Fascicle 8 (Isesaki)
pages.page_topic: Isesaki domain officials roster and military strength
pages.page_summary_en: Printed page 239 continues the fascicle-8 entry for Isesaki domain, whose ○伊勢崎藩 marker and blank 知事 line stand at the end of the facing page 238. The leaf records two overlapping registers of domain officials: a first listing 大參事 Ishihara Masumi and Nagao Okujirō with three 小參事 (Tomioka Hajime, Nagaya Yasujirō, Igarashi Rai), and a second listing a 一二大參事 Nakamura Jinbee, 權大參事 Ishihara Masumi and Suzuki Nobori, and 少參事 Kawada Tōzō and Hōnoki Jihei — the duplication of Ishihara and the alternation of 小參事/少參事 reflecting the two-submission note printed at the head of the section. Military strength is given as 兵士隊 two platoons at forty men each (80 samurai troops), 卒隊 one platoon on the same establishment (40 foot troops), and 大砲 two cannon, for roughly 120 men under arms. The page carries no maru-marker of its own; the running header names Isesaki as provenance.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第八（一宮、泉）
pages.page_header_en: Hansei Ichiran-hyō, Fascicle 8 (Ichinomiya, Izumi)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials and troop complements (fascicle 8)
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf of fascicle 8 records the administrative establishment and troop strength of Ichinomiya domain (Kazusa) and opens the entry for Izumi domain (Iwaki). Ichinomiya's authorized complements are two senior councillors (daisanji), four acting senior councillors (gon-daisanji), seven junior councillors (shōsanji) and nine acting junior councillors (gon-shōsanji); the warichu notes attached to the two senior grades explain that the domain's kōgi-nin (public-assembly delegate) is drawn from those ranks, raising the effective totals to three and five respectively. Its forces number 33 heishi (samurai-rank soldiers) and 47 heisotsu (rank-and-file), the latter annotated as the Seiyū-tai. No governor's name is printed for Ichinomiya, whereas Izumi's governor is given as Honda no Fujiwara Tadanobu. Three acting junior councillors of the preceding domain, Isesaki — Tomioka Shinpachi, Nagaya Yasujirō and Igarashi Kitaru — overflow into the right margin of this page.

pages.page_header_kanji: 藩制一覽表第八（岩村田）
pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview, Fascicle 8 (Iwamurata)
pages.page_topic: Domain officials rosters and standing/reserve troop counts
pages.page_summary_en: A fascicle-8 leaf carrying the tail of Izumi Domain's entry and the opening of Iwamurata Domain's. Right of the ○岩村田藩 marker, Izumi's officials are listed under three office headings — 大参事 (Kuwabara Fujiwara Shigenobu and Hirano Fujiwara Rensuke), 権大参事 (Kitagō Taira Yasusada), and 小参事 (Kameda Tachibana Akira, Takigawa Ōtomo Kazumasa, and Yamauchi Fujiwara Yamahiko) — followed by Izumi's military strength: 30 standing troops (常備兵) and 30 reserve troops (豫備兵), 60 men in all. Left of the marker, Iwamurata's roster begins: the 知事 (governor) heading is printed with no incumbent name beneath it, then 大参事 Takahashi Tōta Norimichi, 権大参事 Uehara Sakunoshin Satotsugu, and 少参事 Inoue Ryōzō Yasuchika. Iwamurata's own troop figures do not appear on this leaf. The printed page number in the bottom margin is 241.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 8 (Hasunoike)
pages.page_topic: Fascicle 8 officials roster — Hasunoike domain
pages.page_summary_en: This is the opening page of Hasunoike domain's Fascicle 8 entry, the survey's roster of domain officers. It names the governor Nabeshima Naonori (Junior Sixth Rank), one senior councillor pair (Naritomi Seiki and Ishii Kyūma), one provisional-senior pair (Naritomi Shin and Ōno Kanae), and a junior-councillor group of six — Tsuruta Seizō, Nagata Yūsuke (flagged 公議人, the domain's delegate to the public assembly), Shibayama Daizō, Tsuruta Bungo, Kagiama Shōgo and Kawazoe Ikuta / Nagasaki Shūzō. Two editorial notes survive in small type: one records that a variant copy writes Shibayama's name as 代之進, the other that Nagasaki Shūzō does not appear in the caretaker-office register (留守官書ニナシ). The right-hand quarter of the page still belongs to the preceding domain, Iwamurata: its four provisional junior councillors and its military line, 兵隊 二小隊 = 43 shizoku plus 51 sotsu, 94 men in two platoons.

pages.page_header_en: Table of Domain Administration, Fascicle 8 (Hanabusa)
pages.page_topic: Domain councillor posts and rifle units
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf of fascicle 8 of the 1870 Hansei Ichiran carries the tail of the 蓮池藩 (Hasunoike, a Saga sub-domain) entry and the opening of the ○花房藩 (Hanabusa, Kazusa) entry. Right of the marker, Hasunoike's provisional junior councillors (權少參事) are named — 副島哲藏, 栗山英二, 尾形榮二郎, 鵜田禮作 — followed by its rifle forces: 銃士 one platoon and 銃卒 four platoons, with a printed note that a platoon is a unit of forty men, giving 160 rifle foot-soldiers. Left of the marker, Hanabusa lists 知事 (governor, heading only), 大參事 at one post with a small-type note that regular and provisional councillors together put three men on duty per day, and 權大參事 at five posts. Four councillor names print for Hanabusa: 西尾鐵之助, 佐藤武彦, 清水源次郎, 柴田源三. The running header names 花房 and the leaf is printed page 243.

pages.page_header_en: Han Institutions Overview, Fascicle Eight (Hachinohe)
pages.page_topic: Domain conciliar officials and troop companies
pages.page_summary_en: This leaf of Fascicle 8 closes the Hanabusa domain entry and opens Hachinohe. Hanabusa's material, all standing to the right of the maru-marker, consists of four carried-over acting-junior-councillor names (Yamada Hyakuzō, Tsuchiya Matahachi, Aoyama Kanji, Hiratomi Tanomo) followed by its military return: two platoons of samurai troops and one platoon of sotsu troops, with a single note fixing company strength at sixty men — 120 and 60 men respectively. Left of the ○八戸藩 marker, Hachinohe reports a twelve-man conciliar establishment: one senior councillor, two acting senior councillors, three junior councillors and six acting junior councillors. Hachinohe's roster is given by surname alone, the column under 大參事 carrying the interlinear disclaimer 名欠 以下同 ("given name lacking; the same below"), and the acting-junior-councillor list reconciles as four surnames plus 二員缺, two vacant posts, against the printed establishment of six.
